summary: Learner reviews math + physics: I reviewed all four lessons as a simulated adult beginner (school arithmetic and everyday life, no study of t…
body:
I reviewed all four lessons as a simulated adult beginner (school arithmetic and everyday life, no study of the topic). Each review was finished before I started the next. I read the transcript and screenshots first, then drove the live lesson in Playwright. I read meta.json only after section 1 was written.

| Lesson | Verdict | Top finding |
|---|---|---|
| odd-numbers-make-squares | fatal | "Show me why" unlocks after one "+ 3" tap. That shows a 2×2, which the question already stated. The reveal then says "Every odd number you added landed as an L" and "the totals cannot miss." The walkthrough bounced between 1 and 2 and still reached the reveal. The prediction also hands over the answer through two worked examples and the title. |
| exponential-growth | revise | The reveal unlocks after one step back, at day 29 (50%), so a learner never has to see day 25. Someone who guessed "about half" is partly confirmed by day 29. "Hides, then arrives at once" is only a sentence in the reveal. No dead controls or false statements found. |
| pendulum-period | fatal | Moving the weight slider alone unlocks the reveal without pressing Release. I confirmed this in my own run, and the walkthrough did it in its first step. The walkthrough then changed weight and string together and only ever watched "out of step with the ghost." That looks like the opposite of the reveal's "every weight stayed locked." |
| projectile-angle | fatal | The reveal unlocks after one launch at any angle. The walkthrough only launched 35°, 50° and 65° (slider starts at 20° in 5° steps). It never saw the 30°/60° pair, yet the reveal states they land together at 35.3 m. When I did launch 30° then 60°, the display worked very well: two arcs ending at the same dot with the caption "same landing spot." |

**Files written** (each opens with the "Simulated learner" label, has sections 1 and 2, and ends with a verdict line):
- `/home/user/system-3-company/company/reviews/odd-numbers-make-squares/2026-10-12-learner-adult-beginner.md`
- `/home/user/system-3-company/company/reviews/exponential-growth/2026-10-12-learner-adult-beginner.md`
- `/home/user/system-3-company/company/reviews/pendulum-period/2026-10-12-learner-adult-beginner.md`
- `/home/user/system-3-company/company/reviews/projectile-angle/2026-10-12-learner-adult-beginner.md`

I added each review path to `evidence.simulatedLearner` in that lesson's meta.json. Before each edit I re-read the file. I changed only that array, using an exact-string replace.

**What I believe and how sure I am:**
- **Same root cause:** In three lessons, the reveal gate opens on a trivial action, not on seeing the key comparison. I replicated it myself in all three, so I'm fairly confident (about 85%).
- **Strongest case:** The pendulum one is the clearest, because it opens with no swing at all.
- **Prediction quality:** Exponential-growth, pendulum and projectile ask real guess questions. Odd-numbers gives its answer away.
- **Clean pieces to keep:** The 30°/60° same-landing display, the 1/1,073,741,824 day-0 marker, and the ghost pendulum are good once the learner reaches them.
- **Limit:** This is a simulated beginner, so it finds problems and says nothing about whether anyone learned.

**Next move, owned by demo-builder:** Gate "Show me why" on the key observation. Candidates are the 30° and 60° launches both done, a pendulum released with only weight changed, and the odd-number steps taken to some minimum. Also revisit the exponential-growth and odd-numbers prediction design, which sits with the learning-designer. I did not add board items or a progress.md handoff, since my task did not ask for them.

**Environment notes:**
- Another process had rebuilt `.next` while I worked, so my first `next start` on port 3501 failed. It worked after a retry.
- I ran `pkill -n next-server` at cleanup. A separate server on port 3504 was still running afterward, so I don't believe I killed anything that wasn't mine.

summary: Fact-check cs + chemistry: All four lessons are fact-checked and the merge-sort-payoff second check is done. No claim is disputed, so no…
body:
All four lessons are fact-checked and the merge-sort-payoff second check is done. No claim is disputed, so nothing blocks on accuracy. The cited sources (Knuth, Krane, IUPAC, USGS, FDA, Nature, NUBASE2020) could not be opened because the egress proxy blocked them. Verdicts rest on my own node scripts and on secondary corroboration from search results.

| Lesson | Verified | Disputed | Added unverified | Fixes needed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| binary-search | 4 (c1–c4) | 0 | 2 (c5, c6) | 1 optional wording note (F1) |
| binary-numbers | 5 (c1–c5) | 0 | 1 (c6) | none |
| half-life | 5 (c1–c5) | 0 | 2 (c6, c7) | F1 (important), F2, F3 (optional) |
| ph-log-scale | 6 (c1–c6) | 0 | 1 (c7) | F1, F2, F3 (optional) |
| merge-sort-payoff second check | 5 (c4–c8) | 0 | 0 | 1 wording fix (F4) |

`npm run check` passes: 18 lessons, 152 claims. Its only warning is the existing disputed claim in herd-immunity, which is not one of these lessons.

**Unrecorded claims I added.** They are `unverified`, so another checker has to verify them.
- **binary-search c5:** a middle guess rules out at least half of what is left.
- **binary-search c6:** 2,000 sorted names need at most 11 checks (recall card).
- **binary-numbers c6:** +1 from 127 flips all 8 switches, and +1 from 255 wraps to 0.
- **half-life c6:** a new run keeps different survivors.
- **half-life c7:** "Each half-life, roughly half of whatever was left decays, even the long survivors."
- **ph-log-scale c7:** coffee at about pH 5 versus lemon juice at about pH 2 gives about 1,000 times the hydrogen ions.

**Fixes routed to demo-builder.**
- **half-life F1 (important):** The lesson allows 8 waits. In my 2,000-run simulation, by the 6th, 7th and 8th wait 35%, 51% and 67% of runs show a decayed share below 33% or above 67%. It is often exactly 0% or 100%. That reads like "overdue" under a reveal that says "roughly half". The 4th wait the explore hint asks for is fine: 91% of runs fall within 33–67%.
- **ph-log-scale F1:** The predict question reads as a fact about real coffee and lemon juice. The lesson's own cited ranges give a ratio of about 180 to about 1,350, so "about 1,000" holds only for pH exactly 5 and 2. Make clear the 1,000 follows from the round values.
- **ph-log-scale F2:** The hook's "How much more acid" is ambiguous. The lesson answers in hydrogen ions, and total (titratable) acid is a different quantity. I did not quantify it.
- **merge-sort F4:** The hook says splitting "isn't" extra work, but the verified claim is only that splitting costs no comparisons.
- **half-life F2:** "halves to a quarter, an eighth" reads oddly.
- **binary-search F1 (optional):** "rules out half" would be literally true as "at least half". 
- **Citations:** Confirm the Krane section and the NUBASE2020 entry (half-life), and the USGS/IUPAC pages (ph-log-scale). For merge-sort, the first checker's open F1 (c2's derivation versus the bottom-up reveal) still stands; I did not reopen it.

**merge-sort-payoff c4–c8.** I wrote my own script and used the lesson's own `deal()` generator. All five are verified.
- **c4:** The maximum over all 70 splits of 8 is 7. Seven is also exact for any merging method, because ceil(log2 70) = 7.
- **c5:** Holds over all 256 splits, and the stage code adds nothing to the counter after a pile empties.
- **c6:** The maximum is 9 for every split from 1+9 to 5+5.
- **c7:** Verified as worded, in comparisons only.
- **c8:** Convention (a one-card list is sorted by definition).

I appended the section "Second check of c4–c8" to the existing review file.

**Confidence.** High on all the arithmetic and simulation results. Medium on the unopened source citations. The claims themselves are standard and several were corroborated by search. The Rao & Fuller coffee range of 4.85–5.13 and Godwin's 5730 ± 40 years for carbon-14 were confirmed. The FDA lemon-juice range of 2.00–2.60 was confirmed from two secondary tables, not the FDA page.

**Next move.** Demo-builder takes the routed fixes. A fact-checker other than me should verify the six claims I added. I made no progress.md handoff entry, because I was told to edit nothing outside meta.json and the review files.

body:
Geography now has 33 concepts (28 added, all 5 original ids unchanged), and the 22 ranked briefs are written. `node tools/company.mjs check` passes: 18 lessons, 152 claims, 1 warning, which is the herd-immunity disputed claim and not mine. I did not run the lesson builds or QA.

Files edited (the briefs directory did not exist, so I created it):
- /home/user/system-3-company/content/curriculum/geography.json
- /home/user/system-3-company/company/domains/briefs/geography.md

**Curriculum:** 16 of the 33 concepts are intro. The one cross-domain prerequisite is `physics:inverse-square` (on `tides-moon`), which exists in physics.json. Every other prerequisite is a geography id. Ten concepts have no brief this cycle: `map-centre-choice`, `projection-families`, `gnomonic-great-circles`, `distance-from-a-point`, `daylight-by-latitude`, `sun-path-sky`, `climate-zones`, `coriolis-effect`, `ocean-gyres`, `river-watersheds`.

**Briefs:** 18 of the 22 use WorldMap or the geo kit; 5 are marked [exploration] (briefs 4, 19, 20, 21, 22). All slugs are unique and none is used in src/demos. Answer letters are mixed, and each prediction has a one-line check. I computed the checks against the kit's own 1:110m data where that applied.

Top 5:
1. `shortest-way-to-tokyo`: the New York to Tokyo great circle is 10,875 km and peaks at 69.8 N over northern Alaska. The straight Mercator line is 12,818 km, 18% longer.
2. `closer-in-winter`: Earth is closest to the Sun in early January (147.1 vs 152.1 million km), so distance does not cause the seasons.
3. `null-island-lat-lon`: coordinates (0, 0) are open ocean in the Gulf of Guinea, about 625 km from the Ghana coast.
4. `coastline-ruler` [exploration]: a divider walk on the Great Britain outline measures about 2,385 km at 200 km, rising to about 3,002 km at 50 km.
5. `half-of-humanity`: 7 countries make up 51.4% of the world's population (UN WPP 2024); 6 reach only 48.8%.

**Unsure about:**
- **Unsourced figures:** the Chimborazo vs Everest distance from Earth's centre, the Bullard 1965 pole values (44 N, 30.6 W, 57 degrees), and the PIRATA buoy at (0, 0) come from memory. The briefs flag them to be dropped if a fact-checker cannot source them. The Bullard rotation direction I did test numerically on the 1:110m shapes.
- **Data resolution:** the coastline lengths in brief 4 are floors that flatten out below about 25 km because the 1:110m data runs out of detail. The antipode and land-hemisphere shares (13% of land has land opposite, vs a published ~15%; best hemisphere 47% land) depend on resolution. The briefs say "about" for both.
- **Brief 12 (date line):** the 50-hour claim relies on the real UTC-12 to UTC+14 spread. The map bands it uses are nominal 15-degree bands, not legal zones, and the brief says so.
- **Brief 7 (China time zone):** it claims only the official UTC+8 standard time and the solar-noon arithmetic. It makes no claim about Xinjiang or borders.
- **Brief 5 (half of humanity):** the population figures are from memory of the UN table. The margin is 1.4 points over half, so a fact-checker should confirm them.
- **Missing kit data:** rivers, climate, and ocean currents need data the geo kit doesn't ship. I left those concepts unbriefed and noted it in the briefs file.
- **Handoff entry:** I did not add a handoff entry to company/ops/progress.md, because you restricted me to the two files.

summary: Fact-check probability + life: Fact-check of birthday-paradox, base-rates, herd-immunity and natural-selection is done. One claim is dispute…
body:
Fact-check of birthday-paradox, base-rates, herd-immunity and natural-selection is done. One claim is disputed (herd-immunity c5). Every other recorded claim is verified, and I added 11 unrecorded claims as unverified. `npm run check` passes with one warning, which is the disputed claim.

| Lesson | Verified | Disputed | Added unverified | Fixes needed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| birthday-paradox | 8 (c1-c8) | 0 | 3 (c9-c11) | 3 |
| base-rates | 6 (c1-c6) | 0 | 2 (c7-c8) | 2, both optional |
| herd-immunity | 7 | 1 (c5) | 3 (c9-c11) | 4 |
| natural-selection | 7 (c1-c7) | 0 | 3 (c8-c10) | 4 |

**Disputed: herd-immunity c5.** It says that below the threshold, an outbreak that takes off "reaches a large share of the unprotected".
- That is false near the threshold. The final-size equation gives 7.6% at Reff 1.04 and 31% at Reff 1.2. My simulation of the stage model gives 34% of the unprotected at 70% immune.
- It holds well below the threshold (about 80% at 50% immune).
- c5 appears only on the "Why trust this?" sheet, not in the stage or reveal text. It still blocks publishing until demo-builder rewords it and another checker re-verifies.

**Recomputed results**
- **Birthday:**
  - Exact chances are 47.57% at 22, 50.73% at 23, 70.63% at 30, 97.04% at 50 and 99.92% at 70.
  - 23 is the smallest group above 50%, and 1 − (364/365)^22 is 5.86%.
  - I copied the demo's generator and ran 200,000 rooms. The shares match the exact chances within 0.0007.
  - The 12 of 21 in the transcript reproduces.
- **Base rates:**
  - A positive means 9.02%, 50.0% and 91.7% at 1 in 1,000, 1 in 100 and 1 in 10.
  - The stage's rounded counts are consistent with the transcript (99 of 108 positives sick at 1 in 10).
  - The right answer to the Harvard question is 1.96%.
- **Herd immunity:**
  - The lesson's own seeds give a mean of 4.2 of 80 at 80% immune and 145.9 of 200 at 50%.
  - 20,000 independent runs give 3.9 and 145.4.
  - A clustered population stays outbreak-prone at 90% immune.
- **Natural selection:**
  - 99.29% dark at generation 100, under 10% through generation 25, and over half at generation 49.
  - The 1% edge reaches 2.66%.
  - A Wright-Fisher run fixed a new copy in 18% of runs, against Haldane's 20% (2s).

**Sources I could not open** (all noted in the review files)
- **Feller, Anderson & May, Diekmann, CDC, Gillespie, Hartl & Clark, Majerus:** not opened. Those verdicts rest on my own working or general knowledge.
- **Bloom (1973) and Munford (1977):** I confirmed only the citations, not the notes. The result they are cited for, that unevenness only raises the chance, is backed by my own Monte Carlo.
- **Casscells 1978 and the peppered moth figures (Manchester 1848, 98% by 1895):** confirmed only through secondary sources.
- **Casscells figures:** 60 participants, 27 answered 95%, 11 correct.
- **Cook 2003:** not opened.

**Unrecorded claims added** (I wrote these, so someone else must verify them)
- **Birthday:**
  - c9 "far more than most people guess" has no source.
  - c10 "pairs grow by the whole room".
  - c11 "the trap is asking about my birthday" is a psychology claim with no source.
- **Base rates:** c7 "99% accurate describes the test", and c8 the recall card's 1-in-10,000 numbers.
- **Herd immunity:**
  - c9 "the immune shield the unprotected" is only partial: 3.3% of runs at 80% still take off.
  - c10 "each step is smaller".
  - c11 the recall card (R0 = 5, 80%).
- **Natural selection:**
  - c8 "1.1^100 is about 14,000" (13,781).
  - c9 "needs time, not a big edge" (a 1% edge needs 462 generations).
  - c10 the recall card.

**Fixes for demo-builder**
- **Birthday:**
  - The reveal sets the learner's tally (e.g. 21 rooms of 29) beside the 50.7% for 23 people. The room sizes differ, so it reads as a test of the 50.7%.
  - c9 and c11 state facts about people with no source.
  - The Feller section number is unchecked.
- **Base rates:**
  - The Harvard "right answer 2%" assumes the test catches every case, and the reveal does not say so (optional).
  - c6's source line should carry the 27-of-60 and 11-of-60 counts once the NEJM paper is opened.
- **Herd immunity:**
  - c5 needs rewording.
  - The "Typical" readout and the reveal's "typically about 4" report a mean. The median is 2 at 80%, and at 60% the mean of 80 of 160 is not a typical run.
  - c8 says the disease is "made up" and that real vaccines are imperfect, but neither sentence is on the stage or in the reveal.
  - "Shield... at all" should say "mostly".
- **Natural selection:**
  - c4's source line has an arithmetic slip: it prints 0.0274 and 0.027, the correct values are 0.0273 and 0.0266. "About 3%" still holds.
  - c5 cites Futuyma & Kirkpatrick "ch. 12", which one table-of-contents listing suggests is a different chapter.
  - The peppered moth paragraph sits beside the 10% edge, but the moth's implied edge is about 20% per generation. Nothing in it is false.
  - c1 should state non-overlapping generations.

**Confidence:** high on every number, since all were recomputed by script. Moderate on the source citations, because most could not be opened.

**Next moves**
- **demo-builder:** reword herd-immunity c5, then work through the fixes above.
- **A checker other than me:** verify the 11 added claims and re-verify c5 after the reword.
- I have not added a `company/ops/progress.md` handoff or board items.

  - `/home/user/system-3-company/company/reviews/base-rates/2026-10-12-fact-check.md`

- Scratch scripts (all in `/home/user/system-3-company/artifacts/scratch/`): `fc-probability.mjs`, `fc-life.mjs`, `fc-herd-extra.mjs`, `fc-ns-extra.mjs`, `fc-apply-meta.mjs`

summary: Learner reviews ai + economics: All four reviews are written, and each lesson's meta.json now lists its review under evidence.simulatedLearne…
body:
All four reviews are written, and each lesson's meta.json now lists its review under evidence.simulatedLearner. All four verdicts are "revise". I found no FATAL flaw in any of them.

Each review follows the independence rules. Section 1 came from the transcript, the walkthrough PNGs, the QA phone PNGs and my own Playwright runs. I read meta.json only after section 1 was written. I did not open build.md or design.md, and I did not read Demo.tsx. The boundary was an adult with school arithmetic and everyday life who has never studied the topic. For meta.json I re-read each file just before editing and changed only the simulatedLearner array.

| Lesson | Verdict | Top finding |
|---|---|---|
| gradient-descent | revise | The reveal unlocks after a single Step at 0.35, before the learner has seen 0.95 or 1.05. The surprising claim that 0.05 and 0.95 tie at 1.39 can arrive purely told. "Slope" is never given a number, so a beginner can't apply "step size × slope". |
| overfitting | revise | The reveal unlocks after one slider notch (bends = 1). "Bends" 1, 2 and 3 look identical on screen (1.5, 1.6, 1.6 °C), so the control looks inert. At 6 bends the worst misses are drawn off the chart, so the 5.1 °C can't be checked by eye. The 0.0 versus 5.1 contrast is the strong part and is earned. |
| compound-interest | revise | The two readouts mix a sliding ten-year window ("YEARS 4–13 ADDED") with a running total ("INTEREST ON INTEREST") with no cue. The reveal unlocks at year 11, so the 40-year balance isn't required. The straight-line $4,900 and "doubles every ten years" are told, not drawn. |
| supply-demand | revise | The title "Cheaper bread, less bread?" nearly gives the answer away. The reveal unlocks at $6.50, before the cap is ever pressed. The cap is silently dropped when the slider moves, while the "Cap at $4" button still looks active. The reveal-state buttons are clipped at the bottom of the card in both the walkthrough and the QA phone screenshots. |

**Cross-lesson pattern:**
- Reveal gating is the same weak spot in all four, and a real learner may well hit it. The reveal button enables after one trivial interaction, so the key evidence can be skipped.

- The gating, the readout numbers and the clipped buttons are firm. I observed them directly in my own runs and in the artifacts.

- All claims in every lesson are still `unverified`. I did not fact-check them, only recomputed a few numbers by hand.
- Overfitting: it never tells the learner the dots are simulated, so the reveal's "each reading is the day's smooth warming plus random jitter" reads as fact about real readings. I flagged this as an honesty question for the fact-checker.

body:
I wrote AMD-001 (status: proposed), the agenda for the constitutional review, and the README index entry. No protected path was touched, and `npm run check` still passes.

**What AMD-001 proposes.** Four parts, each with its exact diff, ready to be ratified separately:
- **(a) `ready` on `<Lesson>`:** an optional `ready?: boolean`. Once it is true during explore it stays unlocked. The lesson root shows `data-ready` only for lessons that pass it, so all 18 current lessons are unchanged. A new contract test checks gated lessons: the key state is not the starting state, the reveal stays disabled until it is reached, and QA must reach it within 400 actions. I chose a boolean over a callback because lesson state lives in the Demo component, not the kit.
- **(b) Rituals:** `retro` (7 days), `eng-review` and `offboarding` (on event) go into the cadence table. I decided against making a second fact-check a gate or a ritual. No second pass has run yet, so there is no evidence it finds anything, and (c1) closes the actual hole. The amendment says what would reopen this.
- **(c1) Second check for checker-added claims:** I changed your suggested rule. All 109 verifications are signed `"fact-checker"`, so "checkedBy ≠ addedBy" would block every legitimate second check. The rule compares review records instead: a claim with `addedIn` must have a different `checkedIn` that exists on disk.
- **(c2) Registry move:** yes, the generator moves to `tools/registry.mjs`. `check` keeps its freshness check and adds two checks that don't depend on the generator: every lesson is imported from its own meta.json, and generated code never sets a status.

**How sure I am.** All four diffs were applied to a scratch copy only. (a) type-checks, but its Playwright test never ran, so I am about 70% sure it will reach key states on real lessons. The company.mjs parts were tested in scratch: (c1) fired on planted cases, a tampered generator (dropped half-life, injected a status) was caught, and the regenerated registry was byte-identical. About 90% there. The learner reviews show the reveal reachable without the key state in at least 16 of 18 lessons; the retro says 18/18.

**Two side effects.** The agenda file makes `status` show constitutional-review as held today, though it has not been held. I also skipped the `progress.md` handoff because you limited me to three files.

**Next moves:**
- The founder chairs the review and fills in the Decision column. My recommendations: re-ratify AMD-000 without the founder casting the deciding vote, and ratify all four parts.
- If (c1) passes, the fact-checker backfills `addedBy`/`addedIn` on the wave 0 claims.
- If (c2) passes, the principal-engineer updates the EDD-001 option 4 sentence that says it needs an amendment.

**Briefs:** I re-computed every number with node scripts. All ten prediction answers are right, so nothing was skipped and #11 was not taken. Two briefs had other errors, which I fixed in the lessons:
- **shared-pasture:** the brief says group income falls to 0 at 20 cows. With its own rule (each herder adds a cow only if it raises their income), adding stops at 18 cows and group income is 36. The lesson says 100 → 36 (claim c4, support "simulation"). cm-economics should correct the brief.

- The reveal is earned in every lesson: the reveal button only unlocks once the learner reaches the key state (for example, the fee at 1%, or the other herders responding). Answer-giving readouts are hidden until the prediction.
- After looking at the phone screenshots I changed each lesson at least once: clipped labels, a hidden player cow, a squeezed axis, and hooks that leaned on the answer. Details are in each `build.md`.
- I'm only moderately confident in the teaching itself; that needs evaluators and real learners.

I built chemistry briefs #1–#10 as 10 lessons. All of them pass check, typecheck, build and the QA contract (20/20, phone and desktop), and they are committed in cedb55d. No briefs were skipped.

Branch `worktree-agent-ad5ad3045ef629da5`, commit `cedb55d` (not pushed).

| slug | concept | prediction → answer (re-computed with a node script) | claims | QA |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| same-sugar-more-water | dilution | 100 mL at 1.0 mol/L made up to 500 mL → 0.20 mol/L | 6 | pass |
| atoms-across-a-hair | atom-scale-size | 70 µm ÷ 0.2 nm → about 350,000 | 5 | pass |
| read-the-bone-clock | carbon-dating | 1/8 of the carbon-14 left → about 17,100 y (3 half-lives) | 5 | pass |
| heavy-but-floats | density | 500 g / 800 cm³ = 0.625 g/cm³ → floats | 6 | pass |
| one-dose-of-acid | buffers | water pH 7 → 2; buffer 4.76 → 4.67 | 6 | pass |
| twice-as-hot-not-twice-as-fast | temperature-particle-motion | 300 → 600 K → 1.41× (air 508 → 719 m/s) | 5 | pass |
| the-tail-that-reacts | reaction-rates-temperature | 50 kJ/mol, 298 → 308 K → ×1.93 | 7 | pass |
| the-tagged-molecule | equilibrium | molecules keep changing both ways in equal numbers | 4 | pass |
| freezer-balloon | gas-laws | 1.00 L at 300 K → 0.85 L at 255 K | 6 | pass |
| same-count-different-weight | moles-counting | 12 g of C and 18 g of water → about the same (≈1 mol each) | 6 | pass |

Every brief's numbers held up, but some content changed:
- **Hair citation:** the brief's "Ley & Bartlett, J. Cosmet. Sci. 2008" could not be confirmed. I replaced it with The Physics Factbook compilation (17–181 µm) and flagged it for the fact-checker.
- **Atom size:** now backed by atomic radii from Cordero 2008 and Bondi 1964.
- **Carbon-14:** uses the NUBASE2020 half-life (5,700 y); the 5,730 and Libby 5,568 values are noted in the claim.
- **Recall questions:** I removed facts that were not recorded as claims, and rebalanced the option lengths so the right answer is not always the longest.
- **Locked stage:** anything that would give the answer away is hidden before the prediction (the decay curve, the balloon's line, the atom-count readout, the ball's state).

All claims are "unverified"; I did not verify any.

**How sure I am:**
- **Numbers and claims:** high confidence.
- **Earned reveals:** medium. QA presses each control only once (a slider moves two steps), so I cannot require the learner to reach the key end state; the reveal button would never unlock in QA. I used `minInteractions` of 2, or 4 ticks for the tagged molecule, and made each reveal describe what the learner actually reached ("You poured to 300 mL; at 500 mL…").
- **Biggest content risk:** the-tail-that-reacts uses a broken energy axis with the tail drawn 250 million times taller. Both are labelled on the stage and recorded as a claim, but the picture may confuse beginners.

**Design changes after looking at the phone screenshots:**
- atoms-across-a-hair: the middle zoom levels were a plain grey square, so I added "still inside the hair" and "a row of atoms, too small to see" labels.
- the-tagged-molecule: one molecule now starts tagged so the learner sees its history strip without having to discover tapping.
- one-dose-of-acid and twice-as-hot-not-twice-as-fast: fixed labels that overlapped.

**Kit and platform requests (for platform-engineer):**
1. `next build` with Turbopack fails in a worktree because the `node_modules` symlink points outside the project root. I built with `npx next build --webpack`. Either the verify step should use that, or `turbopack.root` should be set in `next.config.mjs`.
2. The QA contract can only unlock "reach the end state" reveals if the end state is one press away. A per-lesson QA script, or a kit-level way to gate the reveal on a goal the stage defines, would make "earned" reveals enforceable.
3. During the reveal phase the stage shrinks and cuts off the bottom of tall stages (the tagged molecule's history strip).

**Next moves:**
- fact-checker: verify the 57 claims, especially the hair diameter, atom size, the 50,000-year radiocarbon limit, and blood pH.
- evaluators / evaluation-steward: QA record and borrowed-mind reviews.
- platform-engineer: the three requests above.

I built all ten ai lessons from briefs #1–#10 and committed them. Status is "review" on each. All four checks passed on the final run: company check (0 errors, 0 warnings), tsc, next build, and Playwright QA (20/20, phone and desktop). Not pushed.

Branch `worktree-agent-a649b52d9d2fd72da`, commit `597663d`.

Build caveat: `next build` (Turbopack) fails in this worktree because the node_modules symlink points outside the project root. I built with `npx next build --webpack` instead, changing no config, and restored tsconfig.json with git checkout.

| slug | concept | prediction → answer | claims | QA |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| next-word-tally | next-token | Can it write "the dog sat on the mat"? → Yes, from the counts | 6 | pass |
| never-flag-99 | accuracy-paradox | Approve-all accuracy → ~99% | 5 | pass |
| temperature-reshapes | temperature-sampling | Top word at T=0.5 → ~87% (86.7%) | 7 | pass |
| whose-cutoff-wins | training-data-bias | Fewest-mistakes cutoff → 50, A's line | 5 | pass |
| patrol-feedback-loop | feedback-loops | A's share after 20 rounds → 84% (26/31) | 4 | pass |
| background-shortcut | shortcut-learning | Accuracy on shuffled backgrounds → 50% | 4 | pass |
| spam-threshold-tradeoff | precision-recall-threshold | Threshold 0.25 → more spam caught and more real mail flagged | 4 | pass |
| true-text-false-claims | fluent-not-factual | False rate, 1-word memory → 2 in 3 | 5 | pass |
| attention-shares-one | attention-weights | A's share at 45° → ~45% (44.6%) | 5 | pass |
| clicks-not-value | goodharts-law | Reader value at max clicks → 0 | 4 | pass |

**Skipped briefs:** none. Every brief answer reproduced by running the lesson's own model code; numbers in claims come from those runs.

**Changes from the briefs, each noted in that lesson's build.md:**
- never-flag-99: tapping 1,000 dots is impossible on a phone, so the learner instead flags "the riskiest N" (an invented ranking) with a slider and presets. Flagging 20 catches 8 of 10 frauds but scores 98.6%, below "approve all".
- temperature-reshapes: the question now says 66.5%, not 67%, to match the stage.
- whose-cutoff-wins: I dropped the brief's second slider (group B's share) to keep one control.
- attention-shares-one: my own draft claim "no word can exceed 66.5%" was false (70.0% at 336°). I removed it.

**How each reveal is earned:** every lesson calls interact() only at the state the question asks about, e.g. a finished sentence, T=0.5, the minimum cutoff, round 20, or the click optimiser at its end. Spam is the exception: any two slider moves unlock it, because its stage message describes the trade-off in either direction. Readouts that would give away the answer show "?" while locked.

**Weak spots for reviewers:**

  - The requests are at the end of the briefs file.

I recomputed every prediction with node and all ten hold. All claims are "unverified".

| slug | concept | prediction → answer | claims | QA | reveal unlocks when |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| two-squares-become-one | pythagoras-by-rearrangement | 3,4 → long side 5 | 4 | pass | the two-squares layout is reached |
| fifty-up-fifty-down | percent-change-asymmetry | 100 +50% −50% → 75 | 4 | pass | 50% has been on stage |
| gauss-staircase | triangular-numbers | 1+…+10 → 55 | 3 | pass | n = 10 and the flipped copy is placed |
| circle-slices-to-rectangle | circle-area-unrolled | circle in square → 78% | 4 | pass | unrolled with 16+ slices |
| digits-are-logs | logarithm-as-digit-count | digits of 2^100 → 31 | 4 | pass | the strip reaches 2^100 |
| seventy-two-doubling | rule-of-72 | 8% doubling → 9 yrs | 4 | pass | 8% has been on stage |
| double-the-size | area-scaling | 12" vs 6" pizza → 4 | 4 | pass | 12 inches has been on stage |
| nines-without-end | repeating-nine | gap of 0.999… → exactly 0 | 4 | pass | "All of them, forever" (needs at least one zoom first) |
| one-boss-moves-the-mean | mean-vs-median | boss to 500 → only the mean | 4 | pass | the mean is above 4 of 5 salaries |
| one-recipe-for-sixty | prime-factorization | prime recipes of 60 → 1 | 3 | pass | three different first splits tried |

Each reveal fires `interact()` only when the learner reaches the key state, and the locked stage hides anything that would give the answer away. The QA script presses each control once (two arrow presses for a slider), so each gate is set where that sequence can reach it.

**Brief fixes and deviations:**
- **seventy-two-doubling:** brief claim (3) said 72/r is within about 1 year from 4% to 12%. It is within 0.33 years there; the lesson states the accurate range, within 0.2 years from 5% to 20% (0.55 at 3%). The rate slider runs 2–20%, not 1–20%: 1% takes 70 years and runs off the chart.
- **one-boss-moves-the-mean:** I used bars instead of dots on a number line, because at a 0–500 scale the four low dots overlap on a phone.
- **one-recipe-for-sixty:** the learner picks only the first split; lower splits are automatic. A choice at every node would need tappable SVG nodes, which the QA loop cannot press reliably.
- **digits-are-logs:** it has a "Run to 100" play button alongside a step button and the slider, because one press per control cannot reach 2^100 otherwise.
- **two-squares-become-one:** the slider has only 3 stops for the same reason. Continuous sliding would feel better.

**Screenshot fixes:** at least one per lesson, each recorded in its `build.md`. Examples: rise, fall and net-loss labels on fifty-up-fifty-down; box outlines over the slices on the circle lesson; removed a 31-cell outline on the digits strip that gave away the answer; decluttered the rule-of-72 chart.

**Environment:**
- Turbopack refuses the symlinked `node_modules`, so I built with `next build --webpack`.
- I kept the progress.md handoff out because company/ops is off-limits to me.

**Kit and QA requests (platform-engineer / evaluation-steward):**
1. The QA contract presses each control only once, which pushes builders toward coarse sliders or play buttons whenever the reveal waits for an end state. Could QA allow a lesson to declare its own route to the gate, e.g. `data-qa-steps`?
2. A kit hook for gated reveals would avoid the repeated `Stage` + `useEffect` + `useRef` pattern, e.g. `revealWhen={condition}` on `<Lesson>`.

| slug | concept | prediction → answer | claims | QA |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| monty-hall-100-doors | monty-hall | other door, 100 doors → 99% | 5 | pass |
| five-heads-then-what | gamblers-fallacy | heads on flip 6 → exactly 50% | 4 | pass |
| one-in-a-million-match | prosecutors-fallacy | innocent matches in 5M → about 5 | 5 | pass |
| better-in-every-group-worse-overall | simpsons-paradox | higher overall → B (82.6% vs 78.0%) | 6 | pass |

**Skipped briefs:** none. Every prediction answer held up when I recomputed it in node (exact sums or the lesson's own seeded `model.ts`, run with `--experimental-strip-types`). Two brief numbers were wrong and one citation was misspelled:
- **Brief #2:** about 1 position in 32 follows five heads (about 312 per 10,000 flips), not 1 in 64 or about 150. The claim corrects this.
- **Brief #8:** "about 100" is the SD of the gap; the average gap is 79.8. I changed the question to "on average how far apart", with options Under 5 / About 80 / About 1,000. The stage's 20 runs average 86.
- **Brief #7:** the second author of the Wald paper is Samaniego, not "Samaniuk".

**Reveal gating:** each reveal unlocks only after the learner reaches the key moment. For example: 20 caught streaks, the full 5M search, opening the lost planes, test 2 being sat, reaching 10,000 flips and switching view, visiting hospital B. Answer readouts stay hidden while the stage is locked.

**Chosen seeds:** I picked three seeds on purpose and say so in the claims: `one-in-a-million-match` seed 28 (exactly the expected 5 matches), `twenty-harmless-tests` seed 4 (first batch shows 2 alarms). Seed 2024 in `hidden-third-cause` is untuned.

**Known weak spot:** in `monty-hall-100-doors` the reveal can be reached playing only at 3 doors. The reveal then names that door count.

**Source claims:** Charig 1986 / Julious & Mullee 1994, Thompson & Schumann 1987, Mangel & Samaniego 1984, Tversky & Kahneman 1974, Galton 1886 and the Feller chapters are cited from my knowledge, not checked, and still need checking.

body:
All ten physics briefs (#1–#10) are built and committed. None were skipped, so #11 was not needed. Check, typecheck, build and QA all pass (20/20, phone and desktop). The build only works with `--webpack`, because Turbopack rejects the symlinked node_modules (see requests below).

Branch: `worktree-agent-a33d61dc33a96d6db` · commit `2fe3bfc` (not pushed)

| slug | concept | prediction → answer | claims | QA |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| dropped-vs-fired-ball | independent-components | which lands first → together, 2.02 s | 5 | pass |
| puck-on-ice-no-push | inertia | push to keep 2 m/s → none | 5 | pass |
| current-same-around-loop | current-not-used-up | between the bulbs → 0.50 A | 6 | pass |
| moon-hammer-feather | falling-objects | which lands first → together, 1.36 s | 6 | pass |
| same-push-twice-the-mass | net-force-acceleration | 10 N on 4 kg at 2 s → 5 m/s | 5 | pass |
| doubling-speed-braking | kinetic-energy-speed-squared | 60 km/h → about 28 m (27.8) | 6 | pass |
| flour-on-the-moon | mass-vs-weight | what changes → weight | 6 | pass |
| truck-hits-car-force | action-reaction | who pushes harder → equal | 5 | pass |
| light-at-double-distance | inverse-square | 2 m → 25 lux | 5 | pass |
| coaster-track-shape | energy-conservation | steep or gentle → same, 9.90 m/s | 5 | pass |

**Numbers and physics:** I recomputed every brief number with node scripts that integrate the real equations, and all ten brief answers held. The simulations use real equations: the hammer and feather, crash and coaster use RK4 integration, and the coaster is computed piece by piece from Newton's second law, so 9.90 m/s comes out of the sim rather than being plugged in. One bug turned up in my own code (a landing-time interpolation error) and is fixed. All claims are "unverified"; I did not verify any.

**Illustrative values:** the friction coefficients, the drag in the "air on" mode, and the crash contact stiffness are made-up but plausible. Each is labelled illustrative in its claim.

**Earned reveals:** every reveal is gated on the key moment, by calling interact() only then:
- a run touching down (dropped ball, hammer and feather);
- the no-friction lane plus one other lane (puck);
- the ammeter placed between the bulbs (circuit);
- reaching 4 kg at 10 N, 60 km/h, the Moon, 2 m, or moving into the crash;
- two track changes (coaster).

Answer-revealing readouts stay hidden while the stage is locked.

**Changes made after looking at screenshots** (details in each `company/reviews/<slug>/build.md`):
- **Coaster:** the reveal quoted 9.90 m/s while every readout still showed "?". Results now show as soon as a track is chosen, and the reveal quotes the learner's own two times.
- **Circuit, same-push, puck:** reveals stated numbers the learner might not have seen. They now report what was actually seen.
- **Layout:** fixed the off-screen landing at 25 m/s, objects sinking through the floor at landing, and overlapping labels and arrows.

**Departures from briefs:**
- Puck uses four lane buttons instead of a slider.
- Dropped-ball speed is capped at 25 m/s so the arc keeps its true shape on a phone.
- The same-push hook was rewritten because the brief's framing hinted "half the speed".
- In the braking brief, "28 m" is really 27.8 m.

**What I'm not sure of:** the physics and gating I'm fairly confident about. The text budget is near the limit on truck-hits-car-force and same-push. Sources an evaluator should check most: the NASA ALSJ hammer-and-feather URL, the UK Highway Code figures (rule 126; about 6.4 m/s² is my own arithmetic), and the "five times" photometry rule of thumb.

**Kit and platform requests:**
1. Platform-engineer: `next build` fails under Turbopack with the symlinked node_modules ("symlink target leaves the filesystem root"). Either set a Turbopack root or document `--webpack` for worktrees.
2. Platform-engineer / evaluation-steward: QA presses each control once and waits only about 5 s, so a reveal gated on several animated runs cannot pass. A kit way to gate a reveal on a condition (for example an `earned` flag) would remove the interact() workarounds.

I did not add the progress.md handoff or board entries: company/ops is off-limits for this task.

Next move: evaluators (walkthrough and borrowed-mind review) and a claim verifier other than me check the claims. Cm-physics confirms the departures above.

| back-button-stack | stack-and-queue | where Back lands → B | 4 | pass |

**Briefs checked:** I re-ran every brief number in Node and all were correct, so nothing was skipped and I did not need #11.

**Brief fixes and deviations:**
- **pennies-dont-add-up:** a 12-switch fixed-point model of the sum gives 0.1 + 0.2 = exactly the nearest 0.3 (1229/4096), which would teach the wrong answer. So the switches only show that 0.1 can never be hit exactly, and the sum is shown with real 53-digit values.
- **coin-greedy-trap:** I cited CLRS Problem 16-1 rather than the brief's exercise 16.1-3, which is a different problem.
- **back-button-stack:** I dropped the queue mode to keep one idea per card; the queue gets one contrast sentence in the reveal.

**How the reveals are earned:** each reveal opens only after the learner reaches the key moment on the stage, not on any tap. Examples: fib needs the full 15-call tree and then the memo view; insertion needs two different hands finished; back-button needs a visit that throws away forward pages. The rest are in the build notes.

To make that work with QA, every lesson has a shortcut control early in the page (such as "Open every call", "Finish this hand" or "Join the two lightest"). QA presses each control only once, in page order, so without these it could never reach the gate. Each shortcut still shows the key moment on the stage. Anything that would give the answer away is hidden until after the prediction.

**Confidence:** high that the lessons work and the numbers are right. Two weaker spots:
- **Hanoi:** a learner can open the reveal after 3–4 disks, so 31 and 63 may be told rather than seen.
- **Hash:** the tallies come from seeded random tables (67.7% of 201 collided by key 5, against the exact 69.8%).

**Environment notes:**
- Turbopack refuses the symlinked `node_modules`, so I built with `next build --webpack`.
- Port 3612 was already taken by another worktree's server (agent-ad3cb4…), so QA ran on `QA_PORT=3677`.
- I did not write a `company/ops/progress.md` handoff, because ops paths were off-limits in this task.

**Kit / QA requests** (for platform-engineer or evaluation-steward; I did not edit any of these):
1. QA's "did anything change" check ignores CSS class changes, so state shown only by styling counts as dead. My wall toggles failed on this until walls got a real child element. Consider including class names in the check.
2. QA presses each control once, in page order, so a reveal gated on an end state is only reachable through shortcut buttons. A per-lesson QA script, or repeated presses, would allow stricter gates.
3. Turbopack fails on a symlinked `node_modules` in worktrees. Either document `--webpack` or set the turbopack root.

**Next:** fact-checker verifies the 64 claims; evaluators run walkthroughs, then read the build notes.

The doubling is drawn as ×2 arcs, and when the switches on add up to 3, 7 … 255 the stage says "one less than the next switch". The +1 carry is explained when it happens ("127 + 1 = 128 … like 9 + 1 = 10"), and so is the roll back to 0 after 255. Gate: reach 255, then a +1 from 127 or 255. All 7 learner findings fixed; c6 changed, c7 and c8 added, all unverified.
- **gradient-descent (v2).** Gate: a finished 10-hop run at a tiny step and one at a too-big step. New one-tap "Run 10 at 0.05 / 0.45 / 0.95 / 1.05" buttons and a record of finished runs, so the 0.05 / 0.95 tie sits side by side. A live "Next hop = step × slope" line defines slope. The 0.2 message now describes the hop just taken. c3 and c5 sources fixed (the unread quote is dropped), c8 and c9 rewritten, c10 added, all unverified. Rejected: changing the hook, because the tension is the point and the reveal now says "Bigger is not faster".
- **overfitting (v2).** The slider became tap buttons 0–6. Gate: look at 1–3 bends and at 6. The stage says "simulated data". The comparison with the line now reads "On these dots…" and adds that with other random dots the result varies (c10: 38% / 91% over 500 seeds). "Smooth warming" became "rise and fall", and the true curve is drawn dashed in the reveal. The chart floor is now 0 °C so the 6-bend misses are visible, and each button keeps its miss once seen. Rejected: answering "how many bends should I use" (out of scope for 60 seconds).
- **compound-interest (v2).** Both readouts are now running totals at the chosen year; each decade's gain has its own row. Jump buttons 10/20/30/40. Gate: reach 40 years. The text says "$2,800 of interest: a balance of $3,800". A model label is on the stage and a dashed straight-line pace is drawn. c3 changed, c9 and c10 added. Rejected: explaining $967 vs $700 in text, since the $267 readout shows it and the reveal is at its word budget.
- **supply-demand (v2).** New title "Make bread cheaper by law?", plus "Toy town" on the stage and in the question. The cap is now an explicit state: a red line is drawn, the slider stops at $4, only "Lift the cap" removes it, and the price button is disabled while the cap holds. Gate: press the cap. Gaps are labelled shortage / surplus, and the price button says which way the price moves. c8 changed, c10 and c11 added.
- **mercator-greenland (v3).** I re-measured c3 with d3-geo on the shipped map: 15.39, shown as "about 15". It is drawn whole, no clipping. One mismatch remained: the starting readout used a slightly moved shape and showed 15.0×; it now uses the real one and shows 15.4×. c3 stays unverified for the fact-checker. Gate: slide Greenland at all, then see its true size (within 10° of the equator or on Equal Earth). The equator is now drawn, and the slider shows the current latitude. The v2 design is kept.

Not fixed: when the reveal opens on a phone, the kit's reveal panel squeezes the stage. The bottom control row is cut off in gradient-descent and supply-demand (reveal screenshots), and in compound-interest the years slider and jump buttons are cut off too. body:
All six lessons are revised and committed in 0903e7b (not pushed). Both FATALs (base-rates, half-life) are fixed. QA passes 12/12 (phone and desktop); registry and check give 0 errors, and tsc and next build are clean. Each lesson's reveal now unlocks only after the learner reaches the key state (via `useMilestones`), and the QA path (each control pressed once in page order) reaches it. Where the last control the contract presses moves the stage away, the stage returns to that key state during the reveal, so the text matches the picture. Changed claims are back to "unverified" and every `version` is now 2. None of the six had a `build.md`, so each one is new and starts at "## v2 (revision)". Each lists every finding and what I did with it.

- **base-rates (FATAL fixed):** the reveal needs 1,000 people tested at 1 in 1,000. The other disease buttons stay locked until then and sit after Test all in the page, so the contract hits the gate first. The reveal quotes counts computed by the code that draws the grid (11 positive, 1 sick), and true positives get a ring when there are 10 or fewer. Harvard line reworded with "if the test catches every case" (c6 back to unverified; new claim c9). Not fully solved: "Hide results" is still a toggle.
- **birthday-paradox:** the gate is 20 or more rooms of 23 plus one change of room size. Tallies are kept per size and the reveal quotes only rooms of 23. In the reveal the ring returns to 23 people (253 lines). The locked stage no longer shows a match. c9 and c11 (claims about how people guess) are withdrawn, and I added the bridge "all 253 pairs miss ≈ 50%" (c12). Rejected: the dots-clustering finding, because uniform random draws do cluster.
- **herd-immunity:** c5 reworded as you specified (unverified). The stage now says "Toy disease, R0 = 4", and the readout shows "4 × 20% = 0.8". The gate is one finished outbreak above 75% plus one below it that took off. I replaced the slider with share buttons (50 to 90%): after an outbreak ends, a tap shows the same outbreak's end at the new share. "Typical" is now "Average", and "had it" looks different from "sick now". Rejected: switching to a median, because c4 is a verified mean.
- **natural-selection:** the gate is generation 100 at the 10% edge. I added "Go to 100" and a strip under the bark that draws the share over generations, so a jump still shows the slow start. The ×1.1 → 99 in 100 bridge is computed (about 139 dark to 1 pale). Also: a "100 beetles stand for a huge population" label, the bird-predation reason in the question, edge buttons (1/5/10/20%), and "non-overlapping generations" added to c1. Partly open: parent-to-young links are still not drawn.
- **half-life (FATAL fixed):** "half-life" is defined in the question. The gate is one run watched through half-life 4. Waits are capped at 4, each bar shows how many atoms it started from, and the caption reads "Fewer atoms, more wobble". The reveal quotes that run, and the stage shows it in the reveal even after New run. Kept the Carbon-14 line (now meaningful, verified).
- **ph-log-scale:** the gate is reaching pH 2. Controls run pH down, then a slider (right = more acid), then pH up, so the contract walks 5 → 4 → 3 → 2. "About 1,000" is framed as following from the round values, and real cups vary 200 to 1,300 times (c7). I added a zoomed view for pH 6 and 7, changed the hook's "acid" to "hydrogen ions", and withdrew c6 (the 0-14 sentence is no longer shown). Rejected: landmarks for pH 3 and 4 that I can't cite.

**Trade-offs from the press-once contract:** the order of controls on the page now does design work. I added three shortcuts ("Go to 100", "Wait to half-life 4", pH down), and the pH slider runs opposite to the usual pH chart. On phones, the last lines of some reveals are clipped by the shared lesson card in the screenshots; I can't edit the card, so it is unchanged.

**How sure:** high on the gates and the QA path, which I checked against the screenshots. Medium on wording, since nothing has been reviewed by anyone else.

body:
I built 10 economics lessons (briefs #11–#20) and committed them. Every gate passed: `company check` (0 errors; the one warning is in life/herd-immunity, not mine), `tsc --noEmit`, `next build` with Turbopack (webpack not needed; I restored tsconfig.json afterwards) and QA (20/20, phone and desktop, run twice, the second time after screenshot fixes).

Branch `worktree-agent-af640eafc60c2ee13`, commit `879f980`, not pushed.

| slug | prediction → answer | claims | QA |
|---|---|---|---|
| true-cost-of-free-hours | $50 / $60 / $110 → $110 | 5 | pass |
| widget-marginal-cost | ~$4 / $2 / $102 → $2 | 6 | pass |
| kitchen-crowding | 40 / 28 / 20 → 28 | 4 | pass |
| revenue-sweet-spot | $3 / $5 / $8 → $5 | 4 | pass |
| flour-shock | $6 / $7 / $8 → $7 | 6 | pass |
| apr-apy-gap | $12 / ~$12.68 / ~$14 → $12.68 | 6 | pass |
| insurance-fair-price | $120 / $100 / $0 → $100 | 6 | pass |
| two-bets-split | 50% / 25% / 0% → 25% | 6 | pass |
| wait-or-take-now | $1,000 now / $1,200 later / equal → later ($1,036.61) | 6 | pass |
| cheese-for-bread | no / yes, 24 loaves / only Ben gains → 24 loaves | 5 | pass |

**How they are built:**
- Every answer was recomputed with node scripts, and all 10 brief answers are correct.
- Each lesson gates the reveal with `useMilestones` on the key state, and the QA path reaches it: starting values are offset (for example 48 widgets, 3%, $3) so QA's two arrow presses land on the question's numbers.
- Answer-giving readouts are hidden until the prediction is locked in.
- Each stage has a model label, and the question's numbers come from the same constants the stage draws.
- Claims are all "unverified"; I verified none.
- Each lesson has a 3–4 line build note. I looked at the phone screenshots for all 10 and fixed what I saw: clipped or overlapping labels in apr-apy-gap, flour-shock and widget-marginal-cost; blocks too small at the old scale in kitchen-crowding; a misplaced total label in true-cost-of-free-hours.

**Where I departed from the briefs:**
- **two-bets-split:** the brief says the chance of a loss shrinks as you split across more bets. That is false at 4 bets (31.3%, more than the 25% at 2). The stage shows the true numbers and the reveal says so. A "worst case" readout (−10%, chance halving with each bet) shows the part that really does shrink. cm-economics should fix the payoff wording in the brief.
- **insurance-fair-price:** I dropped the brief's premium slider to keep one picture. Seed 1 was chosen because its first year has exactly one loss, and claim c4 says so. Across 2,000 seeds the 101-year average payout is between $80 and $120 95% of the time.
- **cheese-for-bread:** the brief asked for 16 dragged hour tokens. I used two sliders in 2-hour blocks instead, because QA could not reach the key state with tokens. Ben 8 hours on cheese and Ana 6 on bread is the only plan on that grid that keeps 12 cheeses and makes more than 20 loaves.
- **kitchen-crowding:** QA can only reach 4 workers. So the reveal's "worker 6 adds nothing" sentence changes depending on whether the learner went past 5 workers.

**Skipped briefs:** none.

**Kit request (for platform-engineer):** `useMilestones` needs `interact`, which only exists inside the render-prop. Every lesson therefore needs an inner `Stage` component to call the hook legally. Wave 2 builder: probability: I built 10 probability lessons, all set to status "review", and committed them (not pushed). Briefs 11–20 min…
body:
I built 10 probability lessons, all set to status "review", and committed them (not pushed). Briefs 11–20 minus #16, plus #21 in its place. Every lesson passes QA on phone and desktop (20 of 20), and check, tsc and `next build` (the default bundler, not webpack) are all clean.
Branch: worktree-agent-aa25e756f51ffe15c. Commit: 319d4f5.

| slug | prediction → answer | claims | QA |
|---|---|---|---|
| which-coin-is-it | 50/75/89% → 89% (8/9) | 6 | pass |
| one-in-a-million-daily | never/8 a day/once a year → 8 a day | 6 | pass |
| same-average-different-ride | X/Y/equal → Y (exact 32.1% vs 13.6%) | 6 | pass |
| plus-fifty-minus-forty | grows/shrinks/even → shrinks (median 0.9^50) | 6 | pass |
| at-least-one-boy | 1/2, 1/3, 1/4 → 1/3 | 5 | pass |
| why-seven-wins | equal/3x/6x → 3x | 4 | pass |
| drunk-walk-distance | 1/8/50 m → 8 m (exact 7.96) | 4 | pass |
| friends-have-more-friends | 1.6/2.5/3.4 → 3.4 | 4 | pass |
| collect-all-six-faces | 6/9/15 → about 15 (14.7) | 4 | pass |
| average-that-never-settles | settles/keeps jumping/drifts to 0 → keeps jumping | 5 | pass |

- **Numbers:** every number was recomputed in node, either exactly or by mulberry32 simulation, using the same model.ts the stage draws from. Question and reveal numbers are computed from that model, never typed in.
- **Seeds:** all are untuned and say so in the claims, with the spread over 200–500 seeds, except one. which-coin-is-it uses a chosen seed (9) so the first coin can show three heads; this is disclosed in claim c6.
- **Gates:** each lesson has 2 milestones, and pressing every control once in order (as QA does) reaches both.
- **Claims:** all are "unverified". Two book citations are general: Feller's chapter numbers for collect-all-six-faces and average-that-never-settles are marked "chapter not checked".

**Skipped brief:** #16 fake-the-coin-flips. Its answer is wrong as worded. A run of 5 or more heads-or-tails in 20 fair flips has probability 0.458 (exact count), not 0.25. The 0.2499 is the heads-only figure; the brief's 0.478 and 0.122 are heads-only too. Rewording the question to "5 or more heads in a row" would make 25% correct. The category manager (cm-probability) should fix the brief.

**Changes from the briefs:**
- **drunk-walk-distance:** the brief's "about 10 m" is the standard deviation; the average distance is 8 m, so the question now asks for the average with options 1 / 8 / 50 m.
- **one-in-a-million-daily:** buttons instead of a slider, because two QA arrow presses would never reach 8 million.
- **why-seven-wins:** six "drop this first die's pairs" buttons instead of 36 single taps, so the gate is reachable.
- **friends-have-more-friends:** the stage is the question's 5-person star, not a network the learner builds.

**Fixes from the screenshots:**
- average-that-never-settles originally drew one Cauchy run. On the QA path, "New draws" landed on a calm run that drifted to 0, which supports the misconception. It now draws 5 runs at a time.
- friends-have-more-friends had a "Start over" button; QA ended on 0 picks and the reveal said "your 0 picks", so I removed it.
- why-seven-wins: the dashed roll outlines covered the tile labels; they are now red lines drawn behind the tiles.
- drunk-walk-distance: dots were too small to read; they are bigger now and a tall pile squeezes its spacing to fit.

**Possible overlap:** plus-fifty-minus-forty may overlap math/fifty-up-fifty-down and economics/up-then-down-trap. It teaches a different point (average across players versus the typical player); this is noted in its build.md for the curriculum owner.

**Kit requests (for platform-engineer):**
1. `useMilestones` must be called from a module-level Stage component, because the render-prop pattern breaks the rules of hooks. I used that pattern in all 10. A kit `<Stage>` wrapper or a ref-based `interact` would avoid it.
2. Models can't be run in node because of the `@/` path alias. I used a custom node resolve hook from my scratchpad; a checked-in `tools/run-model.mjs` would let fact-checkers re-run models the same way.

I did not write a progress.md entry or touch the board (company/ops was off-limits per the task). Next: fact-check the 51 claims (fact-checker) and run QA and borrowed-mind reviews (evaluation-steward).

- **Added (cs):** sketch-the-counts c6, "usually close". I wrote it, so it stays unverified for another checker.
- **merge-sort-payoff:** I also re-checked c4-c8. The earlier checker added and verified them itself, so I set their checkedOn to 2026-10-13.

**Disputed**
- **heavy-but-floats c5:** the physics and reveal text are right, but the stage draws the floating ball mirrored (cy sign). At 800 cm³ it shows 37.5% submerged, not the stated 62.5%. At 550 and 600 cm³ it shows 9% and 17% submerged. Only 1000 cm³ is right, which is the only frame in the QA screenshot.
- **same-sugar-more-water c6:** the claim says "about 7 dots" in the bottom 100 mL at 300 mL. The stage (seed 4242) shows 6. The exact value is 6.67, so "6 or 7" is the honest statement.
- **the-tagged-molecule c4:** the reveal says "changed type N times in T ticks", but a tag added later (or the original removed) only covers fewer than T ticks. The hint invites tagging other molecules, so this is reachable in normal play.

**Fixes for demo-builder** (claim text changes it also owns)
1. heavy-but-floats: change the floating position to `cy = SURF + (capDepth(rho/RHO_W) - 1) * r`, then re-QA at 550, 600 and 800 cm³.
2. same-sugar-more-water: reword c6 to "20, 10, 6 or 7, 5 and 4", or change the dot placement.
3. the-tagged-molecule: store a start tick per tag and say "in the N ticks since you tagged it", or start every history at tick 0.
4. Source and wording notes, none disputed:
   - water-follows-the-crowd c3: the source arithmetic says 0.05 and 0.15 mol; it should be 0.10 and 0.30.
   - pennies-dont-add-up c7: the Fowler PoEAA citation could not be read offline, so soften or replace it.
   - huffman-by-merging c2: "8 symbols" reads like an 8-letter alphabet; it means an 8-symbol message.
   - freezer-balloon c6: "long before" is loose for helium (liquid at 4.2 K).
   - squeeze-the-brown-gas c3: 31% is 32% in the exact model.
   - half-life c7: "about the same rate" is a stretch in the roughly 10% of runs where the 4th-step share is 64% or more.
   - when-the-water-is-full: the stage shows 0 g dissolved before Stir, which could suggest salt only dissolves when stirred.

**Confidence.** High on everything numeric: I recomputed it independently, and seeded claims were re-run across 200 to 500 seeds. Seeds 1, 20 and 4242 turned out typical rather than flattering. Medium on a few sources I could only check second-hand because the sandbox has no network: Hajdas 2021 (14C dating limit), Fowler's Money pattern, and the sucrose density values, which are from memory. The magnitudes of those still hold.

**Next move.** demo-builder makes the three fixes above, then qa-tester re-runs QA for heavy-but-floats. A different fact-checker then re-checks the three disputed claims and sketch-the-counts c6. - physics.flour-on-the-moon.c2: the cited source does not contain the numbers shown. The trust sheet cites the NASA Planetary Fact Sheet for Mars 3.71 and Jupiter 24.79 m/s². Search summaries of that sheet give Mars 3.73 and Jupiter 25.92 (mean), 23.12 (equatorial) and 27.01 (polar) at 1 bar. 24.79 is the ESA/Wikipedia figure and 3.71 comes from other references. The values are within the published range, so the physics is fine; the attribution is wrong. I could not reach NASA hosts from the sandbox.

**Seed re-runs**

body:
Fact-check of probability/ and life/ is finished: 44 lessons, 4 sets of claims left open. I disputed one claim (herd-immunity c10) and added one unverified claim (friends-have-more-friends c5). `npm run check` passes (the herd-immunity dispute shows as a warning). Every number was re-computed in `artifacts/scratch/fc-problife/`, and seed-based claims were re-run over 200 to 20,000 other seeds. Every seeded result matched its ledger entry and was typical of the seed spread, apart from the stage-text notes below.

| Domain | Lessons | Verified | Disputed | Added |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| probability | 22 | 105 | 0 | 1 (friends-have-more-friends c5, unverified) |
| life | 22 | 105 | 1 (herd-immunity c10) | 0 |

Review files are at `company/reviews/<slug>/2026-10-13-fact-check.md` for all 44. Each lesson's `meta.json` was saved before I started the next. Still open: herd-immunity c10 (disputed) and friends-have-more-friends c5 (unverified).

**Disputed**
- **life.herd-immunity.c10** ("at 80% immune each step is usually smaller than the one before"): false per step. Over 20,000 simulated outbreaks, 17.5% of steps are strictly smaller, 57% equal and 26% larger. What is true: 0.79 new cases per case on average, and 96.9% of outbreaks fizzle at 16 people or fewer. The reveal text is accurate; only the ledger claim is too strong.

**Fixes routed to demo-builder** (all non-blocking except the first)
1. Reword herd-immunity c10 to the 0.8-per-case and about-97%-fizzle wording above, then have an independent checker re-check it.
2. coin-gap-keeps-growing: the reveal's "every run ended between 49.0% and 50.9%" holds only for seed 1713. Over 300 other seeds all 20 shares stay inside 49% to 51% in only 42% of seeds. The stage's 1,000-flip average is 16, while the reveal quotes the exact 25.
3. friends-have-more-friends: "wherever friend counts differ" is only strictly true for connected networks. A separate triangle plus a separate four-person group where everyone knows everyone gives equality. Added as c5; I did not verify it because I wrote it.
4. one-in-a-million-match: the reveal says "Your search found 5" from a chosen seed. Add the spread; 93% of searches find 2 to 9.
5. Small wording and source fixes:
   - plus-fifty-minus-forty c5: "their average $430" means all 50 players.
   - hidden-carriers c2: ledger says "1 in 50", stage says "1 in 51".
   - dish-runs-out: "stopped" is really "levelled off" (91.5 million at 10 hours).
   - natural-selection c10: add "if the drought selects every generation".
   - spreaders-are-rare: "no case above 7" holds only for the expected-shape picture.
   - antibiotic-already-there c3: cites Drake (1991), a loose fit for per-drug frequencies.
   - same-average-different-ride c6: the source's batch numbering is off by one.
   - Disclose whether seeds were chosen for armour-where-no-holes c2 and coin-gap-keeping-growing c4.

I did not open the Rosenzweig, Feller, Longsworth or Gotelli citations or the Pauly and Christensen paper itself; I verified those claims from the arithmetic, search results and the claims' own logic. Sources I did check by search: Casscells 1978, the kidney-stone data, Tversky and Kahneman, and He and Hubbell.

Fact-check of ai, economics and geography is finished: all 54 lessons with open claims were checked. 4 claims are disputed or still unverified for substantive reasons, and `npm run check` passes (188 lessons, 1032 claims).

Each lesson's meta.json and `company/reviews/<slug>/2026-10-13-fact-check.md` were saved before starting the next. Seeded claims were re-run over 200 to 20,000 seeds.

| Domain | Lessons | Verified | Disputed | Added (unverified) | Left open |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ai | 22 | 107 | 0 | 8 | 0 |
| economics | 21 | 118 | 1 | 1 | 0 |
| geography | 11 | 59 | 0 | 0 | 1 |

The added claims are ai.background-shortcut.c5, border-follows-point.c5, clicks-not-value.c5, draw-the-xor-lines.c5, gradient-descent.c11, penalty-on-wiggle.c5, temperature-reshapes.c8 and economics.two-bets-split.c7. A different checker must verify these.

**Disputed**
- **economics.flour-shock.c4:** the stage numbers are right (price rises by half the cost). The source note states the pass-through rule backwards: in price-per-loaf slopes it is demand slope over the sum, not supply slope over the sum. The note is learner-visible under "Why trust this?".

**Left unverified**
- **geography.half-of-humanity.c1:** I could not open the UN WPP 2024 table. Searches confirm the ranking and a world total of about 8.2 billion, but not the 15 figures, and my memory is not independent of the builder's. A human with access to population.un.org/wpp must compare them.
- **geography.half-of-humanity.c2:** I verified it, but only as arithmetic given c1. The conclusion that seven countries are needed survives errors of about 3%.

**Fixes for demo-builder (wording, none blocking)**
- **border-follows-point:** "moves the decision for every spot around it" overstates. Nudging one point changed only 0.8% of the plane in a 6-point test.
- **draw-the-xor-lines:** "a band between them" holds only for parallel lines. 36 of the 54 solving settings are crossing lines, which give wedges.
- **penalty-on-wiggle:** "nearly flat" at λ=10 is loose; the curve keeps a median 37% of the data's range. "A moderate penalty beats none" holds for λ from 1e-4 to 0.1 (91–94% of data sets each) but only 48% at λ=1.
- **temperature-reshapes:** "a hot model is not more inventive" needs a source or softer wording.
- **gradient-descent:** "Crawling: the hops are tiny" is generous at step size 0.15.
- **two-bets-split:** "the losses left are small ones" is true only from 4 bets on.
- **momentum-sweet-spot:** the best momentum is about 0.67 (10 steps), not 0.8, so "sweet spot" should not imply 0.8.
- **mercator-greenland c4:** the source note's "readout 10.73x" is stale. The measured stretch is about 16×, and "more than ten times" still holds.
- **coastline-ruler:** "for exactly this reason" should be "largely".
- **longer-loan-cost:** the exact payment drop is $94.49, so "about $95" could say $94.

**Routing**
- **Walkthrough harness (qa-tester):** the transcript for half-of-humanity never reached the reveal because it tapped 6 countries and half is crossed at the 7th. The lesson works; the harness step budget needs raising.
- **continental-jigsaw c1:** I verified it from the geometry (+57° about 44°N, 30.6°W puts the Brazil bulge in the Gulf of Guinea). The exact Bullard et al. pole and angle match my memory but I could not open the paper, so it is worth a one-minute human look at Table 1.

I did not touch Demo.tsx or claim text, and did not write progress.md or board entries.

I looked at every phone screenshot and changed each lesson once after looking. tsconfig.json is restored.

| slug | prediction → answer (re-computed in node) | claims | QA |
|---|---|---|---|
| pinhole-flips-the-world | flame appears → upside-down; 10 cm × 15/30 = 5.0 cm | 5 | pass |
| throw-it-fast-enough | slowest throw that never lands → ~7.9 km/s (√gR = 7906 m/s; from the 10 km peak, 7899) | 5 | pass |
| sticky-cart-merge | 2 kg at 3 m/s sticks to 1 kg → 2 m/s (kinetic energy 9 J → 6 J) | 4 | pass |
| brick-on-its-side | pull on the 1/3-area face → ~7.8 N (7.85) | 5 | pass |
| add-a-parallel-bulb | battery current → 2.0 A | 5 | pass |
| kettle-vs-bulb-kwh | which uses more → bulb, 0.12 vs 0.10 kWh | 4 | pass |
| ramp-same-work | push on the 4 m ramp → 122.6 N; work 490.5 J | 4 | pass |
| iss-gravity-still-there | gravity at 400 km → ~90% (88.5%) | 6 | pass |
| ball-at-the-top | acceleration at the top → 9.81 m/s² down (v = +0.97 / −1.00 m/s at 1.4 / 1.6 s) | 5 | pass |
| fall-distance-squares | distance after 3 s → 44.1 m (strips 4.9 / 14.7 / 24.5 m) | 4 | pass |

Every brief's answer held when re-computed. All claims are `unverified` and every status is "review".

Where I departed from a brief (each one is written up in that lesson's `company/reviews/<slug>/build.md`):
- **throw-it-fast-enough:** launched from exactly ground level, every slower throw lands at once, so I added a 10 km peak with heights drawn 40× and labelled. I reworded the question to "slowest throw that never lands", because 79 km/s also never lands.
- **kettle-vs-bulb-kwh:** the brief's power × time rectangles came out a few pixels wide on a phone. I replaced them with kWh bars built from one slice per minute.
- **Pinhole:** I raised the candle from 6 cm to 10 cm so it can be read on a phone; that height is labelled illustrative in claim c3.
- **Buttons or sliders instead of the brief's slider, drag or tap-three-times design:** iss uses height buttons, fall uses a 1–4 s slider, and pinhole uses sliders instead of dragging. The reason is that QA presses each control once.

For the fact-checker:
- **ISS speed:** the throw lesson's c5 says 7.7 km/s (computed). NASA's rounded figure, 17,500 mph, is 7.8 km/s.

Things the platform-engineer or evaluation-steward should know (no kit changes were needed):
1. QA waits only 450 ms after each control press. Any milestone that depends on an animation finishing, while that animation disables the controls after it, fails. That is what broke sticky-cart-merge on its first run. The demo standard says "~5 s per control" and should say 450 ms.
2. Port 3655 already had another server on it that returned 404 for every lesson, so I ran QA on QA_PORT=3671.
3. I did not write the `company/ops/progress.md` handoff, because the brief barred edits to company/ops.

Next step: the fact-checker should verify the 47 claims across the 10 lessons, then evaluators (borrowed-mind reviews) should look at each lesson.

| gauss-staircase | revise | The prediction can be answered by adding 1 to 10 directly; the screenshot is mid-animation. |
| minus-times-minus | launch | The stepping-line picture works; the reveal's distributive algebra is unearned. |
| nines-without-end | revise | The "All of them, forever" button just declares 0.999… = 1, and it is reachable after a single zoom. |
| no-fraction-fits | revise | The near-misses can reinforce "it will hit eventually"; the parity proof is not prepared by anything on stage; labels are clipped. |
| odd-numbers-make-squares (v2) | launch | The prediction is answerable by quick arithmetic; otherwise the L-shape picture earns the reveal. |

| one-recipe-for-sixty | revise | The hook telegraphs "no"; generalising to every number rests on one case. One claim is still unverified in meta.json. |
| paths-by-adding | revise | About 16 taps are needed to reach the key state; the first four taps show no adding. |
| plus-and-minus-chips | revise | The prediction is solvable by plain 5 − 3, and TOTAL shows 2 after the first cancel. |
| product-plus-one | revise | "Remainder 1" is claimed but never shown. The lock behaves correctly: the 13 step is the key state. |
| scoops-in-three-cups | launch | Minor: the fraction buttons lack a "cup" unit; the reveal generalises beyond unit fractions. |
| seventy-two-doubling | revise | The hook gives away that 12.5 is wrong; 72 is unexplained; the chart is cramped and the "doubled" tag clips. |
| steeper-is-not-taller | revise | The reveal quotes the 4-across case, but the reveal opened without the learner visiting it. |
| tear-the-corners | revise | The tearing and moving is never shown, only the end state; the "why" needs parallel-line facts the learner lacks. |
| thirteen-pigeons | revise | The locked reveal gives no hint what unlocks it, and about 13 taps are needed; the badge meaning is ambiguous. |
| two-squares-become-one | revise | The area 25 is stated, not found; the hook says "four triangles" but the reveal says "three". |

First, no-fraction-fits: I first doubted the reveal's "13 values of q you tried", then found it is computed from the values the slider actually passed through, so it is likely accurate and I downgraded it. body:
I reviewed all 22 physics lessons that had a walkthrough transcript. The two v2 lessons (pendulum-period, projectile-angle) were reviewed again because their 2026-10-12 reviews do not name a version. Each review is at company/reviews/<slug>/2026-10-13-learner-adult-beginner.md, was saved before I started the next lesson, and is added to that lesson's meta.json evidence.simulatedLearner. I did the artifact section first, then read meta.json. No servers were started.

| Lesson | Verdict | Top finding |
|---|---|---|
| ambulance-pitch-drop | revise | "Crest" and "Hz" are never introduced; the reveal gives 754, 755 and "about 755" for the same value |
| build-a-balanced-mobile | revise | Last screen shows the lump off while the reveal talks about the loaded ruler; "turns the beam equally" is unexplained |
| clay-boat | revise | The deep cup shows 0.56 L pushed aside but "holds back 0.80 L", and the two are never joined |
| coaster-track-shape | revise | v = √(2gh) appears with g and h undefined; "faster" is ambiguous between speed and time |
| count-the-thunder | revise | "µs" is unexplained; the reveal's 6 s case sits beside a screen stuck at 15 s |
| crumple-zone-stopping-time | revise | The prompt says set 0.20 s, but the run never lands on it; "momentum" and "N·s" are on the first screen |
| current-same-around-loop | revise | The caption "same at every spot" appears at the first slide and gives away the answer; the between-bulbs spot was never tested |
| doubling-speed-braking | revise | The 60 km/h case the question asks about never appears; the "energy" justification is only asserted |
| dropped-vs-fired-ball | revise | Balls are unlabelled; the reveal was not reached (driver limit), so I could not judge it |
| flour-on-the-moon | revise | Mass and weight are one word in everyday speech; the bathroom-scale line contradicts "1 kg stays 1 kg" |
| lifeguard-fastest-path | revise | The reveal's 23.4 s at 56 m was never shown; the light and refraction claim is borrowed, not shown |
| light-at-double-distance | revise | The hook says light is "lost" while the lesson shows it is spread; the 2 m case was never visited |
| moon-hammer-feather | revise | One tap only and no reveal (driver limit); "Air: off" reads as a status but is a toggle |
| pendulum-period (v2) | revise | The reveal gate was not assessed; the question's 2 kg may not be reachable |
| projectile-angle (v2) | revise | A stale caption stays on screen while viewing the 70/20 pair; 30/60 was never tried |
| puck-on-ice-no-push | revise | Pucks started at different times, so "Low" ends up ahead of "None" |
| push-the-swing-in-time | revise | Text says "red dots" but the dots on screen are green; only one rhythm was tried |
| release-the-spinning-ball | **launch** | Persistent straight trails earn the reveal; the string's pull has no arrow, and the outward feeling of whirling is not addressed |
| same-push-twice-the-mass | revise | The 4 kg case the prompt names was never visited; "speeds up by" (acceleration) is introduced without explanation |
| skydiver-speed-limit | revise | The reveal says "at 10 s you saw 42.3 m/s" but that was never shown; the mass slider's counterintuitive effect is unexplained |
| truck-hits-car-force | revise | The reveal says the car's velocity "reversed", but the final screen shows its arrow still pointing right |
| two-ripples-cancel | **fatal** | See below |

**FATAL: two-ripples-cancel.** The reveal is reachable without ever seeing the key state. In the last explore frame "Show me why" is live, yet the learner has seen only 1.4×, 2.0× and single-speaker 1.0×, never silence. The reveal then states "the sound dropped to silent". The stage also draws only crests, so "crest meets trough" has no visual.

**Driver limits, not marked fatal.** In dropped-vs-fired-ball, moon-hammer-feather, pendulum-period, projectile-angle, puck-on-ice-no-push and push-the-swing-in-time the reveal never unlocked. I treated that as a driver limit, since the screenshots do not show the gate is unreachable. Each review says what a rerun must confirm. Pendulum-period and projectile-angle need a rerun that uses the exact values the question names.

**Pattern across lessons.** In several lessons the question or reveal names a value the explore never visited. These are crumple-zone, doubling-speed-braking, light-at-double-distance, same-push-twice-the-mass, skydiver, lifeguard and projectile-angle. The slider steps may not reach those values, which is worth the builders checking.

**Next move.** The demo-builder or learning-designer should revise two-ripples-cancel so the reveal requires the quiet spot, then dispatch a rerun of the walkthrough driver for the six lessons above. The evaluation-steward owns triage.

Confidence is moderate, since this is simulated-learner critique from transcripts and three screenshots per lesson. It is not evidence that anyone learned.

- **Claims:** every claim is "unverified", meta status is "review", builder is "demo-builder". Build notes are in `company/reviews/<slug>/build.md`.
- **Checked by eye:** I looked at the phone screenshots and fixed one round of layout problems (clipped labels, overlaps). I also took extra screenshots of states QA doesn't reach, which caught the water molecule's oxygen covering its shared electron pair.
