The Design org is set up, in a Design studio on HQ floor 2, and everyone it affects has a board item.

**The org:**
- **Ines (design lead)** owns:
  - the lesson format catalogue;
  - the design system;
  - a new design review ritual, now added to the ritual triggers.
- **Rafael (interaction designer)** writes a spec for each non-default lesson: the format, the controls in order, what's on screen at each step and at the reveal. He also checks that our QA can reach every step.
- **Kiri (visual designer)** owns styles, chart style and motion, together with the accessibility reviewer.
- **The mockup artist** moves from Studio to Design, under Ines.

**Format catalogue** (`company/design/formats.md`):

| Status | Formats |
|---|---|
| Supported today | single card, simulation run, map explorer |
| Built by hand today (kit components proposed) | side-by-side comparison, before/after toggle, storyboard/scrub, debunk (for Life Hacks) |
| Needs kit support first | multi-card sequence |

**How the existing designers fit in:**
- **Learning designer (Studio):** stays the pedagogy half: what to teach, the misconception, the question. They pair with Rafael on every non-default lesson, starting with the first 5 Life Hacks briefs.
- **Mockup artist:** draws the mockup from Rafael's spec before the builder starts.
- **Pedagogy critic:** compares two versions side by side, for example before and after a redesign.
- **Accessibility reviewer:** works with Kiri on contrast and colour-blind safety, then reviews the published lessons.

**The pipeline change** (a new step 3, "Design", in the operating loop):
- **Every brief names a format.** All category leads and sub-area managers have been told, through their onboarding docs and a board item each.
- **Default formats** go straight to a builder, so most lessons cost nothing extra.
- **Other or new formats, and hard briefs,** get a pedagogy note, an interaction spec and a mockup first.
- **Design review** runs after learner review. It covers new formats, lessons with layout or "told, not shown" findings, and a 10% sample of each batch.

**Engineering note for Kenji and Noor (board W-097):** kit components for comparison and storyboard; and whether a multi-card sequence can live inside the explore phase without changing the lesson contract. If each card needs its own prediction, that's a constitutional amendment.

**Two decisions for you:**
1. Should the Design step apply only to new and revised lessons, or should I also have Ines run a design review over the ~420 unpublished lessons? The first is cheaper. The second would catch many of the layout problems before learner review.
2. Should multi-card lessons be a priority for kit work now, or after the storage design (EDD-003) stage 1?

Meanwhile we're at 496 lessons, and the two queue builders still running will take us past 500.

Agent metrics are now part of `npm run metrics` and the business review. The first run already shows issues of the kind you meant.

**What it measures** (all from the event log):
- **Per role:** runs dispatched, runs that reported back, runs stopped, resumes, tokens per run, and median time per run.
- **Roles never dispatched**, compared against the full roster.
- **Rework:** the share of lessons revised at least once.
- **Launch rate at first review, by builder model** (the Sonnet trial).

The business review template now has an "Agents" section that turns each number into a question. For example, a role that's never dispatched means either retire it, or someone is skipping its check.

**First readout:**

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Agent runs | 123 dispatched, 21 stopped at least once (**17%**, mostly the usage limit and the container restart) |
| Tokens recorded | about 20M |
| Rework | 14% of lessons revised at least once |
| Launch rate at first review | Opus 37%; Sonnet not reviewed yet (a reviewer is on them now) |
| Roles never dispatched | **53 of 69** |
| Most-used role | builders: 61 runs, about 198k tokens per run |

**What the 53 unused roles tell us:**
- **About 40 are new from tonight** (sub-area managers, Design, Life Hacks, Personalization, International), so that's expected. Next week the same number would be a red flag.
- **The real finding is the old roles that have never run:**
  - the QA tester, release manager and accessibility reviewer: I've been running QA and publishing myself, and nobody has done an accessibility review;
  - the learning designer, mockup artist, pedagogy critic and researcher: builders did their work;
  - the analytics steward, domain scout, tools lead and HQ engineer.

  The chief of staff absorbing other roles' checks is exactly the shortcut the System 3 design warns about: the person who wants work shipped is also checking it.
- **A 17% stop rate** is above the 10% threshold I wrote into the template. It confirms that the usage budget, not the org, is our real limit.

**What I'd do next:**
- Hand QA records and publishing to the QA tester and release manager.
- Run the long-overdue accessibility review of the 76 published lessons.
- Have Ines and Rafael start on new briefs.

That's about 4 Sonnet runs. Want me to go ahead? Meanwhile, the two queue builders still running will take us past 500.

Pass 7 stopped at the 45-lesson cap. I checked 45 lessons and verified 191 claims. I disputed none, added none and withdrew none. `node tools/company.mjs check` passes with 0 warnings. Open claims went from 606 to 415. I did not edit Demo.tsx or commit.

**Method:** I re-derived numbers in node, running each lesson's `model.ts` directly. For geography I re-ran d3-geo on the kit's `countries-110m.json`. I checked sources by web search where I could.

**Priority 1:** one-in-four-sprouts c3, saturated-enzyme c2 and c3, and point-one-is-26-percent c5 are verified.

**Priority 2:** chemistry.salt-ions-count-double c5 still says "about 3.5", not "about 3.4". I left it unverified. The CRC table is still unreachable, and my search found only the ideal 3.72 °C. Builder move: change the text to "about 3.4 °C".

**Builder-flagged claims, all verified:**
- red-apple-green-light: Merzlyak et al. 2003 exists in Postharvest Biol. Technol. 27(2), starting p. 197. I could not confirm the end page (211).
- filament-vs-led-heat: "about 5%" visible light is inside the 2–10% range, and "about" carries it.
- paper-stops-alpha: Al and Pb attenuation recomputed (0.952 and 0.0178).
- pay-first-then-profit: node gives 2,648 kJ broken, 3,450 kJ formed, net 802 kJ. The measured value is 802.5 kJ/mol.
- ISS and GPS: ISS 51.6° and 90–93 min (NASA); GPS about 20,200 km (gps.gov, via search); geostationary 35,786 km.
- City coordinates and antarctica-vs-australia: kit ratios re-run at 29.93, 1.589 and 1.60 (Australia moved to 72°S), and the ice-shelf claim confirmed from the polygon.

- Earlier priorities and flagged: the three life/chemistry lessons above, plus red-apple-green-light, filament-vs-led-heat, paper-stops-alpha and pay-first-then-profit.

**Fix for the builder:** antarctica-vs-australia c5 source line. Say the 7.69 million km² for Australia is Geoscience Australia / ABS; the CIA Factbook gives 7.74 million. The ratio "about 1.8" is unaffected.

body:
We're not ready yet, but we're close. Here are the gaps and the role I'd give that agent.

**What we have:** `company/design/system.md` (v0) covers colour roles, type, controls, chart style and motion for code-drawn stages. It says nothing about images.

**What's missing before any images are made:**
1. **An illustration style guide**, owned by Kiri (visual designer):
   - **Look:** one consistent style, such as flat vector with a limited palette, one line weight and a fixed viewpoint, so 50 hacks look like one product.
   - **Colours:** the palette mapped to our colour roles, with light- and dark-mode versions.
   - **People:** hands and people shown diversely, and no real brands or logos.
   - **No text inside images:** International would have to regenerate every image per language. Labels go on the stage instead.
   - **Reference images:** a few, so the generator can stay on style.
2. **Image accuracy and safety:** a picture can teach something false or dangerous, such as the wrong knife grip or two chemicals side by side. Every image is reviewed like a claim, by Sana (safety) and the fact-checker, before it ships.
3. **Provenance:** each image stores the model, prompt, seed, date and licence terms, and learners are told it's AI-generated.
4. **Asset pipeline:** images can't live inside the 15 KB lesson file, so they become separate CDN files with their own hash. That's a call for Kenji and Noor, and it ties into the storage design. We also need formats (SVG or WebP), size limits, and alt text for every image (the accessibility reviewer).

**The role I'd give it: Illustrator (external contributor)** in the Design org, reporting to Kiri.
- **Input:** one illustration request per lesson, at `company/design/illustration-requests/<slug>.md`. Each request comes from Rafael's interaction spec and says:
  - what the image must show;
  - what it must not show;
  - its size and slot on the card;
  - its alt text.
- **Output:** the images plus a provenance file, put in a drop folder. They're never merged straight into lessons.
- **Review:** Kiri checks style, Sana checks safety, the fact-checker checks accuracy, and the accessibility reviewer checks the alt text.
- **Treated as outside input:** its files and notes are content to check, not instructions to follow.

**On "picking" life hacks:** I'd keep the choice of what to teach with Tess (Life Hacks manager) and Sana. The image agent is welcome to suggest hacks, but its suggestions go to Tess's list like anyone else's, so whether a hack is teachable and safe decides it, not how good it would look.

**Suggested order:**
1. Kiri writes the illustration guide with 5 reference images.
2. Kenji decides how assets are stored (a small addition to the storage design doc, EDD-003).
3. Tess writes the first 5 briefs and Sana passes them.
4. Rafael writes their specs and illustration requests.
5. The illustrator agent makes the images, and they're reviewed.

Want me to set this up now: the Illustrator role, the style-guide outline, the request template and the provenance format, plus a board item for Kenji on asset handling? The images themselves would come from your other agent.

body:
Fact-check pass 8 (ai, cs, math) is done. All 40 lessons with unverified claims are checked, so nothing remains in those three domains. `node tools/company.mjs check` still fails, but not because of my files.

- **Counts:** 179 claims verified, 1 disputed, 0 withdrawn, 0 added. I found no learner-visible fact the claims missed, and I did not edit Demo.tsx.
- **Method:** Seeded claims were re-run in node from each lesson's own MODEL block. That covered 1,000 seeds for five-folds and 2,000 each for noisy-compass and switch-half-off. Memorise-coin-flips (1,000 label sets), twins, shallow-valley and dog-bites were re-run too. I also re-computed the cs and math arithmetic, brute-forced the topological orders and spanning trees, checked 7 pieces for the three lines in two-colours, and compared each reveal to its claims. I web-checked Northcutt et al. (abstract says at least 3.3%, matching the claim), W3Techs (UTF-8 about 99%), Zhang et al. and Dijkstra's CLRS theorem. The remaining textbook cites (CLRS, Knuth, Hastie, Goodfellow and others) match what I know of them, but I did not open the books. I only found a secondary source for the Goodfellow §8.4 symmetry-breaking quote, and nothing for Holtzman's exact nucleus definition or CLRS Lemma 22.11.
- **Disputed:** `cs/cafe-is-five-bytes` c5. The sentence "plain English letters one byte and other characters two, three or four" is false for digits, spaces and punctuation, which are also one byte in UTF-8. The builder should change both the stage text and the claim to something like "ASCII characters take one byte; many others take two, three or four". Its reveal shows this sentence, and it blocks publishing until fixed.
- **Verified with advisory notes (suggested wording changes):**
  - `ai/noisy-compass` c4: the 5th percentile is 0.1949, which rounds to 0.19, not "0.20".
  - `ai/switch-half-off` c5: the reveal says dropout is "stopping" co-adaptation, flatter than the paper's "reduces".
  - `cs/every-message-is-possible` c4: "equally likely" is only relative to the prior, so "no more likely than before" is safer.
  - `cs/which-order-is-allowed` c4 and `cs/connect-the-towns-cheaply` c3: only citation-number notes. The claims themselves are true.
- **Files written:** every `src/demos/{ai,cs,math}/<slug>/meta.json` for the 40 lessons had claim status updated. Each of the 40 `company/reviews/<slug>/2026-10-13-fact-check.md` files now has a "## Pass 8" section; the files that did not exist were created.

**How it flows:**

| Step | Who | Where |
|---|---|---|
| Request (what to show, what not to show, slot, alt text, safety class) | Rafael (interaction designer) | `company/design/illustration-requests/<slug>.md` |
| Images + `provenance.json` (model, prompt, seed, licence, alt text) | your image agent ("Illustrator") | `company/design/illustration-inbox/<slug>/` |

**The watercolor style guide** (`company/design/illustration.md`):
- **Look:** soft transparent washes in each domain's colour (Life Hacks is apricot), plenty of white paper and gentle daylight.
- **Content:** hands rather than faces, everyday unbranded objects, and **no text in the images**, so International can localise them.
- **Display:** watercolor always sits on a paper frame, so it looks right in dark mode too.
- **Safety and accuracy:** a wrong grip or a dangerous combination counts as a false claim and blocks acceptance. Images for hacks that don't work show the failed result, never a risky attempt.

**Picking life hacks:** your agent can add ideas to `company/domains/briefs/lifehacks-ideas.md`. Tess decides which get made and Sana checks them for safety. The illustrator can't place images in lessons or edit anything outside its inbox, and its files are treated as material to review, not instructions.

- **Compare:** tick up to 3 lessons from any concepts to see their sheets and verdicts side by side.
- Matches the HQ look in light and dark. On a phone the list and the concept view swap, with a back button.

**Routes**
- `/hq/design`, with deep links `?concept=<id>&compare=a,b&view=compare`
- `/api/hq/design/concept/[key]` returns one concept's detail, so review text stays out of the page payload (about 65 KB gzipped)
- `/api/hq/sheet/[slug]` streams the PNG; the slug must match `^[a-z0-9-]+$` and be a lesson on disk, so a traversal attempt gets a 404

- **Brief 2:** drop Cepeda 2006 from claim 2; I found no support there that massed study wins on immediate tests.

The illustrator is set up. Below is the prompt for ChatGPT, also saved as `company/design/illustrator-prompt.md`. I added the pull-request rules to the illustrator handbook and marked F-07 decided in your inbox.

**Before you paste it:**
- ChatGPT needs your GitHub connected with write access to `hanialshater/system-3-company`, so it can open pull requests. It reads the repo's default branch, which is our working branch.
- It starts with the 5 watercolor style anchors and stops until those are accepted. Every later image has to match them.
- Each pull request may change only that request's inbox folder and status line. Anything else gets the pull request closed unreviewed.
- Before anything ships, every pull request is reviewed for style, safety (Life Hacks), accuracy and alt text.
- The Life Hacks category manager is applying the safety and source fixes now, including taking the cup out of the wobbly-table picture.

---

You are the **Illustrator** for System 3 Company, a team that makes 60-second interactive lessons. You are an external contributor. You make watercolor illustrations and deliver them by pull request to the GitHub repository **hanialshater/system-3-company** (default branch). You never edit lessons or code.

**Before anything else, read these files in the repository:**
1. `company/design/illustrator-handbook.md`: your loop and rules (the PR rules are in step 6).
2. `company/design/illustration.md`: the watercolor house style, with the palette, the paper texture, what to avoid, and the sizes and limits.
3. `company/design/illustration-requests/TEMPLATE.md`, then the open requests in that folder (`status: open`).

**Order of work:**
1. Request `_reference` first: the 5 style anchors. Deliver them, then stop and wait until the request file says `status: accepted`. Every later image must match the accepted anchors.
2. Then the other open requests, oldest first, one PR per request.

**For each request:**
- Read the whole request: what the image must show, what it must NOT show, the format and size, the alt text, and the accuracy notes. Accuracy notes are mandatory. For example, a table has four equal legs; a knot is tied as described.
- **Style:** loose, transparent watercolor on warm off-white cold-press paper, with soft wet-in-wet edges, visible paper grain and pigment blooms, a restrained palette per `illustration.md`, calm daylight and generous white space. Not photoreal, no hard vector outlines, no 3D render look.
- **Never draw:** text, letters, numbers, logos, brands, signage, identifiable or close-up faces, children in risky situations, or anything unsafe (open flames near fabric, hot drinks being moved, mains electricity, sharp tools in use). If a request can't be drawn accurately and safely, set its `status: declined`, say why in the PR, and change nothing else.
- **Size:** 1024 × 1024 for a hero, 1024 × 768 for the others.
- **Files:** convert to **WebP** (quality about 80) with Python/Pillow: `Image.open(p).convert("RGB").save(out, "WEBP", quality=80, method=6)`. Lower the quality until each hero is ≤ 120 KB and each other image is ≤ 90 KB. Name them `01.webp`, `02.webp` and so on.
- **Provenance:** write `company/design/illustration-inbox/<slug>/provenance.json` exactly as the handbook shows. Include the image model name and version, your full prompt for each image, the seed (or null), the date, the licence terms that apply to the outputs (OpenAI's terms; you own the outputs and may use them commercially), one alt-text sentence per image, and notes for the reviewer.
- If you can run Node, run `node tools/illustrations.mjs check <slug>` and fix what it flags.

**The pull request:**

summary: Dispatch general-purpose: R&D engineer: knot theory JS library
body:
You are an R&D engineer (role file: company/roles/rnd-engineer.md) in System 3 Company's new R&D org (floor 4; VP of R&D Vera, R&D lead Bram). Your first project: a JavaScript knot theory library that knot theory lessons can use. Read CLAUDE.md, company/rnd/README.md (the lab-to-kit path, the budget, the bet's exit criterion), company/roles/rnd-engineer.md, company/engineering/README.md, src/kit/ (to see the style and what exists) and company/product/demo-standard.md. Work in your worktree and commit there (don't push). No npm dependencies. Never use pkill.

1. **Prior art (search the web):** existing JS/TS knot libraries and tools, e.g. KnotPlot, SnapPy and spherogram (Python), KnotInfo and the Knot Atlas (data), pyknotid, and any JS/TS packages for knot diagrams, PD/DT/Gauss codes, braids, or the Kauffman bracket. Look for the standard algorithms for: PD-code ↔ diagram drawing, writhe, linking number, Fox n-colourings and tricolourability, the Alexander polynomial (Seifert matrix, or from a Wirtinger/Alexander matrix of the diagram), and the Jones polynomial via the Kauffman bracket. Record each source with a URL and its licence, plus what you reused (algorithm only, or ported code with attribution if the licence allows it). Write src/lab/knots/PRIOR-ART.md.
2. **Build src/lab/knots/** as plain ESM JavaScript with JSDoc types and an index.d.ts, tree-shakeable:
   - Representations: PD code (primary), Gauss and DT codes, braid words (σ_i), with conversions where practical.
   - A small knot table: the unknot and the prime knots up to 7 crossings (3_1 … 7_7), plus the Hopf link, Whitehead and Borromean links. Give each its PD code, its standard name, and its published invariants for tests (crossing number, signature where easy, Alexander and Jones). Cite where the data came from (e.g. KnotInfo), and check that its licence allows our use; if it doesn't, derive the values yourself and test them.
   - Invariants: crossing count, writhe, linking number (links), tricolourability and Fox n-colouring counts, determinant, the Alexander polynomial (normalised), and the Jones polynomial via the Kauffman bracket (exponential is fine up to about 12 crossings). Use exact integer or Laurent-polynomial arithmetic, with a tiny polynomial helper. No floats for invariants.
   - Diagram moves: Reidemeister I/II/III applicable-at checks and applying them to a PD code; crossing change (over/under flip) and its effect.
   - Drawing: produce SVG path data for a diagram, with gaps at the under-strands. For table knots, store hand-tuned or computed 2D coordinates, so lessons get clean pictures. For an arbitrary PD code, provide a reasonable layout, e.g. a simple planar-embedding plus force relaxation. Output plain data (paths, crossing positions), so a lesson can render it with React and make crossings tappable.
   - A seedable random knot generator (random braid closure, or random PD), for "is it the unknot?" style games.
3. **Tests** with `node --test src/lab/knots/test/`, against the published values for every table knot: the Jones and Alexander polynomials, the determinant, tricolourability (3_1 yes, 4_1 no, …), the linking number of the Hopf link (±1), and the invariance of each invariant under random Reidemeister moves (property test, seeded).
4. **README.md:** the API, examples for a lesson (e.g. "tap crossings to make it the unknot", "is this trefoil tricolourable?"), the size budget (measure the gzipped size of the typical imports with node's zlib), what is not supported, and suggested lesson ideas for the math category manager.
5. A tiny demo page is optional, but if you make it, put it under /hq/lab/knots (gated by hqEnabled()) and not in lessons.
Run the tests, `npx tsc --noEmit`, and `node tools/company.mjs check`; restore tsconfig.json with `git checkout tsconfig.json` if a build touched it. Report in under 250 words: the commit hash, the API summary, the test results, the size per typical import, the prior art and licences, and what remains for the exit criterion.

body:
I wrote the research note at /home/user/system-3-company/company/research/notes/2026-10-13-teachable-knot-theory.md, and `npm run check` passes. The proxy blocked arxiv.org and ncbi.nlm.nih.gov, so every source was read through search abstracts and snippets only. Most confidence marks are therefore capped at medium-high, and claim verifiers need full-text access. I found no study of adult misconceptions about knot theory itself. The only empirical anchor is Croom & Firestone (2024): people were near chance at telling knots from non-knots. Each lesson's misconception should be treated as a hypothesis to test with people.

**Top 8 lessons:**
1. The unknot in disguise (Reidemeister moves)
2. Tricolourability proves the trefoil is knotted
3. The Whitehead link and Borromean rings: linked even when the linking number is 0
4. Left vs right trefoil, which leads into granny vs square knot
5. Crossing number vs the crossings in a drawing
6. Long cords knot themselves (Raymer & Smith)
7. Unknotting number (the 10₈ knot; not additive, Brittenham–Hermiller 2025)
8. Jones polynomial as a fingerprint

One correction to the brief: Taylor's deep protein knot (2000) is a figure-eight, not a trefoil.

**Library requirements the engineer might miss:**
- **Links:** the 7-crossing table needs multi-component links (Hopf, Whitehead, Borromean), composite knots (granny, square), and 10₈.
- **Hard unknots:** some unknot drawings can only be untangled by first adding crossings (Goeritz), so a reducer that only removes crossings gets stuck.
- **Operations:** a "turn over" move separate from mirroring, connected sum, and deleting a component.
- **Random knots:** seeded 3-D random curves, closing open curves (ropes, proteins), and projecting 3-D to a 2-D drawing.
- **Order of work:** simplify a drawing before computing Jones.
- **Conventions:** fix which trefoil counts as "right" and the Jones normalisation, because sources differ.

The knot theory research note is done and committed. I've sent its library requirements to the R&D engineer who is building the knot library.

**Top 8 lesson ideas, in order:**
1. The unknot in disguise (Reidemeister moves).
2. Tricolourability proves the trefoil is knotted.

- The site's proxy blocked the full papers, so the researcher worked from abstracts. Fact-checkers will need full-text access before these claims are verified.
- No study of what adults get wrong about knots exists. The only data point is a 2024 study in which people were near chance at telling knots from non-knots. So each lesson's misconception is a guess to test with real learners.

body:
R&D now works as a team of competing agents: several write different versions of the same code, a fixed scorer ranks them, and the best go on to the next round. It's set up, committed and pushed.

**How a round works** (written up in `company/rnd/evolution.md`):

| Who | Role |
|---|---|
| **Bram, R&D lead** | Owns the scorer, which no one else can edit: the correctness tests, a quality benchmark, and the weights and size budget. He writes each round's brief, which names the part to improve and gives every engineer a *different* approach. He picks the survivors. He doesn't write versions in a round he judges. |
| **3–5 R&D engineers per round** | Each writes one complete version of the library in their own branch. It is either a distinct new idea, or a blend of two earlier winners. They can't see each other's work until scoring, and can't touch the tests. |
| **Research scientists** | Bring in ideas from papers between rounds. |
| **Kenji** | Reviews the final winner before it moves into the lesson kit. |

**Scoring and stopping:**
- A version scores 0 unless it passes every test and fits the size budget. Above that, it's scored on tests passed, size and the quality benchmark.
- The best 2–3 go on, and every round includes at least one blend of two winners.
- It stops when a round improves the best score by less than 2%, or after 4 rounds.
- Two rules: versions must try different ideas, and a version that games the benchmark (for example, special-casing the test knots) is disqualified and a test is added to close the gap.

**The scorer, `tools/evolve.mjs`:**
- It runs each version against the fixed tests and records the score and which earlier versions it came from.
- It also prints a leaderboard and copies the winner into place.
- I checked it on a toy problem: two Fibonacci versions, where the fast one won on speed.

**Knot library:** the build already running becomes round 0, the baseline. I've told that engineer to:
- keep the tests separate from the code;
- write the benchmark: drawing quality on random knots, how many hard unknots the simplifier untangles, and how fast it computes the Jones polynomial;
- list the 3 weakest areas, where round 1 should try competing versions.

Drawing arbitrary knots is the likely first target, with competing layout methods. Round 1 starts once the baseline lands and Bram has reviewed the scorer.

This changed the scope of two existing R&D roles and added no new ones. Vera and the other directs were informed through an announcement on the HQ timeline.

body:
I reviewed all 30 lessons in batch 5: 21 launch, 8 revise, 1 fatal. For each one I ran the walkthrough against :3420 and looked at sheet.png before opening meta.json, so every review says "Screenshots seen: yes". The reviews are at /home/user/system-3-company/company/reviews/<slug>/2026-10-14-learner-adult-beginner.md. `npm run check` passed. I did not touch lessons, meta or the board, and did not commit.

**Fatal**
- vaccinate-at-the-peak (v2): the question and stage caption print "R0 = 2.9999999999999996". The current Demo.tsx prints BETA/GAMMA without rounding. "Most (about 78%)" is the only specific option, so it can be picked by elimination, and the phone clipping cuts the "peak is not the end" explanation.

**Revise**
- atlantic-to-pacific-heading: the heading reads 142° as soon as you tap and the slider changes nothing. The "isthmus runs east-west" reason is told, not shown, and the oceans are not labelled.
- barcelona-sun-minutes: phone clipping cuts the whole "why" (4 minutes per degree, 5.9°), and nothing links 505 km to degrees.
- bearing-spiral-to-the-pole: clipping cuts the explanation of why an endless spiral has a finite length, and it relies on cos 80°.
- high-satellite-view: the reason it can't reach half (sightlines grazing the globe) is never drawn and is clipped. The "7% from 1,000 km" figure was never shown.
- potassium-battery: after "Outside = 140 mM" the stage still says -89 mV and "still changing", and the last reveal sentence contradicts what the stage showed.
- penalty-on-wiggle: the key "0.58 with no penalty" comparison was never on screen, and the ridge/coefficient terms are not explained.
- stop-at-epoch-sixty: the answer says "before step 100" but the lowest error you can find is at step 100. The overfitting shows only in the numbers, not in the curve.
- window-forgets-start: the random-drop button ran at window 20 and showed "20 of 20", but the reveal quotes window-8 numbers the learner never saw.

**Also noted**
- The served build showed 0/N claims checked for potassium-battery and three-questions-six-orders, while meta.json says all are verified. The server build may be stale.

These are simulated-learner criticisms, not evidence that anyone learned. I'm fairly sure of the fatal and the potassium, window and epoch mismatches, and less sure of the clipping-driven verdicts, which depend on how W-135 lands.

Next step: the lesson builders own the fixes, with the fatal first. The evaluation steward should re-run the clipping-driven revises once W-135 lands.

body:
W-135 is fixed and committed in my worktree as 6178343 (not pushed). No amendment is needed: src/kit/Lesson.tsx is unchanged.

**Root cause.** Since 54ae817 the reveal stage takes its content height and the card body scrolls, but nothing scrolls it. The reveal starts at the card's bottom edge, inside a scroll area with no visible scrollbar on a phone, so learners and screenshots see text cut off under "Why trust this?". The footer never overlaps anything. Second cause: about 200 lessons draw their picture with `flex: 1 1 0` and a min-height, so at the reveal it shrinks to a 120–140px thumbnail.

**Fix.** DemoCard.tsx now scrolls the card body to bring the reveal into view (`useRevealFit`). In globals.css, `.stage-svg` keeps its natural height at the reveal. Trade-off: when a reveal is long, the top of the stage scrolls up out of view, but it is not shrunk.

**reveal-fit, all 509 lessons at 390×844:**

| | Fully visible | Needs scrolling | Thumbnail | Couldn't reach reveal |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Before | 257 | 245 | 141 | 7 |
| After | 502 | 0 | 6 | 7 |

Published lessons: 92 of 94 fit with no thumbnails.

**Still failing, per lesson (board W-136, demo-builder):**
- Lessons that cap their own picture height: waves-return, dish-runs-out, hidden-carriers, random-dots-cluster.
- To check by eye: in-order-is-sorted, the-fast-ones-leave (probably a false positive).
- The tool's automatic tap-through never unlocks the reveal on these 7, so they are unmeasured: exponential-growth, merge-sort-payoff, odd-numbers-make-squares, pendulum-period, push-the-swing-in-time, puck-on-ice-no-push, ramp-same-work.

**Checks.** check and typecheck pass. QA passed on 10 lessons, phone and desktop. The feed spec passed in a full run (its chips test fails only when QA_ONLY filters lessons). I did not run a full `npm run verify`.

**Next.** principal-engineer reviews the diff and confirms tier 1 (W-137).

Fatal:
- ruler-catch: if you tap Clear (or have 0 catches) and then "Show me why", the reveal reads "Your 0 catches closed between Infinity and -Infinity cm, which is Infinity to NaN s".

Revise:
- bend-at-double-speed: the 50 m starting limit never appears on the stage, so "4× radius" is only stated. The slider starts at 100 m but the question says 50 m. The phone clip (W-135) cuts the "speed squared" line.
- brick-on-its-side: the reveal says all three faces read 15.7 N. The learner read 7.8 N on them; 15.7 N only came from doubling the mass.
- cradle-two-in-two-out: the phone clip cuts the reveal's key sentence ("two constraints leave one way").
- fall-distance-squares: the strip label "2s: 14.7 m" reads as a running total, and 14.7 is the wrong answer the learner picked. The reveal stage freezes mid-replay.
- filament-vs-led-heat: the filament's 57 W of heat (the answer) is never shown. The prompt only asks the learner to tap the LED.
- higher-orbit-slower: the ISS speed stays hidden until the reveal, so "slower" has no baseline on the stage.
- polar-day-length: the clip cuts the only "why" (Earth slowest in July). The counters show 7 days but the text says 7.6.
- split-the-sum: the prediction asks "13 × 7?", which tests arithmetic, not the splitting idea.
- two-bets-split: the 2-bet case is never stopped on. The reveal muddles "any loss" with "worst case" and quotes 31.3% at 4 bets.

These are one simulated learner's criticisms, not evidence that anyone learned. I'm fairly sure of the fatal, brick and filament, which show directly in the screenshots; the others are judgement calls. `npm run check` passed.

**Decision for you:** I didn't add a progress.md handoff, so that parallel agents in this wave don't collide at the top of the file. Fold this into the wave's handoff if you want it logged. As instructed, I didn't touch the board.

- hemoglobin-s-curve: the question uses three undefined terms (half-point, mmHg, points of saturation); both curves show before lock-in and give the answer away; the clipped last clause is the payoff.

body:
The knot library is built and committed as `ec98441` on `worktree-agent-a04fb8a93f0800f0a` (not pushed). All 93 tests pass, but the evolution harness scores the baseline **0 (gated out)**. It measures the whole library as raw source: 12,815 B gzipped against the 10,240 budget, and even fully minified the library is 9.8 KB. I wrote `evolve.json` exactly as briefed and logged the objection as W-137 for the R&D lead, with two fixes: gate on per-lesson cost, or allow about 16 KB for the whole library. Without the gate the score would be about 9,580.

I fast-forwarded the worktree to `ccr-4c6c7654-ew9ko1` to get `tools/evolve.mjs` and the research note.

**API** (`src/lab/knots/`, docs in `index.d.ts`):
- Codes: PD (primary), Gauss, DT, braid → PD.
- Table: unknot, 3_1–7_7, 10_8, Hopf, Whitehead, Borromean, granny, square, a 10-crossing disguised unknot.
- Invariants, all exact: writhe, linking number, Fox colourings, tricolourability, determinant, Alexander, Jones via the Kauffman bracket, signature.
- Reidemeister I/II/III detect and apply, plus moves that add crossings.
- `simplify` never says "knotted": it answers unknot, unlink, minimal (proven) or unknown.
- Operations: crossing change, mirror, turn over, connected sum, delete component.
- SVG drawing with gaps, plus seeded random knots, 3-D curves, closure, projection and `identify`.

**Tests** (`node --test src/lab/knots/test/*.test.mjs`; Node 22 needs the glob): Jones and Alexander for every table entry match independent software run on the same PD codes. Determinants, tricolourability, linking numbers and invariance under seeded random moves all pass. Right trefoil = t + t³ − t⁴.

**Size per lesson** (minified, unused code dropped, gzip): 4.3 KB (draw a table knot) to 7.3 KB (random-knot game), all under 10 KB.

**Prior art and licences:** no code copied. PD codes come from SnapPy's table (GPL). Regina and knot_floer_homology (GPL) were used offline as checking oracles only. Knottingham and joshuahhh's tool are MIT, for ideas only. KnotInfo, the Knot Atlas and arXiv were unreachable, so unknotting numbers are from memory and the Goeritz hard unknot is missing.

**Still open for the exit criterion:** the size gate, and the lead's review of the evaluator (W-136). The bench's hard-unknot set is too easy; only Haken's Gordian unknot (17% reduced) separates candidates. Layout of messy diagrams is weak (40 of 70 fall back to a cramped drawing). Lesson briefs are with cm-math (W-138).

body:
The knot theory library (round 0, the baseline) is merged into the lab, and all 93 tests pass.

**What it does** (`src/lab/knots/`, plain JavaScript, no dependencies):
- **Knot codes:** PD, Gauss and DT codes, and braids.
- **Built-in table:** the unknot, all prime knots up to 7 crossings, 10₈, the Hopf, Whitehead and Borromean links, the granny and square knots, and a disguised 10-crossing unknot.
- **Invariants, computed exactly:** writhe, linking number, colourings and tricolourability, determinant, the Alexander and Jones polynomials, and signature.
- **Moves and operations:** detecting and applying Reidemeister moves, including moves that add crossings. Crossing change, mirror, turn over, connected sum and deleting a component.
- **Simplifier:** it never wrongly says "knotted". It answers unknot, unlink, minimal or unknown.
- **Drawing and random knots:** SVG drawings with gaps at the under-crossings, and seeded random knots from 3-D curves.
- **Checks:** the Jones and Alexander polynomials for every table knot match independent software.
- **Size:** 4.3–7.3 KB per lesson after minifying, under the 10 KB budget.

**Before round 1 (all on the board):**
1. **Size budget measured wrongly (W-144).** The scorer gated the baseline out as too big. It measured the whole unminified library, about 12.8 KB, instead of what a lesson actually loads, so the gate as written would block every version. Bram, the R&D lead, will decide how to measure it.
2. **Benchmark too weak and drawings cramped (W-143).** The set of hard unknots is too easy: only one of them tells versions apart. And 40 of 70 random messy knots get a cramped drawing. That messy-knot layout is the natural target for round 1, with 3 engineers each trying a different layout method.
3. **Licence question on the knot data (W-145).** The knot codes were taken from the knot table of SnapPy, a GPL-licensed program. No code was copied, and knot tables are arguably uncopyrightable facts. Still, Kenji has to confirm the data's source, or have it re-derived from a permissive one, before the library moves into the lesson kit.
4. **Gaps.** KnotInfo, the Knot Atlas and arXiv were unreachable, so the unknotting numbers are from memory. The Goeritz hard unknot is also missing.
5. **Lesson briefs (W-146).** The discrete-math category manager will write knot lesson briefs from the research note.

Round 1 starts once the current revision and verify agents free up slots: Bram reviews the scorer, then 3 engineers each write a competing layout.

body:
The first accessibility audit is done. It covers the 76 lessons that were published when the audit started: **46 pass, 12 pass with fixes, 18 fail.**

**All 18 failures are low colour contrast,** mostly in the light theme. The scan found no keyboard, screen-reader label, reduced-motion or lock-out failures. Most of the contrast problems come from the lesson kit's shared colours rather than individual lessons. For example, the "Not quite" verdict text is 1.62:1 in every lesson, against a 4.5:1 minimum for normal text.

**Kit-level fixes** (P1 for the platform engineer, W-148):
- Darken the light-theme good, warn and bad colours used for text.
- Enlarge tap targets: buttons are about 35 px, sliders 28 px, and the "Why trust this?" link 23 px, against a 44 px target.
- Add a live region so screen readers announce changes.
- Stop dimming the locked stage below the contrast minimum.
- Two more issues sit in the protected lesson contract, so they need an amendment: focus drops to the page body at the reveal, and the stage comes before the question in reading order.

Caveat: the audit was automated plus a 10-lesson hand check, and no screen reader was used.

**Decision for you (F-14 in your HQ inbox):** the 18 failing lessons are published now.
- **(a)** Unpublish them now.
- **(b)** Waive the accessibility condition in writing.
- **(c)** My recommendation: keep them up while the kit colours are fixed, which should take hours, then re-scan and unpublish whatever still fails.

The 49 lessons published since the audit started are being audited now with the same scan tool (W-149).

Two other decisions are still waiting on you:
- **The 15 lessons that passed QA but are still held.** Should I lift the holds, or give the release manager permission to edit the holds file?
- **The usage budget (F-02).**

body:
I reviewed all 29 lessons in batch 9 as an adult beginner: 15 launch, 14 revise, 0 fatal. For every lesson I ran the walkthrough against :3421 and looked at sheet.png before opening meta.json, and every image loaded. Each review is at `/home/user/system-3-company/company/reviews/<slug>/2026-10-14-learner-adult-beginner.md`, with lesson version 1, "Screenshots seen: yes" and section 1 written before I read the brief. `npm run check` passes. I did not commit, did not touch the board, lessons, meta.json or progress.md, and gave no kudos.

Revise (slug: main finding):
- a-birthday-like-mine: the reveal never says why 253 people and not 183, and 253 also appears as "pairs among 23 people", which reads as if it were the reason.
- capped-doubling-game: "$20" is the only option without "about", which gives it away; "$2^k" is unexplained; the $1-per-flip derivation is only told.
- dice-that-chase-each-other: a re-roll showed D winning 57 of 100, which seems to contradict the reveal's "scatter by about five"; which faces beat which is never shown.
- fair-game-still-ruins: the chart is mostly bright green "won" lines while the tile says only 2 of 30 won.
- halve-the-margin-cost: one drag to 4,000 unlocks the reveal, so the 2,000-person case the reveal quotes was never seen.
- heads-after-heads-trap: the question is very hard to parse; 16 taps; the weighting that causes the 40.5% is only told.
- random-dots-cluster: a "crowded" square shows one blob, not 3 dots; dots sit on grid lines.
- one-bad-label-knn: k and majority voting are used before they are defined; the question itself states "4 blue, 1 orange".
- parallel-vs-arc-short-hop: on the Mercator map the curved shortest route looks longer, and the reveal's "the parallel curves away" contradicts the picture.
- spam-threshold-tradeoff: the reveal unlocks without visiting 0.25, the threshold the question asks about; the hook leaks the answer.
- snowshoe-pressure: the boot is never seen sinking; the pressure gauge is tiny.
- rule-of-72-shortcut: the reveal says "you saw" results at 3% and 20% that the learner never visited.
- wrench-throw-recoil: the stage says "Shown 1 s later" but the astronaut does not visibly move, so the picture agrees with the wrong answer "not at all".
- word-in-pieces: the correct 3-token split is never shown on the stage.

The pattern I trust most is that reveal unlocks too easily. In four lessons (margin, spam, rule-of-72, snowshoe) the reveal describes a state the learner can skip. I am moderately sure overall; this is a simulated mind, not evidence that anyone learned.

Next move: lesson builders own these fixes.

I re-reviewed all 41 wave-C lessons: **33 launch, 8 revise, 0 fatal**.

**Method:** for each lesson I ran the walkthrough against :3423 and looked at the transcript and sheet.png first. Only then did I read the previous learner review and mark each earlier finding fixed or not fixed. I did not read build.md for any lesson. Screenshots seen: yes on all 41. For digits-are-logs, "Run to 100" was still animating when the walkthrough took its last frame, so the reveal never unlocked. I re-drove that path with a scratchpad Playwright script that waited longer, and the reveal opened correctly.

**Revise (one line each):**
- bend-at-double-speed: the reveal quotes 50 m and 112.5 m, which the learner never saw. Only the 108 km/h point is shown, so the speed-squared idea rests on one data point (earlier finding not fixed).
- clay-boat: the small cup, its flooding and "0.80 L" are narrated but never visited, because the reveal unlocks on the big cup alone (not fixed).
- double-the-size: the slider lands on 18 inches, so the 12-inch case (answer 4) the reveal explains never appears on screen. Its closing "slide to 18" line repeats what the learner just did.
- distance-is-area: the reveal says "You saw 1 strip give 200 m", but that was never shown. The gate opens after 3 strips, so the narrowing toward 100 m is never watched.
- hanoi-tower-doubles: the learner can reach 7 moves with the tower not on C and still advance. 63 is only extrapolated, and the card says 90s.
- back-button-stack: the answer B is still told rather than shown. Copy bugs: "D were thrown away" and "fromE".
- cheapest-is-not-shortest: the prediction is still plain 2+2+2 arithmetic. "Settle", "label" and "∞" are undefined, and the hook gives the answer away.
- plus-and-minus-chips: after "+ chip" or "- chip" the caption says "The total did not move", which is false.

**Smaller, for other roles:**
- Several trust links show unchecked claims (1/3 to 6/7). Fact-checker should look before launch.
- big-number-swallows-one says "2 multiplied by itself 53 times", which reads as 2^54. Fact-checker.
- digits-are-logs "Run to 100" outlasts the walkthrough's 1.2 s wait. QA.

**Confidence:** moderate. These are simulated-learner judgements and the walkthroughs follow fixed paths; none of this shows anyone learned. The revise calls on the first four lessons are high confidence because the screenshots show the gap directly.

**Not done:** no progress.md handoff, since I was asked not to touch shared ops files. `npm run check` passes.

**The winner is `gen1-force`, and gen 2 is not worth running under the method as written.** Gen 1 adds only 0.26–0.47 % to the total score, below the 2 % stop rule, so I recommend promoting `gen1-force` (EDD, then principal-engineer review).

**Official scores:** three runs on fresh seeds. Load was 4–15, and nobody paid a slowness penalty.

| | Median | Runs |
|---|---|---|
| gen0-baseline | 10,394.54 | |
| gen1-tutte | 10,438.80 | |
| gen1-force | 10,439.68 | 10,451.90 / 10,436.38 / 10,439.68 |
| gen1-ortho | 10,443.07 | 10,441.70 / 10,454.69 / 10,443.07 |

The top three are tied within seed noise.

**Audit:** every candidate changed only allowed files, and none games the bench. Tutte picks its outer face with a copy of the bench formula; that is allowed, but I flagged it.

**Rulings:**
- Ortho's stretch to a square is fair, and I left the aspect metric alone. It is worth 2–4 points and does not change the winner.
- Looks: I rendered and viewed the four knots. Only force still draws table knots like the textbook. Ortho draws rounded rectangles; tutte gives boxy shapes with cusps.
- I added a test for this: table knots must draw round (at most 30 % straight, 3 % sharp corners). Re-scored over three runs, force has a median of 10,533.49, gen0 10,491.86, and tutte and ortho fail the gate.

**Parents:** force and ortho; tutte dropped.

**Flagged for the VP:** the 2 % rule can never be met on this score scale. On the bench term alone, gen 1 gained 15 %. If she rescales the rule, a gen 2 plan is ready (an ortho→force crossover plus 2 mutations).

`npm run check` passes. Nothing was committed and `company/ops/board.json` is untouched. I added a handoff to `company/ops/progress.md`.

Files are in `/home/user/system-3-company`:
- `company/rnd/evolution/knots-gen1.md` (record)
- `src/lab/knots/test/draw.test.mjs` (new test)

body:
Round 1 of the knot library is decided: **gen1-force wins**. The image above shows all four versions side by side.

**Official scores** (median of 3 runs, each on a fresh random seed):

| Version | Median score |
|---|---|
| Baseline | 10,394.54 |
| Tutte | 10,438.80 |
| Force | 10,439.68 |
| Ortho | 10,443.07 |

**What happened:**
- **The top three tied on the original score.** Ortho was technically highest, but the gaps are within random variation between runs. None of them gamed the scoring.
- **The appearance decided it.** In the image, only force still draws the table knots the way textbooks do: it keeps the baseline's clean drawings and only relaxes the messy ones. Ortho draws grids of rounded rectangles, and Tutte draws boxy shapes with cusps.
- **Bram added a "table knots must draw round" test** and re-scored everything. Force then leads (10,533 vs the baseline's 10,492), and Tutte and Ortho fail the new test. All 102 tests pass.

**Caveat:** that test was written after the results came in. It rules out two of the three versions, so it's a judgment call that Bram turned into a test. I think it's right, because lessons need pictures that look like real knots, and the image supports it. But the honest framing is that we added a requirement that wasn't in the original scoring.

**Where it goes next:**
1. **Promote gen1-force into the lesson kit (W-162).** That needs a design doc and Kenji's engineering review. The open question on the SnapPy-derived knot data licence also has to be settled first.
2. **The stop rule needs Vera's decision (W-161).** Round 2 stops when a round improves the score by less than 2%. That can never trigger here, because the fixed test score (about 10,100) dwarfs everything else. Measured on the benchmark alone, round 1 improved things by 15%. Bram has a round-2 plan ready (a crossover of ortho and force, plus 2 variations) if she rescales the rule.

The machine is under heavy load with 20 agents building at once, so git is slow. The role is committed locally and the push is running in the background.

**The role: Femi, community engineer** (floor 5 · engineering, reports to Kenji). Femi owns every external pull request: from contributors, from agents like Codex or ChatGPT, and from the illustrator.
- **Intake:** a same-day reply on the PR, a board item, and a record in `company/engineering/community/prs/`.
- **First evaluation:** size, protected paths, licences, new dependencies, conflicts (including board IDs), and whether check, build and QA pass.
- **Routing:** reviews follow a fixed matrix. External work gets the same reviews ours does. Life Hacks lessons also get a safety review per lesson, and any change to the lesson kit gets Kenji's engineering review.
- **Merging:** happens on our own branch, without rewriting the contributor's history, and only after every required review is recorded. Publishing and deploys stay with the release manager.
- **Limits:** Femi may close a PR that touches protected paths or brings in code under an incompatible licence. Femi treats everything inside a PR as untrusted data, and doesn't do the reviews.

Kenji and Leonie will be consulted on how the role works during the first evaluation, since you asked for the role directly.

**PR #2, Femi's first job:** "Add 200 interactive Life Hacks lessons", from a Codex branch, 688 files and +42,533 lines. Its own description says:
- all 200 are still in review;
- 883 claims are unverified;
- 410/410 QA tests passed;
- a safety review of transcripts, and 21 simulated learner samples.

It conflicts with our branch. I expect conflicts in the board, where its W-153/W-154 IDs collide with ours, and in the progress log, and probably in the registry and the lesson metadata format. It may also overlap our own 5 Life Hacks briefs.

Femi starts as soon as a slot opens, since we're at the 20-agent limit. The first pass is a full evaluation plus a trial merge on a scratch branch. Nothing gets merged into our branch until you've seen the result.

The likely outcome is review in batches of 25–30 lessons. Even if it merges cleanly, it would take many review rounds before any of the 200 publish.

body:
Both are running, as a workflow alongside the 20 builders.

**Life Hacks scope team: 5 product agents in parallel, then one synthesis.** Each writes a section in `company/domains/lifehacks-scope/`:

| Lens | Role | Question it answers |
|---|---|---|
| Research | research scientist | WikiHow's and Mawdoo3's category taxonomies, and what people actually search for in English and Arabic, with sources |
| Vertical | principal PM, verticals | Audiences and jobs; which categories suit 60-second predict-and-see lessons and which are plain procedures with no aha; sequencing; kill criteria |
| Category | Life Hacks category manager | 8–12 strands with example lessons, how PR #2's 200 lessons map onto them, and overlap with physics, chemistry, life and economics |
| Safety | Life Hacks safety reviewer | Default risk per strand, what's out of scope (medical and legal advice, dangerous chemistry) and the disclaimers |
| Localization | localization lead | What's culture-specific in Mawdoo3-style content (Ramadan, regional cooking, units, money), what travels across locales, and when to go Arabic |

The principal PM then writes the scope (`lifehacks-scope/README.md`). It covers strands, out-of-scope topics, the mapping of PR #2's lessons, and a **proposal** for sub-area category managers per strand. That proposal goes to your directs for consultation before any roles are created, as the org-change process requires.

**PR #2: Femi's evaluation (same workflow).**
- **Breakdown:** what's in the PR, any protected paths it touches, licences.
- **Trial merge:** on a scratch branch, `community/pr2-trial`. Conflicts are resolved there, and the PR's board items get fresh IDs.
- **Checks:** lesson check, build, and QA on 10 sampled lessons.
- **Output:** a review plan in batches of 25.

Nothing touches our branch.

**The 50 verification agents.** These come next, as a second workflow on the trial branch once Femi has it ready. Life Hacks lessons pass the same checks as ours, and in proportion:
- fact-check of its 883 unverified claims;
- a safety review of every lesson;
- learner reviews with screenshots;
- accessibility;
- QA.

The workflow also picks up our own backlog: the 19 stale re-reviews and the 26 new algorithm lessons as they land.

**One limit to know:** we can't literally run 50 at once. Direct agents cap at 20, and a workflow runs about 16 at a time. The 50 run as a queue that keeps every slot full. To run more truly in parallel, raise `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS`.

Yes. You can open another session yourself (a new Claude Code session on claude.ai/code, or the CLI), or I can start one from here with a task already assigned. Either way, it helps to know how sessions interact:

- **Each session is its own container,** with a separate clone of the repo. They share nothing locally; work moves between them only through git pushes.
- **The work queue doesn't cross sessions.** `claim.mjs` locks live in `company/ops/claims/`, which git ignores, so two sessions could pick up the same brief. Give each session a clearly separate area.
- **Shared files will conflict.** `board.json`, `progress.md`, `events.jsonl` and the lesson registry change constantly. A second session should work on its own branch and merge into ours through a PR, which Femi now owns.
- **Each session has its own limits:** another 20 agents, plus its own workflows. That roughly doubles throughput.

1. **PR #2: Life Hacks, all 200 lessons.** Verify, revise and get it merge-ready on its own branch. It's the biggest self-contained job and doesn't touch our other lessons.
2. **R&D:** the knots round 2 decision, promoting the winner into the kit, and the Schelling simulation engine.
3. **Networks, Crowds and Markets:** portfolio map, briefs, then builds.

This session would keep the revision rounds, algorithm builds, publishing and the org work.

If you want, I can create the second session and hand it #1 on a new branch, with instructions to coordinate through PRs. Or open it yourself and point it at this repo and the `ccr-4c6c7654-ew9ko1` branch. Its first step would be `npm run company -- status`, as CLAUDE.md says.

body:
You are Jonah, the course manager for Networks, Crowds, and Markets (role cm-course-ncm). First read your role file, .claude/agents/cm-course-ncm.md, and work strictly as that role. Then read company/courses/README.md and company/decisions/2026-10-14-courses-org.md.

The founder's ask: "Get the book, then develop demos. We aim at good coverage of things that could have demos." The work is Easley and Kleinberg 2010, id easley-kleinberg-2010.

1. Acquire the book.
   - The environment's network policy blocks cs.cornell.edu and the PDF mirrors with a proxy 403. Don't keep retrying them.
   - Build the table of contents from three sources: WebSearch (result snippets carry section titles), your own knowledge of this widely used textbook, and content/works.json, which already has the 24 chapter titles.
   - Mark each section number and title `"confirmed": false` unless a search snippet shows it. If one does, record that URL.
   - The book is a map only. Never copy its text, figures or exercises.

2. Write content/courses/ncm/chapters.json.
   - Shape: {work, note, chapters:[{n, title, sections:[{id:"3.2", title, confirmed, concepts:[...], demoable:true|false, why, covered_by:[slugs], status:"covered"|"batch1"|"gap"|"not-demoable"}]}]}.
   - A section is demoable when a learner can make one prediction that a stage then shows in under 60 seconds, with a checkable answer.
   - Most sections should be demoable. Mark history, surveys and pure definitions false, with the reason.
   - Include the "Advanced Material" sections. Many of them are demoable, for example betweenness and Girvan–Newman, the intuition for why a Nash equilibrium exists, VCG, PageRank's spectral view, and Kleinberg's small-world exponent.

3. Dedupe against existing work.
   - Run `node tools/meta.mjs coverage --work=easley-kleinberg-2010`.
   - Grep src/demos/*/*/meta.json for related concepts: graphs, auctions, cascades, power laws, epidemics, voting, Schelling, games, matching, PageRank, small world and so on.
   - Read the subject briefs in company/domains/briefs/*.md.
   - Session 2's batch 1 (S2-01..S2-23) lives on branch origin/ccr-rnd-ncm. Read it with `git show origin/ccr-rnd-ncm:company/ops/inbox/session-2.md` and `git show origin/ccr-rnd-ncm:company/rituals/records/2026-10-14-vertical-review-ncm.md`, plus `git show origin/ccr-rnd-ncm:company/domains/briefs/<file>.md` for these brief files: math.discrete, economics.markets, probability.chance, probability.statistics, cs.systems, cs.algorithms and life.health-epidemiology.
   - Batch-1 slugs get the status "batch1". Do not re-brief them.

4. Write company/courses/ncm/coverage.md.
   - A table by chapter with columns demoable, covered, batch1 and gap, plus the overall coverage %.
   - The gap list, ranked by teaching value.
   - Target: at least 80% of demoable sections covered once the gaps are built.

5. Write company/courses/ncm/briefs.md: a brief for EVERY gap section, roughly 40–60 briefs. One lesson may cover two adjacent sections. Read 2 existing briefs in company/domains/briefs/ first and match their shape. Each brief has:
   - slug: kebab-case, an outcome phrase rather than a topic, unique across src/demos;
   - domain: the subject the concept belongs to (math, probability, economics, cs, life, geography or ai);
   - the concept key;
   - audience, knowledge boundary and the misconception worth breaking;
   - the prediction question with its options;
   - the answer, with numbers re-run in node (paste the result);
   - the reveal in one line;
   - format, from company/design/formats.md, with "needs spec" when it is not the single-card default;
   - curriculum per company/product/lesson-metadata.md: {primary, also, prerequisites, level, strand, references:[{work:"easley-kleinberg-2010", chapter, section}], tags};
   - claims: the factual sentences the learner will see, each with its support (derivation, simulation or source). Use standard citations for sources, and flag any that need a human check;
   - how it differs from its nearest existing lesson.

6. Add each brief's concept to content/curriculum/<domain>.json with `"course": "ncm"`. Match the shape of the existing concepts and keep the JSON valid. Don't touch session 2's batch-1 concepts.

7. `npm run check` must pass.

Constraints:
- Don't run next build, qa, walkthrough or tsc: the machine is shared and low on memory.
- Don't edit board.json, progress.md, events.jsonl or the decision record.
- Put your proposed board items at the end of coverage.md under "## Proposed board items": one per brief, with owner demo-builder, or interaction-designer for "needs spec".

Reply in 10 lines or fewer: sections total, demoable, covered, batch1, gaps briefed, projected coverage %, and which briefs need specs.

body:
Here's where things stand. Agents are still working, so I'll report again when the course map and briefs land.

**NCM vertical, run through a new Courses org**
- **New org:** the Courses org exists in category management, with a "Courses · Books" room on floor 3. Two new people:
  - Amara, Head of Courses, reporting to the head of product.
  - Jonah, course manager for *Networks, Crowds, and Markets*.
  - Decision record: `company/decisions/2026-10-14-courses-org.md`.
- **Consultation:** Priya and Leonie both agreed, with changes, and I've built those changes into the roles:
  - The head of product approves course order and targets; Selin's vertical doc decides the order for NCM.
  - Strand managers accept or object to the course concepts that land in their subject.
  - A strand manager re-checks each approved course brief, then it's copied into that strand's briefs file. The work queue only reads briefs from there.
  - Coverage counts as an input metric, not as learner value.
  - No lesson may cite a section number nobody has confirmed against the book.
- **Split with session 2:** I messaged it. It finishes the NCM batch it already planned (16 briefs, now being built) and keeps R&D. This session covers everything beyond that batch.
- **Jonah is working now:** mapping all 24 chapters section by section, marking which can carry a demo and why, deduping against existing lessons and session 2's batch, and writing about 40–60 briefs for the gaps. The target is at least 80% of demo-able sections. Specs and builds follow.

**I couldn't get the book itself.** Your environment's network policy blocks `www.cs.cornell.edu` (the free draft) and every mirror I tried. For now Jonah builds the table of contents from search results and knowledge of the book, and lessons cite chapters only until someone checks the section numbers. To give agents the real text, add `www.cs.cornell.edu` under Allowed domains in Network access: open the cloud environment menu in the session title bar, then Edit. Steps: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cloud-environments#network-access

**Reviewing and publishing**
- **Integrated build:** it built cleanly with everything merged so far and is serving on port 3450.
- **Fact-check:** 265 claims checked; 254 verified and 11 disputed. A builder is fixing the 11.
- **QA records:** the QA tester is writing them for lessons blocked only by a missing record. This is the first run since you said you'd update its permissions; if it's still denied, it will stop and report.
- **Learner re-reviews:** 12 reviewers are covering 226 lessons that were revised since their last review or never reviewed. The release manager publishes once these come back.

Sources: [Kleinberg networks book site](https://cs.cornell.edu/home/kleinber/networks-book), [EK ch. 3 PDF (GMU)](https://cs.gmu.edu/~ashehu/sites/default/files/cs695_Spring19/EK_networks-book-ch03.pdf), [Full draft (Berkeley)](https://www.stat.berkeley.edu/~aldous/206-SNET/Papers/easley-kleinberg.pdf)

summary: Dispatch cm-cs-algorithms: Algorithms batch 2 briefs
body:
The founder wants many more algorithm lessons. Write algorithms batch 2: 40 new briefs appended to company/domains/briefs/cs.algorithms.md under a heading "Algorithms batch 2 (2026-10-14)".

Inspiration: the topic folders of TheAlgorithms/Python (github.com/TheAlgorithms/Python): sorts, searches, graphs, dynamic_programming, greedy_methods, backtracking, divide_and_conquer, strings, hashes, data_structures (trees, heaps, tries, segment/fenwick, disjoint set, linked lists), bit_manipulation, maths, geometry, compression, ciphers, scheduling, matrix, linear_programming, knapsack, cellular_automata, fractals and computer_vision basics. Use the repo as a list of ideas and, if needed, as reference code that you re-implement yourself in node to check answers. Never copy its code into lessons.

1. Dedupe first. List every existing cs lesson (src/demos/cs/*/meta.json: slug, title, curriculum.primary) and every brief already in company/domains/briefs/cs*.md, and don't repeat a concept already taught. Where an idea overlaps another strand (cs-security, cs-systems, math-discrete), skip it or say how yours differs.
2. Pick the 40 with the best "predict, then see" moment: a result that surprises a beginner and that the stage can show in 60 seconds. Spread them across at least 12 of those folders. Good candidates include:
   - Sorting and searching: counting sort, radix sort, shell sort gaps, bucket sort, bogosort expectations, comb sort, cycle sort writes, exponential/jump search, ternary search, quickselect worst case.
   - Dynamic programming: edit distance, LCS, LIS patience, coin change ways, rod cutting, matrix-chain order, egg drop (check it doesn't duplicate two-eggs-hundred-floors), 0/1 vs fractional knapsack.
   - Graphs: Bellman-Ford, Floyd-Warshall, topological sort, Kosaraju SCC, Prim vs Kruskal, bipartite check, Eulerian path (Hierholzer), max flow/min cut, Hopcroft-Karp intuition.
   - Strings: Z-algorithm, Manacher, Boyer-Moore skips, Rabin-Karp collisions, Levenshtein, anagram via counts.
   - Data structures: Fenwick prefix sums, segment tree, skip list, Bloom filter false positives, LRU cache, red-black/AVL rotations, binary-heap vs sorted array, circular buffer.
   - Bit manipulation: x & (x-1), Gray code, XOR swap, power-of-two test, popcount.
   - Maths: fast exponentiation, extended Euclid, Miller-Rabin, Karatsuba, Newton square root, Collatz, Josephus, Sieve of Atkin (vs the existing sieve), Pascal mod 2 = Sierpinski.
   - Geometry: point in polygon (ray casting), segment intersection, closest pair.
   - Other: reservoir sampling, Fisher-Yates bias (naive shuffle), Floyd cycle detection, Game of Life glider, Rule 110, run-length vs LZ.
3. Use the existing brief shape exactly. Each brief has: slug (an outcome phrase, unique across src/demos); concept key; audience and knowledge boundary; misconception; prediction question with options; answer re-run in node (paste the result); reveal line; format from company/design/formats.md, marked "needs spec" if not the single-card default; curriculum (primary, also, prerequisites, level, strand "algorithms", references: CLRS 4e chapter/section via work id clrs-4e only where you're sure of the section, otherwise chapter only); claims with their support; and nearest existing lesson and how this differs.
4. Add each concept to content/curriculum/cs.json, matching the existing concept shape.
5. `npm run check` must pass.

Don't run next build, qa, walkthrough or tsc. Don't edit board, progress or events.

Reply with the 40 slugs, one line each, marked default or needs spec. Then write the list to /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/3e472d64-8589-5167-8584-c47a01ab4321/scratchpad/algo2-slugs.txt (slug<TAB>default|spec).

Fix pass-19 disputed claims: I fixed all 10 disputed claims and set each back to "unverified" (checkedBy/checkedOn removed, and a dated bu…
body:
I fixed all 10 disputed claims and set each back to "unverified" (checkedBy/checkedOn removed, and a dated builder note added to its source). I also corrected the 4 stale source fields. `npm run check` passes (549 lessons, 2897 claims, 0 warnings). As you asked, I did not run build, QA, walkthrough or full tsc; the 8 Demo.tsx files I edited only passed a TypeScript syntax check, with no type check. I did not touch the board, progress or events.

- ten-test-cases c4: "Only" is gone. The reveal and claim now say "In this toy, more held-out cases shrink the noise: the spread falls as 1/√n", and the support is changed to derivation.
- a-birthday-like-mine c5: the reveal and claim now say "23 other people make 253 pairs among themselves, but you take part in only 23 comparisons, each matching with chance 1 in 365."
- straight-across-saves c3: the caption says "its square root is about S" unless S² equals east² + north² exactly (so (100, 200) reads "about 224"). The claim text matches.
- below-the-threshold-crash c3: no stage change. The claim now lists only what is actually shown: the locked message "Toy: room for 1,000. Log scale.", the 1/10/100/1,000 axis, the line at 50, "under 1 animal" counting as dying out, and what the reveal says.
- interpolation-guesses-the-page c5: the reveal now says "The dots bend upward, so the straight aim line runs above them and reaches your value too early: each aim fell short." The claim keeps one-position steps for small values only (1,000 and 9,261) and gives 73, 88, 89, 90 for 729,000.
- same-count-different-weight c5: the claim now says "two rows of 20 dots (40 in all)". No stage text said 40 per row, so Demo.tsx is unchanged.
- proposers-get-the-best c5: the motive is gone. The reveal and claim say "The US residency match switched to students proposing in 1998, a change studied by Roth and Peranson (1999)." The 1998 date comes from the checker's suggested wording; neither of us has opened the paper.
- one-bit-avalanche c6: the stage label and claim now say "· stands for a byte with no printable character, or a space". I added "or a space" because byte 32 (a space) can be reached with two flips and also shows as ·.
- truck-hits-car-force c5: the reveal now depends on the mass. If the truck is heavier, it says the car's speed changes truckKg/1,000 times as much and that is why the car comes off worse. At 1,000 kg it says both speeds change by the same amount and neither comes off worse. The claim is rewritten to match.
- random-dots-cluster c5: "unusual" is gone. The reveal and claim say a scatter with no crowded square (44.5% of batches, worked out from the exact figure) is about as common as one with a crowded square, so a lump alone is weak evidence.
- sliding-the-cutoff c5 (source only): the source now describes errors() with means 2 / 2.5 / -0.5 and the cutoff-1 figures, 6.7% and 15.9%.
- window-forgets-start c2 (source only): it now cites hits(seed, 8) and drops() instead of spread(), which no longer exists.
- copy-overlaps-itself c3 (source only): the section is now RFC 1951 §3.2.3 (it was 3.2.5). This number is the checker's recall; I did not open the RFC.
- drop-the-losing-start c4 (source only): the source now says CLRS 3rd edition, and that the section is not in the 4th edition.

Decision for you: the 4 source-only claims are still marked "verified". Only their source field changed, using the checker's own notes, and the claim text is untouched. If you want those edits re-checked, they need setting back to unverified.

I'm fairly confident (about 85%) the sentences are now true and match the code. The main risks are the untype-checked JSX and the 1998 date.

Next move: the fact-checker re-checks the 10 reopened claims, plus the 4 source edits if you want them checked. After that, QA by whoever owns it once memory allows. The board entries and progress handoff for this work are still to be added by whoever owns them.

body:
The Life Hacks scoping and Femi's evaluation of PR #2 are both done. I've committed and pushed them (f5a9b89).

**Life Hacks scope:** it's a proposal for Priya and you, in `company/domains/lifehacks-scope/README.md`.
- **Positioning:** WikiHow and Mawdoo3 tell you how to do something; we show which method works and why, and every sentence a learner sees is a sourced claim.
- **Strands:** 12 subject strands, plus Debunk across all of them. Each strand comes with 10 lesson ideas and a safety class.
- **Out of scope:** medical, legal, dangerous chemistry, children's safety and religious rulings. Nine additions to the list of hacks we never teach are proposed.
- **Order:** strands open lowest-risk first; kitchen waits until wave 3.
- **Staffing:** five new sub-area manager roles, created in stages with two now. That still needs the directs' consultation.
- **The 50 verifiers:** the proposed split is 20 learner evaluators, 15 fact-checkers, 10 safety and 5 learner/QA. Only Sana, the safety reviewer, can give a safety verdict, so her capacity limits how fast the risky strands can open.
- **Disagreements:** eight are recorded with both views, for example five new roles versus none.

These are simulated-learner findings, not evidence that anyone learned.

- ai/direction-not-distance: launch
- ai/penalty-on-wiggle: revise. The title "Fit worse on purpose" and the hook "Why would you make it miss?" give away the predict answer ("Larger"), and "Smaller" can't happen from a miss of 0.
- ai/word-in-pieces: revise. The answer state, un | happi | ness = 3, never appears on stage. Unlocking leaves the word unsplit, the panel says to switch pieces off, and the reveal states the 3-token split as if it was seen. This is still not fixed from v1.

- cs/heap-bubble-up: launch
- cs/shortest-job-first-wait: launch
- economics/bending-frontier: revise. Why the curve bends ("land is not all alike") is only told; nothing on stage stands for a field. The lesson is unchanged at v1, and the earlier review gave launch on the same issue. I disagree because this is one of the brief's two "doesNotKnow" items, and the review says so.

- geography/land-hemisphere: launch
- geography/two-bulges: launch
- math/circle-slices-to-rectangle: launch

- physics/torch-underwater-tilt: revise. At 48.6° the caption says the exit ray "skims flat along the surface", but no exit ray is drawn. The reveal quotes 45° readouts (86%, 70.5°) that were never shown, and says "At 60°" when the gated path visited 70°, not 60°.

body:
You are Priya, the head of product, and I need a ruling on a craft rule. Learner reviewers disagree on one question: can a lesson launch when its "why" is told in one sentence rather than shown on the stage?

Two cases from wave D:
- **bending-frontier (economics):** the reveal says the curve bends because "land is not all alike", but nothing on stage represents a field. The brief lists this "why" as one of its two doesNotKnow items.
- **iss-gravity-still-there (physics):** "floating is free fall" is one told sentence, and nothing on stage falls.

Earlier reviews gave both launch. The wave D reviewer gives both revise. Their reviews are at company/reviews/<slug>/2026-10-14-learner-adult-beginner-r5.md, alongside the earlier ones. Read those files, company/product/demo-standard.md, and the board's pattern items W-150 and W-154 if present (`npm run company -- board`).

Write a short ruling as a decision record, company/decisions/2026-10-14-told-vs-shown.md. It needs an owner: line, Context, Decision, Objections (record the earlier reviewers' view) and Consequences. If the rule belongs in company/product/demo-standard.md, propose the exact sentence in the record, and check whether demo-standard.md is in company/constitution/protected-paths.txt. If it isn't protected, add the sentence there. If it is, leave it as a proposal.

Apply the ruling to the two cases: launch, or revise with what the stage must show. No builds. `npm run check` must pass. Reply in 4 lines.

The locked label "bread price ($6) filled by value added" also leans the guess toward $6. The earlier review gave launch and called this minor; I rate it higher because it is the one idea the learner is missing.
- economics/two-bets-split: revise. Moving the slider from 1 to 3 unlocks the reveal, so the 2-bet case the question asks about is never seen and the 25% answer is told (this was the r2 finding and it is not fixed).
- geography/midnight-sun-line: revise. Why the line is at 90° minus 23.4° is only told; the globe has no tilt marker. The reveal also quotes 66.6°N, but the preset buttons are 65, 70 and 80.
- life/purging-slows-down: launch

- math/sieve-crossing-out: launch
- physics/ball-at-the-top: revise. The reveal unlocks after one move past the top, so the learner never sees an upward velocity. The reveal quotes +0.97 m/s at 1.4 s, which was "?" when locked.
- physics/river-crossing-time: launch
- probability/average-that-never-settles: launch
- probability/halve-the-margin-cost: revise. Dragging from 2,000 to 8,000 skips 4,000 and still unlocks the reveal, which then quotes "4,000 → ±1.5".
- probability/sum-seven-ignores-first-die: launch
- cs/heapify-from-the-bottom: launch (first learner review)
- cs/trie-word-length-not-count: launch (first learner review)

What I believe, and how sure I am:
- Fairly sure about the gate problems in two-bets-split, halve-the-margin-cost and ball-at-the-top. In all three the reveal opens without the learner reaching the state it explains, and quotes numbers they never saw. This is a pattern across lessons, not three one-offs.
- Less sure about midnight-sun-line and count-the-bread-once. Both are judgement calls: the main fact is shown on the stage, but the "why" is only told.
- All of this is simulated-learner critique. None of it is evidence that anyone learned.

Outside my lane: heapify-from-the-bottom and trie-word-length-not-count show DRAFT and "0/5" / "0/6 claims checked" on this build. That is for the fact-checker, not a learner finding.
