body:
Fact-check pass 24, batch 1: the 17 lessons had 37 open claims. 36 are verified, 1 is disputed and none were withdrawn. `npm run check` passes (its 3 warnings are other lessons in review with disputed claims). I ran no builds and edited no lesson text.

**The dispute**
- **cs.wheel-needs-four-colours.c4**: the numbers hold. Backtracking on the ring of 4, with 3 or 4 colours allowed, gives red, blue, yellow, blue, yellow (3 used). The problem is a branch the learner can reach where the reveal says something false:
  1. Choose 4 colours, then Ring of 4, and colour by hand using all 4 (C red, 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 purple, 4 yellow). That colouring is stored as the ring-of-4 record.
  2. Then press Run backtracking. It finds a 3-colour colouring and reaches the ring-of-four milestone, but `setSeen` keeps the first successful record.
  3. The reveal then says "On the ring of four the two colours alternated all the way round: done with 4 colours", and the runs line shows "4 ring: done, 4 used".
  - Fix (demo-builder): for the ring-of-four record, keep only runs that used 3 colours or fewer, or keep the run that used the fewest. I put it on the board as W-231 (owner demo-builder).

**Notes that don't block publishing (written in the records)**
- near-and-far-links: the 1/d² "1% far" is really 10 of 2,000 links (0.5%), rounded up, so those three shares add to 101%.
- keep-one-of-a-stream: after a run at 4 items, the tally switches to the 5-item numbers when the 5th item arrives, with no re-run.
- one-odd-loop-blocks-two-camps: if the learner presses "Try all 64 splits" before picking loops, no walk is ever drawn, but the reveal still says "On those walks".

**How I checked and how sure I am**
- I read every Demo.tsx, including all reachable branches and the state after Reset or Start over, before reading the build.md Pre-flight notes.
- I re-ran every number in node with copies of each lesson's own functions, with mulberry32 copied from src/kit/random.ts. Each lesson's numbers came out as its claims state.
- No verified claim rests only on a source I couldn't open (Vitter, Knuth, Fenwick, Bentley & Yao, the Easley–Kleinberg book, Maynard Smith, CLRS). Each of those claims stands on its derivation or the lesson's own code.
- I'm highly confident in the 36 verified claims and in the dispute.

**Files written**
- In each lesson's meta.json I set status, checkedBy and checkedOn, and appended a "FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 24)" note to the source field. Paths are /home/user/system-3-company/src/demos/<domain>/<slug>/meta.json for all 17 lessons in fc24-1.txt.
- A "Pass 24" table is appended to /home/user/system-3-company/company/reviews/<slug>/2026-10-14-fact-check.md for all 17 lessons.
- A new board item, W-231.
- A handoff entry at the top of /home/user/system-3-company/company/ops/progress.md.

**Next move:** demo-builder fixes W-231 in cs/wheel-needs-four-colours. Then a fact-checker rechecks c4, the only claim in this batch still blocking publication.

body:
Pass 24, batch 3 is finished. There were 36 open claims across the 17 lessons: 34 are now verified, 2 are disputed and 0 were withdrawn. `npm run check` passes with 3 warnings, two of them from these disputes. I did no builds and edited no lesson text or code.

**Disputes**
- **physics/iss-gravity-still-there c6:** the claim says the zoomed-in view keeps "every angle true", which is false. The height stretch (about 5.8×, shown as 6×) keeps each point's direction from Earth's centre, so throws still land in the right place. But it draws a path's angle to the ground about 6× steeper. Learners see this sentence in the lesson's claims list. Suggested fix: "keeping Earth's radius and each point's direction from Earth's centre true".
- **geography/continental-jigsaw c4:** "Published fits use the edge of the continental shelf" rests only on Bullard, Everett and Smith (1965), which I couldn't open. The paper and the copies at royalsocietypublishing, pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov, earthguide.ucsd.edu and open.edu all return a proxy 403. Search snippets, which I could read but not open, say the best fit was at the 500-fathom contour, "on the steep part of the continental edge". The pops-seen milestone still fires on that path. Fix for the builder: either step through the pops frame by frame on Next number too, or show the clause only if the replay was actually seen. **Held (3).** Each rests only on a source I could not open. Wikipedia, arxiv, cornell, repec, sfu and readthedocs all fail DNS.

Insert next then stays disabled, the first-rotation milestone can never fire, and the reveal never unlocks. On the board as W-235 (owner: demo-builder). Its claim c6 is verified.

Disputes:
- **geography/shrinking-degree c2.** The lesson gives 55.6 km at 60°N, 19.3 km at 80°N and 111.2 km at the equator, as if they were Earth's figures. They are only right for a perfect sphere of radius 6,371 km. On the real Earth (the WGS84 shape) they are 55.80, 19.39 and 111.32 km, and the lesson's own c4 tells learners 111.3 km for the equator. Nothing on the stage says the globe is a sphere. Fix (builder): label the sphere model on the stage and in the claim, or round to "about 56 / 19 / 111 km".
- **cs/range-min-in-four-nodes c7.** Two things the claim says don't hold on every path:

  - Fix (builder): record the Seen minimum only once (or change the claim), and keep the dashed outline on those blocks, or reword to "not lit or highlighted".

All nine other lessons passed. I checked every open claim against Demo.tsx, including all control paths, Reset or its absence, and reduced motion. I re-ran the numbers in my own node copies of each lesson's logic (BigInt Karatsuba trees, seeded ruler trials, the stack's Next number stepping, d3-geo areas and projections, all 6-person friend/enemy networks for the balance rule). How the examples were chosen: for Karatsuba, 11141313 × 13111224 meets the stated selection rules (digits 1-4, four distinct halves, 27 one-digit leaves and 64 schoolbook leaves). I did not re-run the builder's search script. The ruler seed (1) is used as stated. No claim rests only on an outside source I couldn't open. I'm highly confident in every verdict, since each is re-computed rather than taken from a source.

Fact-check pass 26, batch 1 (10 lessons) is finished. There were 20 open claims: **18 verified, 2 disputed, 0 left unverified.** `npm run check` passes with 2 warnings, both "in review with a disputed claim". No builds were run.

Disputes:
- **physics/throw-it-fast-enough c6.** The numbers hold. The problem is the reveal sentence "your {fastest landing} and 7.9 km/s throws both fell 17.6 km": the 17.6 km comes from the 7.9 km/s flight only. The slider is a native range input, so a learner can go 7.8 → 0.79 with Home or a click on the track, then click to 7.9. The reveal then says the 0.79 km/s throw fell 17.6 km, which is false: it landed at 46 s. The same happens with 4.0 km/s. Fix: when the fastest landing has no first-minute record, leave it out of that sentence.
- **geography/eratosthenes-shadow c5.** "At Syene the Sun was straight overhead" is stated as fact in the reveal and on the stage label ("Syene: Sun overhead, no shadow"). Syene is at 24.09 N, north of the Tropic of Cancer; the lesson's brief puts it about 0.65 degrees north today and asks for "in the account" framing. Fix: "In the account, the Sun stood straight overhead at Syene at noon on the summer solstice…". The question ("At noon a well in Syene has no shadow") also leaves out the solstice.

**One bug that is not a claim:** horizon-ruler can never open its reveal. Demo.tsx registers only two milestones (`names={["eyes","hundred"]}`) but sets `minInteractions={3}`, and `reach("tower")` is ignored. I verified c1 there anyway.

- Read every open claim against Demo.tsx (and model.ts for the throw lesson), covering all branches, the lack of a Reset control, and reduced motion.
- Re-ran each lesson's own logic in node: every press order for the matching lesson, `fly()` for the throw lesson, the seed blocks for the lineage lesson, all 2,495 caption/readout pairs for the bettor lesson, and `split()` for every q.
- proposers c1: the example meets its stated selection criteria. I did not re-run the builder's search that found it.
- all-lines c7: the 25- and 100-women means use the same seed block as the 1,000-run, as the claim says.
- eratosthenes c3: the web was blocked, so I checked it against data I could open locally from npm. The GeoNames extract (cities.json) confirms the coordinates to two decimals. GeographicLib's WGS84 constants give a meridian of 40,007.86 km.

How sure I am: high on the 18 verified, since each rests on my own re-runs. High on the throw dispute, since the path is reachable by reading the code, though I did not try it in a browser. Medium-high on the Syene dispute: the brief's own caveat supports it, and my figure for Eratosthenes' time (a few tenths of a degree north) is my own estimate, not from a source I opened.

body:
The fix is pushed as commit 1a879c6 on ccr-4c6c7654-ew9ko1. It fixes the tap-target breakage, but it only partly fixes the crop: in 3 of the 6 lessons, 99–275px of the stage top is still cut off.

1. **Cause:** the W-135 fit (`useRevealFit` in `src/components/DemoCard.tsx`) scrolls the card body to bring the reveal's bottom on screen. At the reveal the stage takes its full height (the 2026-10-13 `.stage { flex: none }` rule, plus the W-135 `.stage-svg { flex: none; height: auto }` rule), so that scroll pushes the stage top off the card. No `scrollIntoView` is involved; the CSS rules only make the overflow bigger.
2. **Fix:** before scrolling, the fit now shrinks only the stage's pictures (svg drawings that contain no controls, largest first, down to 40% of their natural height), then scrolls whatever is still over. Controls never shrink. My first version scaled the whole stage and broke the 24px tap-target check; the snapshot commits 740f5a1 and 01006ec put it on the branch, and 1a879c6 replaces it. Only `DemoCard.tsx` and a comment in `globals.css` are committed; `tsconfig.json` is reverted.
3. **Before → after**, at 390×844 with touch: px of stage top cropped. The reveal is fully visible in every case:

| lesson | before (build 4, :3480) | after (:3490) |
|---|---|---|
| bending-frontier | 187 | 33 |
| one-odd-loop-blocks-two-camps | 155 | 45 |
| a-star-heads-for-goal | 351 | 200 |
| every-second-seat-out | 467 | 275 |
| midnight-sun-line | 231 | 99 |
| good-lists-make-good-pages (NCM) | 103 | 0 |

4. **What's left:** where the controls plus the reveal are taller than the card, shrinking the picture can't make enough room. In midnight-sun-line the globe the reveal names is still off screen. The options are trimming or hiding controls at the reveal, shorter reveals, or a reveal that scrolls inside itself (which relaxes W-135). That is a design-lead decision (W-259).
5. **Protected:** no. `src/kit/Lesson.tsx` and `tests/qa` are untouched. I'm treating it as tier 2 because it changes every lesson's reveal: principal-engineer review is W-237.
6. **How sure I am:** certain of the cause and that the tap-target problem is gone. Medium confidence this is the best fix the kit can make on its own.

Not done: a full `npm run verify` on the final build (only contract QA on those 73 lessons, plus `npm run check`, which passes). 1. Verdict: approve with changes (W-237 moved to done). The code is correct and has no layout loop: resize, Reset, re-entering the reveal, reduced motion and SVGs without a viewBox all behave, and the fit settles in two passes. The problem is text inside the pictures. I copied the fit into a page probe and ran it on build 4 (:3480) over 638 lessons (593 measurable). Separately, 7 absolute-positioned overlays get squashed out of line with their HTML nodes and free 0px.
2. Accessibility and the floor: the 24px rule passes only because the contract checks just tagged controls. Three lessons have untagged pointer targets inside pictures that get shrunk; I have not checked those by hand. A fixed 40% floor is defensible only for pictures without text (52 lessons). For pictures with labels the floor should be set by text size. My estimate is that a 9px floor leaves about 60 lessons fitting fully instead of 261; that is a calculation from the probe data, not a measurement.
3. Board: W-287 (platform-engineer) adds the 9px legibility floor, undoes shrinks that free no space, and skips stretched (preserveAspectRatio="none") and absolute-positioned SVGs. It blocks release: if it is not in the build that ships, revert 1a879c6 for that build. W-288 (platform-engineer) covers the untagged targets and a re-measure. body:

body:
Ruling: meaning-carrying SVG labels get a 10px rendered floor (`SVG_TEXT_FLOOR_PX=10`) and decorative or `aria-hidden` labels get 8px (`SVG_DECOR_FLOOR_PX=8`). Per picture, k = max(0.4, 10 / smallest non-aria-hidden text px); k ≥ 1 means no shrink, a label already under 10px at natural size is never shrunk, and text-free pictures keep 0.4. New lessons should target 11px at natural size, matching iOS.
Why 10 and not 11 or 12: in the probe, 288 of 390 pictures already have natural labels under 11px, so a higher floor would condemn existing lessons instead of limiting the shrink. By my estimate from the probe, the fit fully resolves about 44 of 433 lessons at 10px (66 at 9px, 36 at 11px, 261 today). The rest goes through the W-264 to W-267 route. The 10px figure is a judgement; I did not test it on a device or with learners.
Written to `company/design/system.md` (new section "Accessibility: minimum text size in lesson pictures") with the reasoning and the constants. The W-289 board item has a ruling note for W-287 (platform engineer) to set the constants, and I moved it to done. `npm run check` passed. I did not add a progress.md handoff.

body:
1. **Decision:** yes, we revisit option (a), but as a per-row opt-in "fold at the reveal", not a kit-wide collapse. A builder marks a `Row` foldable only if the reveal quotes nothing in it. The fold runs only at the reveal and only when the card overflows, before any picture shrink. One "Show controls" button (at least 44 px) takes the place of the first folded row, and one tap brings every row back in DOM order, at full size, with its state kept.
2. **QA contract:** no amendment is forced. `contract.spec.ts` presses every control before the reveal, and its 24 px check after the reveal skips `display:none` controls, so the spec allows `display:none` only (never height, scale or visibility). It never presses the button, though, so that coverage gap went to the evaluation steward as optional (W-334); `tools/reveal-fit.mjs` will do that check meanwhile.
3. **Your two caveats:** 174 of 217 is an upper bound from build 5, and W-287 will make crops larger (system.md estimates the fit resolves about 44 lessons at the 10 px floor, down from 261 today). So no builder opts in until a re-sweep on a W-287 build (W-333). Rows the reveal quotes stay visible to answer caveat 2, and learner re-review W-338 includes a re-check task.

body:
The interaction designer approved the plan to fold controls away at the reveal, with five changes:
- **What can fold:** a row of controls only folds if the learner loses no evidence by it. No row with a readout folds, every way the reveal can open is checked, and the row's state must still show in the picture.
- **The button:** it reads "Show more controls" when some controls stay visible, and it has to look like a control, not a caption.
- **When it happens:** the fold is decided once, before the reveal first appears, so rows never disappear later.
- **Focus:** keyboard and screen-reader focus moves to the button, and expanding doesn't jump the page.
- **Worth it:** a row only folds if that saves at least the height of the button itself.

Fewer lessons will benefit than the sweep's upper bound of 174. In gradient-descent, for example, every control is evidence for the reveal, so nothing folds there.

The design lead is now writing those five changes into the plan. After that, the platform engineer writes the design doc and builds the fold. The review is committed and pushed.

Build 6 is still running. Once it's served, I'll start the shared dev server and launch fixes for the 40 lessons that got "revise".

summary: No, the latest work isn't live on Vercel. There are two reasons:
body:
No, the latest work isn't live on Vercel. There are two reasons:

1. **Vercel's daily limit is used up.** Vercel's GitHub app tries to deploy every push to the branch, and the free plan allows 100 deployments a day. We push dozens of times a day, mostly work-in-progress snapshots, so the quota ran out. The last status on GitHub, at 10:51 UTC, reads "Deployment rate limited — retry in 24 hours". PR #2's preview was hit by the same limit this morning.
2. **We've never run a deliberate release.** `company/ops/deployments/` has no deployment records. The release tool (`npm run deploy -- preview|production`) needs a Vercel token and project IDs, and this environment has neither.

So "published" (592 lessons) is currently a status in the repo. Learners don't see it until a deploy goes through.

My recommendation is to stop the automatic preview on every push. I'd add an `ignoreCommand` to `vercel.json` so Vercel only builds commits whose message contains `[deploy]`. I'd mark one commit per publish wave that way, which spends a handful of deployments a day instead of 100.

You'd need to do one of these to get it live:
- **Easiest:** wait for the quota to reset, which is within 24 hours of when it ran out. Once I've added the `[deploy]` filter, the next marked push will deploy.
- **Or:** give this environment a Vercel token and project IDs as secrets. The release manager can then run proper preview and production deploys with smoke tests and rollback.
- **Also check:** which branch Vercel treats as production. If it's `main`, nothing on `ccr-4c6c7654-ew9ko1` reaches production until it's merged there.

Should I add the `[deploy]` filter now?

body:
Draft a constitutional amendment for the founder to ratify. Don't apply it.

Problem: .github/workflows/ci.yml (a protected path) runs on every push, and agents push dozens of work-in-progress snapshots a day. GitHub Actions now has about 300 queued CI runs, and runs queued at 09:05 finished around 12:45. The deploy workflow (.github/workflows/deploy.yml) only runs after CI succeeds, so releases wait hours behind superseded commits.

Proposal: add a top-level `concurrency: { group: ci-${{ github.ref }}, cancel-in-progress: true }` to ci.yml. Superseded runs on the same branch are then cancelled. PR runs keep their own group through github.ref.

Do this:
1. Read company/constitution/ and its amendment procedure (look for AMD-* records), and draft AMD-<next> in the same format. Cover:
   - the exact diff;
   - why it doesn't weaken any gate: the latest commit is still fully checked;
   - the risk: a cancelled run hides a failure that only an older commit had, which matters little because the newest commit is the release candidate;
   - the rollback.
2. Put it where pending amendments go, and add a board item for the founder to ratify. The ratified commit must include "Amendment: AMD-<n>", or CI fails.

Don't edit ci.yml. `npm run check` must pass. Reply in three lines.

summary: No, we aren't stuck with it. The one-build-for-everything setup will hold to about 1,000 lessons, and the principal engineer already has a …
body:
No, we aren't stuck with it. The one-build-for-everything setup will hold to about 1,000 lessons, and the principal engineer already has a plan for 10,000. We're about 140 lessons from the point where that plan says to switch.

**Where we are at 863 lessons (build 7):**
- One Next.js build compiles every lesson. It took 2.3 min to compile, 2.0 min to type-check and 2.8 min to generate pages, about 7 minutes in total, and the output is 1.2 GB.
- A full browser QA run on 200 lessons takes about 45 minutes, so the whole catalogue takes several hours.
- At 10,000 lessons the same setup breaks. The build would run over an hour, every change would re-test everything, and feed pages already carry far too much data.

**The plan (EDD-003, written 2026-10-13, still "proposed"):**
- **Stage 0, now to 1,000 lessons:** fix what's already broken.
  - The feed ships about 1.8 MB against a 300 KB budget, because every page carries every lesson's claim records.
  - The fix is a slim feed index, full lesson metadata loaded on demand, and pagination.
- **Stage 1, 1,000 to 10,000:** lessons stop being compiled into the app.
  - Each lesson becomes its own content-hashed bundle, loaded at runtime into a sandboxed frame.
  - A generated manifest of slug, version and bundle replaces the registry, so publishing or rolling back a lesson is just a pointer change.
  - The app builds once, and each lesson builds only when it changes. QA runs only on changed lessons.
  - This starts when any one of these is hit: 1,000 lessons, a build over 10 minutes, or full QA over 2 hours. The QA trigger has effectively fired already.
- **Stage 2, 10,000 to 100,000:** lesson sources move out of the app repo into domain-sharded content repos.

**The other lever is already proven: lessons as data, not code.** The 200 Life Hacks lessons are 9–33 line shells over 3 shared engines. Most of what a lesson is lives in its spec, not its code. Fewer engines with many specs means much less to compile and test. At 10,000 lessons, most new lessons should be variants built from specs on existing engines, not new React code.

**What I'd start now:**
1. The principal engineer and platform engineer finish the stage-0 feed fix (EDD-001). It's overdue.
2. The stage-1 spike, W-074, is in review: 3 lessons loaded as separate bundles in a sandboxed frame. It needs the principal engineer's verdict, then a decision record for the bundler, since that adds a new dependency.
3. QA only what changed. The QA tester and platform engineer get a "changed since the last green build" mode, so a wave of 40 lessons doesn't re-test 863.

The plan also contains decisions only you can make: the bundler dependency, and whether "the disk is the memory" means git specifically. I can have the principal engineer close EDD-003's review and bring you a one-page decision.

Should I start items 1–3?

**Scope of the index.** Use a server-side index of company/ markdown, built at build time or on request. Don't add a new npm dependency: plain JS search, for example tokenised titles and headings plus substring and term-frequency scoring, is enough. The types and their sources:
- Reports: company/rituals/records/ (WBR, MBR, OP planning, retros, launch reviews, eng reviews).
- Decisions: company/decisions/.
- Tech design: company/engineering/edd/, any ADRs, company/engineering/reviews/, company/engineering/notes/.
- Strategy: company/product/ (including verticals/), company/domains/ (charters, briefs, scope).
- Requirements: PRDs and BRDs wherever they live (search for them; head-of-product owns company/product).
- Constitution and amendments: company/constitution/.
- Courses: company/courses/.
- Reviews: company/reviews/** is thousands of files, so include it but let users filter it out. Default filter: everything except per-lesson reviews.
- Progress log: company/ops/progress.md, split into dated entries.

1. **Roles.** A category manager for each, `cm-books` and `cm-big-ideas`, with 2 or 3 strand managers each where it makes sense. **Method.** For each lesson I read Demo.tsx (and model.ts where there is one) first, on every reachable path. - The only outside sources I opened were two PyPI packages:
  - ht 1.2.0, ISO 10456 and ASHRAE property tables, for metal-feels-colder c3.
  - pint 0.26.1, which defines the inch as yard/36 with yard = 0.9144 m (since July 1959), for cm-to-inches c1 and its recall. pint is a secondary source (a software unit registry), so a reviewer may want to weigh it.

**Held as unverified (sources I could not open):**
- metal-feels-colder c6 (thermoreception)
- hailstone-27-climbs c4 (Collatz verification bound) and c5 (problem still open)
- lh-scale-recipe-portions c5 (food-safety guidance)

  - calibrated-but-unequal-alarms c1: the quoted line is attributed to the stage but is really reveal text.

I wrote 9 Life Hacks briefs for Wave J, not the 10 you asked for. The charter's rules leave no room for a 10th: details below.

Nothing is built or committed, and no lock was taken. I added a line to `company/ops/brief-skips.json` for each of the 9, so the queue holds them until the safety reviewer has seen them. That means the queue does not hand them out yet, on purpose.

**Slugs, in rank order** (ranks 6-14 under "## Wave J" in `company/domains/briefs/lifehacks.md`):
1. `mix-the-problem-types`: study, interleaved-practice, safety class none
2. `style-match-needs-a-crossover`: study, learning-styles-debunk, none

7. `lid-on-boils-first`: kitchen, lid-boils-water-sooner, full review
8. `steak-keeps-cooking`: kitchen, resting-meat, full review

Each brief has:
- **Safety:** a class and a checklist for the reviewer.
- **Format and stage:** a format from the catalogue, plus a call between an existing Life Hacks engine and a custom stage. Most need custom stages: the study engine has no interleaving or growing-gap model, and the one engine fit (battery on ResourceLesson) waits on board item W-518, an open design issue with that template.
- **Demo standard:** preset buttons in DOM order with milestones, labels of at least 10px, and a reveal draft of 59-74 words, counted by script.

**Why 9, not 10:**
- Amendment A2 bars any demand-1 or demand-2 brief.
- Study reaches its cap of 15 with briefs 1, 2 and 5.
- Every other demand-3 concept in an open strand already has two or more lessons.
- Cleaning is wave 4, and no rule lets it be briefed early. So cleaning can't open, and kitchen is only prepared under A3. The A3 tripwire is now in the head of product's hands (W-570): kitchen briefs exist and are held, cleaning has none.

**Something you should know: wave 2 is not open on the record.** The gate needs the Domain Launch Review and a published `spaced-beats-cram`, and 0 Life Hacks lessons are published. A1 only allows the digital lessons once their wave is open. So the skip lines for the two digital briefs also wait on that ruling (W-570). Separately, the portfolio manager's note on W-401 files these briefs under Wave K, which is gated by W-556; I asked the head of product whether that applies.

Kit: multi-card sequence format: ## Summary
body:
## Summary
I built the multi-card sequence format as a kit component. It did not need any change to Lesson.tsx, the lesson contract or tests/qa. Every test passes: contract QA on the example 2/2, contract QA on 10 random lessons 20/20, and reveal-fit phoneFit true with 0 px crop.

**Branch:** `design/multi-card-sequence`, in worktree `/home/user/s3c-cards`. One commit, `4dc6ba9`. No `[deploy]` anywhere; it ends with the footer you gave me. It is ready for you to merge.

## API (`src/kit/sequence.tsx`)
```tsx
<Lesson minInteractions={4} …>   {/* = sum of every sub-card's milestones */}
  {({ phase, locked, interact }) => (
    <CardSequence label="Euclid's proof in three steps" phase={phase} locked={locked} interact={interact} revealCard?="divide">
      <SubCard id="multiply" title="Multiply" milestones={["all-six"]} trace={`${k} primes`}>
        {({ reach, reached, active, locked, phase, index, count }) => …}
      </SubCard>
      …2-4 sub-cards
    </CardSequence>)}
</Lesson>
```
- `useSubCard()` gives the same context to components deeper inside a sub-card.
- **DOM order is the QA path.** A row of step buttons (the "trail") comes first. Only steps already visited and not current are enabled, so the trail is fully disabled when QA reaches it. Then come each sub-card's own controls, then its own "Next". Pressing each control once therefore walks every sub-card.
- **Hidden sub-cards** stay mounted (state kept) and use the `hidden` attribute.
- **Control budget:** trail steps + all controls + (sub-cards − 1) Next buttons ≤ 16. A dev-only warning fires above 16, or outside 2–4 sub-cards.
- **Sizes:** every control is 44 px tall (the contract floor is 24 px).
- **Milestones** belong to each sub-card. Only they call `interact()`; Next, the trail and swipes never count.
- **Reveal quoting:** the reveal may quote any sub-card's `trace` (shown in the trail once that step is done, so it stays on screen) or the picture of `revealCard`. `revealCard` defaults to the last sub-card and is set before the reveal's first paint.
- **No Back button.** You go back by tapping a visited step in the trail or swiping right. A Back button would either send QA backwards or make the visual order differ from the focus order.
- **Swipe:** touch or pen only, at least 48 px and mostly horizontal, and never when it starts on a control. The area uses `touch-action: pan-y`, so vertical scrolling still works.
- **Accessibility:** after Next, focus moves to the new sub-card. A polite live region speaks only after a swipe. There is no animation under reduced motion.

## Test results
The build is `.next-cards` on :3570. Load average was 23–38 because of other agents.
- **Contract QA on `euclid-three-steps`:** 2/2. The first phone run timed out at 45 s after 36 s on the cold page load; the re-run passed in 39.7 s. In the phone explore screenshot, all three steps are ticked and sub-card 3 is showing.
- **Contract QA on 10 random lessons, phone and desktop:** 20/20. These were lh-standby-days-add-up, true-text-false-claims, scoops-in-three-cups, call-stack-depth, lh-align-price-units, momentum-sweet-spot, weight-spread-on-table, which-answer-wins, london-december-noon-sun and few-shortcuts-shrink-the-world. 17 passed on the first run. Three phone runs (momentum-sweet-spot, which-answer-wins, call-stack-depth) timed out under load and passed when re-run with one worker. None of these lessons import the new code.
- **`node tools/reveal-fit.mjs --strict` on the example:** phoneFit true. Crop 0 px, nothing hidden below, nothing named hidden, 63 words.
- **My own behaviour check (scratch script, not committed):** focus moves correctly, going back through the trail keeps state, swipes work in both directions, a short swipe is ignored, reduced motion gives `animation: none`, all controls are 44 px, and there were no page or console errors.
- `tsc`, `next build` and `npm run check` pass.

## Files
- `/home/user/s3c-cards/src/kit/sequence.tsx` and `/home/user/s3c-cards/src/kit/sequence.module.css`
- `/home/user/s3c-cards/company/engineering/edd/EDD-006-multi-card-sequence.md`
- `/home/user/s3c-cards/src/demos/math/euclid-three-steps/` (Demo.tsx, meta.json, styles.module.css). It is a draft and all 6 claims are unverified. **It is under math because no books domain existed yet.**
- `/home/user/s3c-cards/src/lib/hq-design.ts`: the Design inspector now detects `<CardSequence>`.
- `/home/user/s3c-cards/company/design/concepts/multi-card-sequence.md`: updated the kit line.
- Changelog, progress-log handoff and board items (`company/ops/`).

## What I believe
- **No Lesson.tsx change is needed** (high confidence).
- **The QA path reaches every sub-card** (high confidence).
- **No regression** (fairly sure).
- **Not checked:** a real phone (swipe against the feed's vertical scroll), a screen reader by ear, dark theme, and a 4-card sequence with longer titles.
- The example teaches the same concept as the published product-plus-one lesson (infinitude-of-primes).
- When I started, the disk had only 17 MB free because of many `.next-*` build directories left by other agents. I cleared only the npm cache and left their directories alone. Whoever owns them should prune them.

## Next moves
- **W-477, principal-engineer:** review EDD-006.
- **W-478, interaction-designer:** design review of the example (the no-Back choice, the trail at 390 px).
- **W-479, accessibility-reviewer:** review the stepper's keyboard and screen-reader behaviour.
- **W-480, cm-math:** decide whether the duplicate-concept example ships, merges or stays a reference only.
- **Then the design lead** changes the formats.md row from 🔴. Book Summaries builders should wait until then.

- bag: the 6 kg total is never shown, and there is no volume at all.

1. W-477 is fixed and in review, but not committed or deployed. `/spike` now returns 404 unless NODE_ENV is development or the server-side flag `SPIKE_ENABLED=1` is set. The cdn origin is picked on the server from the `SPIKE_CDN_ORIGINS` allow-list (default http://localhost:3141), so `?cdn=` can only choose a listed entry and never becomes a frame, fetch or script source. Frame paths from the manifest are refused if they would leave that origin. The spike now keeps progress under its own key (`s3c:spike:progress:v1`) and no longer sends frame events to `/api/events`. Separately, `/api/events` returns 403 for `Origin: null` (sandboxed frames), other origins, cross-site requests and a `/spike` referer. Progress has no server API; it lives only in localStorage.

summary: PE review W-477 spike fix: 1. I approved W-477 (c5e050b) and moved it to done. `npm run test:spike` passes 5/5, and I probed the guards …
body:
1. I approved W-477 (c5e050b) and moved it to done. `npm run test:spike` passes 5/5, and I probed the guards with about 20 more adversarial inputs. Nothing from the query string reaches a frame, fetch or script source; tricks like `/\evil.com`, `//host` and `@host` either get refused or stay on the allowed CDN origin. In production /spike can't be reached: NODE_ENV is read when the request runs (if it were baked in at build time it would read "production", which is still blocked), the page is always rendered per request, and there's no static export, rewrite or middleware.
2. The events guard lets real lesson events through, including behind Vercel. A request shaped like Vercel's (Host is the deployment host, X-Forwarded-Host is the custom domain) gets 204. A cross-site browser page can't forge Host or X-Forwarded-Host. Requests with no Origin still pass, which I accepted because the intake is anonymous and curl could always write to it. I also ruled that 403 is the right response, not a silent 204, so a guard that breaks shows up in the logs.
3. Nothing is blocking, but I recorded these risks: no production build or preview has been run, and I skipped `next build` too because the machine is overloaded. If any page ever sets a `no-referrer` Referrer-Policy, its lesson events would arrive with Origin null and get a silent 403. An X-Forwarded-Host with a port in it wouldn't match. The spike QA reuses an already-running server without SPIKE_ENABLED (reuseExistingServer), so it fails with a 404, not open. And SPIKE_ENABLED must never be set on the production project.
4. Files: /home/user/system-3-company/company/engineering/reviews/2026-10-14-w477-spike-review.md (new), plus updates to /home/user/system-3-company/company/ops/board.json (W-477 done, new W-609), /home/user/system-3-company/company/ops/progress.md (top entry) and the kudos log. `npm run check` passed. Nothing was committed or deployed.
5. Next: release-manager runs W-534 once the founder approves the deploy, then W-609 on production and the custom domain: /spike returns 404, a lesson's events return 204, Origin null returns 403, and SPIKE_ENABLED is absent from the Vercel env. If the events check fails, revert only the events-route half and reopen W-477. Whether to delete the route outright waits for the EDD-003 stage review (principal-engineer).

6. **Copyright and legal risk.** Turn the binding rules into a builder checklist, and frame the open question of a legal read for the founder.

1. **Verdict: approve with changes.** One blocker: in `src/components/Feed.tsx`, when a page fetch fails, `.catch` sets `loading:false` but leaves `next` where it was. body: Ok how many cards is one book? Would we be able to cover ideas ?

summary: **One book is usually about 6 cards: 2 lessons of 3 cards each.**
body:
**One book is usually about 6 cards: 2 lessons of 3 cards each.**

- **Lessons per book:** 2 by default. A third is added only when it needs a different kind of interactive picture and reaches a different verdict from the first two.
- **Cards per lesson:** once the multi-card checks close, each Books lesson is 3 cards, about 60 seconds in all:
  1. **The case:** the book's example, rebuilt as our own interactive picture.
  2. **Your test:** you predict, then try the mechanism yourself.
  3. **Holds up?** The evidence as a picture: replication results, the measured effect, or where the idea breaks.
- **How it hangs together:** a book's lessons form a short path, so its summary is the sequence, roughly 2 minutes per book.

**Will it cover the book's ideas?** It covers the main ones, not all of them. That's a deliberate choice:
- **What's covered:** each book's 2–4 key ideas are listed in the curriculum, and we teach the 2 most testable ones. Here's how that looks for a few books:

| Book | Ideas we teach | Ideas not taught |
|---|---|---|
| *Thinking, Fast and Slow* | anchoring, loss aversion, the planning fallacy (3 lessons) | most of its ~38 chapters |
| *The Goal* | the bottleneck sets the pace; random delays pile up along a chain | the novel's plot and the management story |
| *Outliers* | the relative age effect; the 10,000-hour claim, which mostly doesn't hold up | the cultural chapters |
- **Why not everything:**
  - **Copyright:** a card-by-card retelling of a whole book is exactly what the copyright rules forbid. We teach ideas in our own words, not chapters.
  - **The format:** each lesson needs something you can predict and test. Ideas that can only be told, such as most narrative or historical arguments, don't fit, and the strategy skips them.
  - **Honesty:** the "holds up?" card is the value we add over a text summary, so we pick the ideas worth testing.

**If you want deeper coverage,** say 4–5 lessons for the top 10 books, that's possible for the testable ideas. It would cost about 20 more lessons out of the 60 still conditional, so it fits the 120 target. Tell me and I'll have Hester rework the list. The deciding question is whether you want breadth (50 books × 2 ideas) or depth (fewer books, more of each).

2. **Book-level framing.** Opening and closing cards: the book's question, a map of the ideas, a verdict summary across ideas ("what holds up from this book"). Navigation and progress across ideas: resume mid-book, and the feed showing a book as one tile. How each idea still gets its own predict→explore→reveal and its own recall.
3. **Where it stops being a retelling.** Draw the copyright line concretely: what a card may and may not contain.

I've recorded your call as a founder decision (ef4415e): Book Summaries becomes its own multi-card experience and covers more of each book. It replaces the earlier plan of 2 short lessons per book.

The design lead is now designing the Book format, working from the interaction designer's and Hester's records. The format answers:
1. **The unit:** most likely a book "deck" of 4–6 idea modules, each with its own predict, test and "holds up?" step, plus opening and closing cards: the book's question, a map of its ideas, and what holds up overall.
2. **Navigation:** how a reader moves through a book, resumes partway, and sees the book as one tile in the feed.

Design lead: Book experience format: 1. Unit: a book is a deck. An opening card (the book's question, a map of the ideas, a bet on how much will h…
body:
1. Unit: a book is a deck. An opening card (the book's question, a map of the ideas, a bet on how much will hold up) leads into 4–6 idea lessons (default 5), then a closing card that sets the bet against the verdicts. Each idea is its own lesson with its own slug, claims, predict/explore/reveal and recall, and uses 3 sub-cards (the case / your test / holds up?). That is about 60–75 s per idea and about 6 min per book (8 max).
2. Navigation: one feed tile per book (Start, "Resume: idea 3 of 5", or See the verdicts). Resume works from the `completedAt` lessons already record and is never mid-idea; only the bet is newly stored. Above each idea sits a book bar with one plain 16×8 segment per idea and no titles, so it can't wrap at 390. The idea's own trail stays at 3 steps, so the 4-step wrap to 71px (W-601) never comes up.
3. Copyright line, all countable: at most 20 words per idea and 120 per deck saying what the book argues. At most 1 quote per deck, no chapter numbers or titles shown, no book order, no book coinages, characters, figures or recaps, our toys only. Each deck also gets a concatenation test: all its "argues" sentences together must not read as a synopsis.
4. Kit (tier 2): a deck shell only, with no change to `Lesson.tsx`, `sequence.tsx` or `tests/qa`. It needs a deck manifest, `src/kit/book.tsx` (BookBar, `bookState`), BookDeck plus a `/b/[work]` route, a "book" feed tile, a bet store and 4 events. A new `tools/book-probe.mjs` walks a deck one press per control and checks resume and every sub-card's fit with the bar. Each idea is at most 14 of the 16 allowed controls and passes today's QA as it is.
5. Mockup: a *Thinking, Fast and Slow* deck, card by card, with 8 wireframes at 390×844 and labels 11px or larger. I rendered them and checked them by eye. All wording is draft and not yet claims; the verdicts are my reading, and the fact-checker can overturn them.
6. Capacity: a deck costs about 6 lesson reviews against 2 for a 2-lesson book, so the 60 committed slots buy about 10 books, not 30. I recommend fewer books at the same pace: 5 ideas per deck (4 if only 4 pass), at most 2 decks in progress at once. The Wave K pilot would be the TFS reference deck plus the 5 other drafts, each kept as idea 1 of a later deck, so still 10 lessons.
7. How sure: about 70% that the deck shape is the smallest that keeps the contract, the QA budget and the claim gate; about 50% on the time budget and the opening bet, since neither has been tried with learners. The interaction designer has no W-601 record yet, so the spec works around 4-step trails rather than resting on that ruling. No Books lesson publishes before F1 (a book source) and F2 (the legal read).
8. Next: board items W-647 (head-of-product, rule on the format), W-649 (cm-books, depth and list), W-651 (evaluation-steward, which I added: may a deck manifest hold claims?), W-650 (design-engineer, writes the kit EDD), W-648 (principal-engineer, reviews it); files are `/home/user/system-3-company/company/design/specs/book-format.md` and `book-format.svg`, plus a 🔴 "Book deck" row in `/home/user/system-3-company/company/design/formats.md` and a handoff in `company/ops/progress.md`. `npm run check` passes, and nothing was built or committed.

summary: Book deck format spec: opening bet, 4-6 idea lessons of 3 sub-cards, closing verdicts; countable copyright line; W-647..W-651
The design lead has proposed the Book format (pushed as 640b34b). The head of product is reviewing it now.
body:
The design lead has proposed the Book format (pushed as 640b34b). The head of product is reviewing it now.

**A book becomes a "deck", about 6 minutes long:**
1. **Opening card:** the book's question, a map of its ideas, and a bet: you guess how much of the book will hold up.
2. **4–6 idea lessons** (5 by default), each 3 cards and about 60–75 seconds:
   - **The case:** the book's example, as our own interactive picture.
   - **Your test:** predict, then try it.
   - **Holds up?** The evidence, shown as a picture.
3. **Closing card:** your bet against the verdicts, showing what actually holds up from this book.

**In the feed:** each book is one tile showing Start, "Resume: idea 3 of 5", or "See the verdicts". A thin bar above each idea shows where you are in the book.

**The copyright line can be counted:**
- At most 20 words per idea saying what the book argues, and 120 per deck.
- At most one short quote per deck.
- No chapter titles, no characters or figures from the book, only our own examples.
- All of a deck's "the book argues" sentences read together must not amount to a synopsis.

Your legal read would confirm this line.

**The kit change is small:** it adds a deck shell around today's lessons and leaves the protected lesson contract and QA untouched. It still needs the principal engineer's review.

**The cost:** a deck costs about as much review as 6 lessons, so the 60 committed Books slots now cover about 10 books in depth, not 30 thin ones. The design lead recommends going deep, with at most 2 decks in progress at once. The first reference deck would be *Thinking, Fast and Slow*. The 5 existing Books drafts would each become idea 1 of a later deck.

How sure the design lead is:
- **The deck shape:** about 70% sure it's right.
- **The 6-minute time and the opening bet:** about 50%, since neither has been tried with learners.

After the head of product rules, I'll bring you what's left for you. Expect the depth-versus-breadth call and whether the 120 target counts books or idea-lessons.

body:
1. I ruled on W-647 (now done) in /home/user/system-3-company/company/decisions/2026-10-14-book-deck-format.md. It has 6 rulings and 13 objections, each with an outcome. I accepted the deck format with three changes. A deck has 4 ideas by default, 3 allowed and never 5 or more, because the charter (/home/user/system-3-company/company/domains/books.md line 52) caps a book at 4 ideas and sends a fifth to the Courses org, and the spec did not account for that. Decks use the shared six verdict words from my earlier Ruling 3. The charter's "each must stand alone in the feed" now means each idea is complete on its own, not that it gets its own feed tile.
2. Depth against breadth: fewer books at the same pace. Slots measure review cost, and a deck costs its ideas plus 1 for the deck-level review. I recommend the 120 target count idea-lessons, not decks, but that unit is the founder's (F4). The committed 60 slots buy about 12 decks, or about 48 counted lessons. Reaching 120 idea-lessons would take about 150 slots.
3. Pilot: the Thinking, Fast and Slow deck is wheel-number-pulls-guess plus 3 new ideas that cm-books picks, plus the deck review. With the 5 kept drafts that is 10 slots. The drafts become idea 1 of later decks and do not publish on their own. I added no new W-556 exemption, so the 3 new builds wait for the gate, the multi-card reviews (W-604, W-601, W-602) and the deck kit. The copyright counting rule binds from now, and the "does it read as a summary" test now includes the idea titles and is run by someone other than the builder. I added questions Q7 to Q9 for the founder's legal read (F2).
4. W-651 is framed for the evaluation steward with a product requirement: every deck-level sentence is a claim held by the same publish gate as lesson claims. I prefer putting deck claims in idea 1's claims array, which needs no amendment, over a manifest, which needs an amendment to tools/company.mjs. The steward rules. - **Every verdict uses the same six words**, shared with Big Ideas.
- **Each idea still stands on its own:** someone who only does idea 2 gets a complete lesson. The book shows as one tile in the feed.

**The pilot is a *Thinking, Fast and Slow* deck:** the anchoring lesson already built, plus 3 new ideas. The other drafts become idea 1 of later decks and don't publish on their own. The 3 new ideas wait for three things: the multi-card reviews, the deck kit, and the wave gate.

**Copyright:** the counting rule applies from now. A different person from the builder checks that a deck's "the book argues" lines and idea titles together don't read like a synopsis of the book. The head of product added three questions (Q7–Q9) for the legal read.

**Your four answers unblock everything:**
1. **Is this what you meant by "more per book"?** A 3–4 idea deck with an opening bet and a closing verdict card, 4 at most.
2. **What does the 120 target count?** The head of product recommends idea-lessons, not books. At about 4 ideas per deck, 120 idea-lessons is about 30 books. The 60 committed slots cover about 12 decks.
3. **The legal read:** commission it, with the extra questions included.
4. **A book source:** name someone who can fill in chapter sheets from copies in hand. Without it, no Books lesson can publish.

body:
We have 12 categories today: 9 subjects, plus Life Hacks, Book Summaries and Big Ideas, which are still incubating. There are three kinds of expansion open.

**1. Verticals: a goal that cuts across categories.** The verticals plan (`plan-to-2000.md`) already weighed these:

| Vertical | Plan's call | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **Exam prep** (intro physics and intro statistics, e.g. AP Physics 1 and AP Statistics) | **Add, as a pilot** | Clear job ("pass the course"). A syllabus defines the demand, which no other option gives us. About half the lessons already exist. |
| Workplace skills | Defer | Overlaps Life Hacks, Books and AI-society. It would be a path over existing lessons, not new content. |
| Parents and kids | Decline for now | Child health hits the refuse list, and there's no child-safety reviewer. |

**2. New subject categories.** These haven't been assessed yet. Some that suit predict-then-see:
- **Astronomy and space:** orbits, seasons, scale, light travel time. Very visual, and checkable by derivation.
- **Psychology and the mind:** biases, perception, memory. This overlaps Big Ideas and Books, so it would need a boundary.
- **Music and sound:** intervals, harmonics, rhythm. Interactive by nature.
- **Language and linguistics:** sound change, word frequency (Zipf), ambiguity.
- **Engineering and how things work:** bridges, gears, circuits, everyday machines.
- **Health and the body:** high demand but high risk, because of medical claims and the safety refuse list.
- **History through data:** populations, trade, epidemics. Strong when built on data, weak as narrative.

**3. A second course, like Networks, Crowds and Markets.** The Courses org can adopt another well-known book or course and map every chapter. Candidates: *Thinking in Systems*, an intro statistics text, or game theory.

**My recommendation:**
1. Approve the **exam-prep pilot**. It's the only option with demand we don't have to guess.
2. Have the **domain scout** assess 2–3 new subjects. My pick is **astronomy** first: high visual payoff, mostly checkable by derivation, little overlap.
3. Hold everything else until real learner data arrives.

Each new category costs review capacity, which is the current bottleneck, so I'd add at most one at a time.

Want me to send the domain scout on astronomy, plus your top two from the list?

5. **Sources:** what I opened came from PyPI, GitHub raw files and a public git clone: the PDG 2026 database, Čertík's Theoretical Physics, ht, CoolProp, chemicals, iapws, astropy, pyproj, GeoNames, tzdata, and ERA-Interim winds from xarray-data. The phone-fit check passed on the 4 lessons whose stage or reveal changed: each fits, with nothing cropped or hidden. `npm run check` passes and `tsc --noEmit` is clean.

- **W-674, heat-the-ammonia-maker c2/c3:** I switched to the full-data values instead of adding a caption, because that needs no extra text. `kAt()` now works K out from the NASA TM-4513 coefficients, which are copied into Demo.tsx. The stage and reveal show K of 5.6 × 10⁵, 0.39 and 4.9 × 10⁻⁵, and NH₃ shares of 94%, 15% and 0.23%. "A factor of billions" still holds (1.1 × 10¹⁰). I left c5 and c6 alone because they were outside this dispatch.
- **W-675, limestone-crossover c5:** I dropped the unsourced "measured about 890 °C" sentence from the claim; learners never saw it. The recall's why now ends "near 850 °C (an estimate from 25 °C data)".
- **W-676, significant-but-false c5 and ten-thousand-replies-still-wrong c5:** both are marked `withdrawn` rather than reset to unverified, as the fact-check offered. Neither was ever shown to learners, so they don't change.
- **W-686, checking-is-not-finding c4:** the reveal and the claim now say "yet nobody knows a method that finds one quickly in every case". c4 still needs a source the fact-checker can open for subset-sum being NP-complete.
- **W-707, duck-rides-the-wave c4:**
  - The wave-train front now moves at half the crest speed (3.12 m/s), with crests moving at full speed inside it. The buoy starts to bob at 32 s.
  - A dashed marker labelled "front 3.1 m/s" shows the front.
  - "1 wave" and "10 waves" now show a steady train filling the sea, which was the fact-checker's optional fix.
  - The label, Seen row, reveal and c4 now say 32 s. The reveal adds "not 16: a wave's energy travels at half its crest speed".

W-732 is done. All 8 changed claims are now verified. The two withdrawn c5s never appear in the lessons themselves, but learners can still see them in the "Why trust this?" sheet (details below), so I could not confirm "never shown". `npm run check` passed. Nothing was built or committed, and I did not touch board.json or progress.md.

**Method:** I read Demo.tsx (and model.ts / solar.ts) v2 first, then re-ran every number in node or python from my own copies of the lesson logic. I did not use the dev server. The only sources I opened were on GitHub and PyPI, and each note names the file it rests on.

**One line per claim:**
- **heat-the-ammonia-maker c2: verified.**
  - The coefficients in Demo.tsx match Cantera `data/nasa_gas.yaml` (NASA TM-4513) digit for digit.
  - K comes out at 5.604e5, 0.391 and 4.91e-5. The ratio is 1.1e10, so "a factor of billions" holds.
- **heat-the-ammonia-maker c3: verified.** A second solver, set up differently, gives 93.8%, 14.8% and 0.227%, which display as 94%, 15% and 0.23%.
- **limestone-crossover c5 and its recall: verified.**
  - The switch is at 845.46 °C, shown as 845, and "about 850" is the nearest option.
  - The recall's "estimate from 25 °C data" is honest: my own run with the full NASA data gives 893 °C.
  - The withdrawn 890 °C sentence is gone everywhere.
- **checking-is-not-finding c4: verified, on an opened source.**
  - The source is Barak, *Introduction to Theoretical Computer Science* (git clone of github.com/boazbk/tcs, 68d6dde).
  - It has the definition of NP, a "Hardness of subset sum" theorem (3SAT ≤p SSUM), and calls P vs NP "the great open question".
  - Optional for the builder: put this citation in the source field in place of the unopened CLRS / Karp.
- **duck-rides-the-wave c4: verified, on derivation plus my own wave-packet simulation.**
  - Group speed is c/2 = 3.12 m/s, so the buoy is reached at 32.02 s (shown 32), against 16 at crest speed. My packet moves 125 m in 40 s.
  - At the buoy, the wave's height ramps up from 30 s and is at half of full height at 32 s.
- **The leftover approximation in the buoy preset:** for the first 2 simulated seconds (about 25 ms of the 400 ms replay) the duck rides up to 4 px above the drawn water. No number the learner sees comes from it, so it does not block.
- **darkest-evening-of-the-year c3: verified.** The 8.32 min noon drift splits into 5.92 min from tilt (71%) and 2.22 min from orbit shape (27%). astropy 8.0.1 puts perihelion at 2027-01-03 03 UTC.
- **which-sea-gets-the-rain c5 and its recall: verified.**
  - I am not the checker who recorded c5.
  - The ridge is the divide (c3), and 280 of the 300 km lies east of it. The west strip would need 14 times the rain per km to flip the answer, and "probably" covers that.
- **Withdrawn c5s (significant-but-false, ten-thousand-replies-still-wrong): not confirmed as never shown.**
  - The lessons are clean: the citations are not in Demo.tsx, the title, the hook or the recall.
  - But the learner-facing "Why trust this?" sheet (`src/components/DemoCard.tsx` lines 103-113) lists every claim with no status filter. A learner who opens it sees the claim text "(Not shown to the learner.) Optional context: Ioannidis (2005)…", or the Literary Digest equivalent, under a "withdrawn" label.
  - The claim counter (`src/lib/feed-index.ts` line 16) also counts withdrawn claims in the total, so these lessons show 4/5 and can never reach 5/5.
  - This affects all 36 lessons that hold a withdrawn claim. I left both c5s withdrawn and did not block on this.

**Files written:**
- meta.json (status, checkedBy, checkedOn, note) in:

It also refuses on a founder decision record with no route or objections.

**Rules that wait for you:**

**Marketing:** Celeste is VP of Marketing and reports to you, on HQ floor 7. She'll have no staff until you approve a public channel, and she has seven refuse rules: no posting, no outcome claims, no fake testimonials, and so on. Approve this as W-757.

I ran the Vertical Review and wrote the record. Its central conclusion is that the founder's 100 History lessons can't be reached unless the founder decides two items: W-764 (the review route for sensitive topics) and W-583 (a fact-check session with web access). Under today's rules only 39 of History's 114 concepts can be built.

I dispatched no category managers, as you asked, and worked from their written records. `npm run check` passes (945 lessons, 2 Life Hacks warnings that aren't mine). The commit is b200339, pushed to `ccr-4c6c7654-ew9ko1`. `git pull --rebase` was refused because other sessions have unstaged files in the tree. The push still fast-forwarded, so the remote had nothing newer.

**Files written**
- `/home/user/system-3-company/company/rituals/records/2026-10-14-vertical-review.md` (the record)
- `/home/user/system-3-company/company/ops/founder-inbox.json`: new item F-16

- `/home/user/system-3-company/company/product/verticals/2026-10-14-history-and-next-categories.md`: §1 marked superseded in part (target and wave slot only; the entry rules, boundaries and kill rule still apply)
- `/home/user/system-3-company/company/ops/events.jsonl`: a `ritual` event and one kudos to cm-history

**The 5 most important conclusions**
1. **History at 100 depends on W-764 and W-583, not on more briefs.** 54 concepts are sensitive and 30 have no openable data. Maps-borders has only 6 buildable concepts, so without W-764 History launches as population and price charts. I recommend yes on W-764. The one caveat: until AMD-006 is ratified, `company publish` doesn't read the sensitive hold, so the publish loop is the only guard.
2. **The plan to 2,000 absorbs History's 100 without displacing anything committed (F-16, option a, high confidence on the arithmetic).**
   - The total stays 2,000, and the extra 40 come from the uncommitted Waves N-Q pool (648 slots down to about 608).
   - History runs in two tranches:
     - **Tranche 1:** about 25 standard briefs, roughly 2.5–3M tokens.
     - **Tranche 2:** about 75 lessons, released only when W-764 lands, the Domain Launch Review five pass, and held claims are at or under 25%.
   - The 40 Wave K-M slots History no longer uses stay empty until the drain wave finishes, because History's reviews use the same reviewers.
   - I recommend History lessons count in the W-556 queue measure.
3. **Books is held at the reference deck until F1 (the book source).** Its 6 drafts have 0 of 38 claims verified, and nothing Books builds can publish without F1. My positions:
   - **F1:** the founder or a named person fills the pilot's chapter sheet with a copy in hand, about half an hour. Then one connected fact-check session per wave.
   - **F2:** start the legal read now; it costs no calendar time because F1 blocks publishing first.
   - **F4:** agree with head-of-product: count the target as 120 idea-lessons, and decide the unfunded ~30 slots at Wave N cycle planning.
4. **Life Hacks is the main reason the W-556 gate is shut for every other category.** All 200 lessons count in the queue: 14 have a learner review and 0 are published. The queue outside Life Hacks is 137, already under the 160 limit. The gate rule (Amendment 1) already allows a written triage record to park lessons that get no review work. I asked cm-lifehacks to write one, and head-of-product confirms the count; I did not move the gate. Big Ideas stays a pilot (6 drafts, 0 verified); its 170 target is a ceiling against a 58-concept map.
5. **Exam prep can start now.** The syllabus blocker I recorded earlier is gone. AP documents and openstax.org are unreachable from this host. However, the OpenStax textbook tables of contents are reachable on raw.githubusercontent.com (Introductory Statistics 2e and College Physics for AP Courses 2e). The mapping is zero builds and reversible, so I ask head-of-product to authorise it now. W-582 then shrinks to the founder deciding the 36 Wave K build slots. It still ranks first among everything on the table. The AP alignment is unconfirmed, and nothing in this review is market evidence: there is no deploy and no learner data.

**Board asks (for the chief of staff to add)**
1. Authorise the exam-prep mapping now, inside the roadmap (0 builds; W-543, W-544); W-582 then covers only the 36 build slots. Owner: head-of-product.
2. W-543 note: map intro physics against the OpenStax College Physics for AP Courses 2e table of contents on raw GitHub; label gaps "AP alignment unconfirmed". Owner: cm-physics.
3. W-544 note: the same for the Introductory Statistics 2e table of contents. Owner: cm-probability.
4. Licence note on using the OpenStax tables of contents (CC BY-NC-SA) as a mapping reference only. Owner: research-lead.
5. Rule whether History lessons count in the W-556 queue measure (I recommend yes). Owner: head-of-product.
6. W-794: keep the strand-balance hold on History briefs 25–30 until the launch-review five form across all three strands; release when that review passes or W-764 lands. Owner: head-of-product.
7. Form History's launch-review five across all three strands, with at least one maps-borders lesson (brief 6 or 10). Owner: cm-history.
8. Write a Life Hacks triage record parking every lesson outside the active v2 batches and launch-review candidates. Owner: cm-lifehacks.
9. Record the Wave J slug list in `waves.json` (W-585); without it the gate's "Wave J ≥ 60% published" condition can't be checked. Owner: chief-of-staff.
10. Add my recommendations to the founder items W-764, W-615 and W-582. Owner: chief-of-staff.
11. Close W-688 as moot, and add a note to W-689 that the boundaries still bind. Owner: chief-of-staff.
12. A UI concept for History's shared "dated series on presets" pattern, once two such lessons pass design review. Owner: design-lead.
13. History two-step paths from each lesson's prerequisite lesson in another category, plus a zero-lesson astronomy-interest path. Owner: personalization-lead.

**Next move:** I write the History Project Review proposal with the two-tranche budget (W-723 and W-802, both mine, due 2026-10-16). The founder answers F-16, W-764, W-615 and W-582. Head-of-product takes asks 1, 5 and 6.

I built and committed five History lessons, all claimed through the shared lock. Every one passes phone fit and QA locally.

| Slug | Fit (390x844) | QA (phone + desktop) |
|---|---|---|
| rome-placed-too-far-east | fit, crop 0, nothing named hidden, phoneFit true, 79 words | pass |

| doubling-stopped-speeding-up | fit, crop 0, nothing named hidden, phoneFit true, 84 words | pass |
| italy-poorer-in-1800 | fit, crop 0, nothing named hidden, phoneFit true, 76 words | pass |

- **Branch:** history-build-1, in /home/user/s3c-hist-1. Three commits (d7f34ce, e332e1c, 4d35214), not pushed, no [deploy].
- **Measurements:** word counts include the verdict line. Labels are 11px on a 340-unit-wide chart drawn about 330px wide, so about 10.6px on screen. `npm run check` and the typecheck pass. I looked at every phone screenshot.
- **Data:** the numbers in each lesson are copied straight from the pinned files, and a node script confirmed each copy matches its file exactly. Everything else on screen is computed in the lesson using the check scripts' formulas; I typed no numbers by hand.
- **Status:** all lessons are draft, domain history, owner cm-history, every claim unverified. Each has a Pre-flight v1 in `company/reviews/<slug>/build.md`.
- **Cleanup:** the dev server is stopped, `.next-h1` and the `AGENTS.md` it generated are deleted, `tsconfig.json` is reverted, and the worktree is clean. Stopping the `npx` process alone left the real `next dev` child running, so I stopped that one by its own PID too.
- **Claims:** all five briefs stay claimed by me, because they are built. I released nothing, and I did not touch board.json or progress.md.

**Deviations from the briefs, for cm-history to accept or reverse** (each is recorded in that lesson's build.md):
1. **wages-bought-more-wheat:** the reveal unlocks after "wages divided by price" and "best year", not the first alone, because the reveal names 1785. I also renamed the buttons "Mark the best year" and "Mark the worst year". At the reveal, the button row is tucked behind a "Show controls" toggle to save space, and the fit tool was counting the hidden "Best year" button as something the reveal points at.
2. **rome-placed-too-far-east:** names are not shown on tap, which would add 12 tap targets to QA. Only the closest estimate is named.
3. **children-dying-before-five** and **doubling-stopped-speeding-up:** a few presets the brief listed as milestones don't gate the reveal; the gate is exactly the one each brief states.

**For the fact-checker:** in doubling-stopped-speeding-up, the "0.87% in 2023" growth figure comes from the check script's formula, which uses the file's 2024 value. Gapminder may mark that value as a projection. It is disclosed in claim c3, and no year after 2023 is drawn. Each lesson has at most one held source sentence, with its fallback in its claim.

**Something you should know:** while my dev server was running, the log showed requests for `income-flat-then-sixteenfold` on my port 3621. That lesson doesn't exist in my worktree, so another builder may be pointing their tools at my port.

**What I believe:** confident that the numbers match the pinned data and the check scripts, and that each lesson passes the measured gates. Less sure whether the deviations above will be accepted.

**Board items** (I didn't add them; whoever runs the board should):
- fact-checker: verify claims for the five lessons, starting with the held sentences and the 2024-value disclosure.
- cm-history: accept or reverse the deviations in the build.md files.
- An evaluator: walkthrough and learner review of all five.
- After that, status draft → review is mine to set once review passes.

body:
I reviewed all 32 lessons as a borrowed adult-beginner mind, using each lesson's own meta.json learner boundary. Result: 27 pass, 4 revise, 1 block. These reviews find problems; they are not evidence that anyone learned.

For each lesson I read transcript.md and sheet.png first, wrote my findings, and only then read build.md (in a separate "After reading build.md" section). All 32 walkthroughs already existed, so I recorded none. I added each review path to `evidence.simulatedLearner` in its meta.json. The JSON was rewritten without other changes; I checked beforehand that a no-change round-trip matched every file exactly. `npm run check` passes. I made three commits, `b4a538b` (13 lessons), `5708e1d` (10) and `da1a23c` (9), each pushed to origin/ccr-4c6c7654-ew9ko1. Each commit names only my files.

One slip: I briefly added a board item (W-818) for the block, then saw you had said not to edit board.json. I reverted it with `git checkout -- company/ops/board.json` before any commit, and board.json was not otherwise modified. That means the block below is not on the board yet.

**Block (1)**
- the-doctor-picks-the-patients: block. "Coin again" gives exactly the same 11.8 vs 12.2 split as "Coin chooses" (seeds 58 and 59, confirmed in build.md). The dots are sorted inside each box, so the two frames look the same even when cropped side by side. To a learner the control looks dead, and it undercuts the reveal's claim about chance. Fix: make each coin press visibly change the gap, draw the dots unsorted, and keep a tally of coin gaps.

**Revise (4)**
- quarters-add-to-a-third: revise. After "Reset to level 1" the reveal stage shows level 1, so "the leftover corner shrank toward nothing" is not on screen. Put level 6 back on the stage at the reveal, show the leftover at level 6, and say why hatched and dotted pieces are there.
- total-signups-hide-the-slide: revise. The reveal says a running total "can't tell you which way you are going", but the stage shows a bending-down "worse" curve and a bending-up "better" curve. The locked stage already shows the bending-down curve, so a careful learner can answer "It fell" and be marked wrong. Narrow the reveal sentence, use a locked frame without the bend, and use neutral preset names.
- which-sea-gets-the-rain: revise. The locked stage shows no relief, so the right answer (east) depends on terrain the learner was never shown, and "west" is the rational pick. Show the relief before the prediction, or add a "can't tell from distance" option. The builder hid it on purpose under the "no answer before the commit" rule, so this is a design call.
- why-the-poles-get-less-sun: revise. The picture is equinox noon, where the pole's beam "grazes the ground" (close to nothing), but the answer is a yearly 41% that depends on Earth's tilt and polar summer, which the card never mentions. Read from the picture, the "About 10%" option looks right. Add one line about the polar summer, or ask the equinox-noon question instead.

**Pass (27), with the main fix for each**
- opposite-flows-swap-more: the explore prompt sends the learner away from the same-way picture; say "look at same-way first" and label "level arriving".
- raters-reward-agreement: restore the 70% vote grids at the reveal, and make "user right: both alike" visual.
- same-dose-levels-off: add a "cleared this interval" readout so in-equals-out is seen.
- same-grey-in-shadow: reword "judged B lighter than the light it sends".
- savings-outlast-the-division: restore the $40k at 5% readout at the reveal, and add a year-1 earned vs taken line.
- screening-survival-clock: show the legend on the locked stage; label the toggle as an action.
- secret-in-the-counts: after deletion, say the model falls back to one word; restore the leaked output at the reveal.
- significant-but-false: make missed real effects visibly different at phone size.
- sixteen-of-twenty-got-better: show the no-pill group first, then step the days; optionally add an "if the pill worked" case.
- slowest-station-sets-pace: restore the Double S1 pile at the reveal; name The Goal as Goldratt's novel.
- small-n-favours-the-slow-curve: the 43/44 presets give away the crossover; consider a slider.
- snap-the-magnet: label the arrows as tiny magnets, and add the compass rule.
- steady-catch-from-a-lake: "In your run, 120" over-claims on a drag path; reword or prompt 120. Show growth at the current level.
- sudden-skill-or-strict-score: keep one filled/dashed encoding across presets.
- ten-thousand-replies-still-wrong: label the whisker as the margin.
- ten-times-taller-giant: name the cube/square rule; the caption is stale after "thicker legs"; label the toggle as an action.
- the-equals-sign-balances: the unknown beam state looks level; the prediction may be too easy for adults.
- tug-of-war-scale: show "?" on the locked dial; reword "can only be stretched if".
- twenty-cultures-twenty-plates: give both rows the same summary (average, empty, max); explain the jackpot doubling.
- two-four-six-rule: the free-build path can teach "disconfirming tests just agree"; add a nudge. The Wason credit build.md mentions was not visible on this path.
- two-pages-swallow-the-rank: make per-page shares readable; define "Scaled PageRank".
- two-routes-to-co2: say diamond is a form of carbon; use "total" instead of Σ.
- wheel-number-pulls-guess: write the model line plainly, and separate the simulated crowd from the 1974 study in the reveal.
- where-the-axis-starts: no fix needed.
- which-step-to-speed: the gate-width picture is unreadable; show the current state of the controls.
- which-way-the-water-goes: wind and net-flow labels collide in two frames.
- winning-bid-overpays: reorder the 2-bidder sentence; hide the always-disabled "Step" button.

**How sure I am:** confident about the block, which build.md confirms and a cropped-frame comparison backs up. Moderately confident about the four revises: each is a mismatch between what the stage shows and what the question or reveal says, not a false fact. The pass findings are hypotheses. I saw the screenshots mostly at contact-sheet size, so legibility findings (gate widths, shadow strength, small bars) need a human look at full size. A pattern worth knowing: several lessons rely on a "Seen" trace after Reset, so the reveal's numbers survive but its picture does not.

**Next moves (for you to route, since I did not edit the board):**
- demo-builder: the doctor-picks-the-patients block.
- cm-math / demo-builder: quarters-add-to-a-third.
- cm-books / demo-builder, plus fact-checker on the scope of the reveal sentence: total-signups-hide-the-slide.
- cm-geography with learning-designer: which-sea-gets-the-rain (prediction design versus the no-answer rule).
- cm-geography / demo-builder, plus fact-checker: why-the-poles-get-less-sun.
- qa-tester or fact-checker: check whether the two-four-six-rule Wason credit renders.

Files are in /home/user/system-3-company: 32 reviews at `company/reviews/<slug>/2026-10-14-learner-adult-beginner-r10.md`, plus the 32 updated `src/demos/<domain>/<slug>/meta.json`. The block is in `company/reviews/the-doctor-picks-the-patients/2026-10-14-learner-adult-beginner-r10.md`.

body:
I ran the overdue design review and wrote it to `/home/user/system-3-company/company/rituals/records/2026-10-14-design-review.md`. It is committed as 6814e0d and pushed to `ccr-4c6c7654-ew9ko1`. `npm run check` passes. I did not touch `board.json` or `progress.md`, and I made no new walkthroughs or build directories.

**What I looked at:** existing walkthrough sheets for 15 lessons, read before any code or notes. I read no builder notes (`build.md`). I opened CSS and grepped code only afterwards, to confirm causes.
- **CardSequence reference:** `euclid-three-steps`.
- **Board items:** W-573 `cluster-stops-the-cascade`, W-574 `enemy-of-my-enemy`, W-575 `metal-feels-colder`, and the four W-567/W-642 lessons.
- **Sample:** 7 drafts, one each from books, big-ideas, chemistry, ai, economics, geography and physics.

**Limits you should know about:**
- The walkthroughs for W-573/574/575 and the W-567 lessons were recorded before the r9 fixes. So §2 covers the versions learners flagged, written as checks for the r10 re-review (W-640), not as new revise orders.
- I wrote the Book deck spec, so I gave it no verdict.
- For CardSequence my section is input to the interaction designer (W-601), not an approval.
- Both formats stay 🔴 in `formats.md`.

**Top findings**
1. **Kit stage layout (affects every lesson).** In `globals.css`, `.stage` is a scroll box with its content centred vertically (`overflow: auto; justify-content: safe center`).
   - In predict, the last control row is cut off inside a nested scroll with no cue: `each-element-pops-once`, `same-grey-in-shadow`, `cluster-stops-the-cascade` v4.
   - `wheel-needs-four-colours` scrolls its own caption off screen during explore.
   - The picture drops 40–65 px when the prediction locks in and shifts again between steps.
   - Direction: anchor stage content at the top. The platform engineer must measure the effect on reveal fit before anything changes.
2. **The reveal opens on emptied evidence.** On the QA path the last control is Reset or a hide toggle, so the reveal shows an empty stage while quoting it. This happens in 4 of 15 lessons: `secret-in-the-counts`, `two-locks-wait-forever`, `which-sea-gets-the-rain`, `wheel-number-pulls-guess` (hidden-wheel picture, slider still on 65, no "no wheel" label).
3. **CardSequence holds its main promise.** The reveal shows the trail traces plus card 3, it is 62 words, and by eye it fits. The one design defect: the trail floats mid-stage and drops about 65 px from predict to explore. For W-601 I recommend not accepting the 71 px four-step trail: four-card lessons should use one-word titles and traces of 8 characters or fewer, or use three cards.
4. **Book deck spec is stale.** `book-format.md`, its SVG and the `formats.md` row still say 5–6 ideas and the old verdict words. The W-647 ruling set 4 ideas maximum and the shared six verdict words. This must be fixed before W-648 drafts the EDD. Separately, `wheel-number-pulls-guess` (idea 1) may go about 14 px over with the 44 px book bar; the book probe has to measure it.
5. **Domain pastel used as text.** `tug-of-war-scale` (`.labT`, 10.5 px) and `metal-feels-colder` (`.readNow`) set their readouts in the domain colour, which `system.md` forbids as text.
6. **Pictures that work against their own reveal.**
   - `hydrogen-per-litre` uses an unlabelled log axis, so the 2,900× gap looks like about 4×.
   - `winning-bid-overpays` separates red and green dots by colour only, and its "Step: one auction" button is never enabled on the QA path.

**Sample result:** none of the 7 has a blocking layout defect. 6 have fixable design findings, and 4 of those trace to findings 1 and 2. All 7 reveals are 62–78 words and fit at 390×844 by eye. How sure I am: high on what the artifacts show; medium on pixel numbers, which are estimates from the sheets.

**Board asks** (also listed in the record)
1. Measure top-anchored stage content against today's centring with `tools/reveal-fit.mjs` on a 30-lesson sample, including the predict stages that cut their last row — platform-engineer
2. CardSequence: anchor the trail at the top of the stage, then re-run the sequence probe — design-engineer
3. W-601 input: four-card title and trace rule; do not accept the 71 px trail — interaction-designer
4. Bring `book-format.md`, its SVG and the `formats.md` row in line with the W-647 ruling, before W-648 — design-lead
5. Chair the Book deck reference design review; the book probe measures `wheel-number-pulls-guess` with the bar — interaction-designer
6. Reveal opens on emptied evidence (`secret-in-the-counts`, `two-locks-wait-forever`, `which-sea-gets-the-rain`, `wheel-number-pulls-guess`): reorder the controls or restore the quoted picture — demo-builder
7. Pattern check: Reset or hide toggles never come last in DOM order unless the reveal restores the picture — pattern-librarian
8. Domain pastel as text in `tug-of-war-scale` and `metal-feels-colder` — demo-builder
9. `hydrogen-per-litre` log-axis label or a ×2,900 marker (record it as a claim); `winning-bid-overpays` shape encoding and the dead Step button — demo-builder
10. `winning-bid-overpays` shows AVG GUESS $99.2 at 2, 10 and 20 bidders; confirm it is correct — fact-checker
11. Run the r10 design checks in §2 for W-640 and W-642 — learner-evaluator
12. `same-grey-in-shadow`: keep the checkerboard full size at the reveal instead of shrinking it to about 130 px — demo-builder

**Next move:** the chief of staff files these asks. My own first item is ask 4, before W-648. I flip the multi-card row (W-630) only after W-601 and W-602 close.
